about.thirdPartyText: The system image is a collection. The Linux kernel, the Debian packages and the libraries in use keep their own licenses; the sources of the GPL parts are linked with every release.
about.title: About TitanOS
access.certChain: Certificate, followed by the intermediate certificates
access.certExpiring: This certificate is only valid for {days} more days. Put a new one in place in time.
access.certFormHint: Paste certificate and key in PEM format or choose the files.
access.certKeyNote: The key is stored on the stick and never handed out again by the web interface.
access.certNone: In development mode the web interface runs without encryption.
access.certOwn: Use a certificate of your own
access.certRemove: Remove and use the one from TitanOS again
access.certRemoveText: Your certificate and its key are deleted from the NAS. The web UI then uses the self-signed certificate of TitanOS again; browsers will warn when you open it until you accept the exception.
access.certSaved: The certificate is in place and in use from now on. Reload the page so that your browser uses it.
access.certSelf: TitanOS made this certificate itself. The connection is encrypted, but the browser cannot check who is at the other end and warns for that reason. With a certificate of your own – say from the certificate authority of your home network or for a domain of yours – the warning goes away.
access.letsEncryptActive: A certificate from Let's Encrypt holds for {names} until {date}.
access.sshFingerprint: Fingerprint of the NAS (compare at the first login)
access.sshNetworksAll: From all networks at the moment.
access.sshNetworksConfirmText: The address you are connected from right now ({address}) is in none of the networks. From this device you can no longer log in to the NAS over SSH afterwards. The web interface stays reachable.
access.sshNetworksError: sshd refused the list; the previous one stays in use. {detail}
access.sshNetworksNoHome: The NAS is not in any network right now that would do as home network.
access.sshNetworksRecovery: Locked out? The web interface is not affected by the list. Without the web interface the local console (Ctrl+Alt+F2, “titand -network-recovery”, choice 3) lifts the restriction.
access.sshNetworksShort: The networks SSH logins may come from.
access.sshNetworksText: One network per line in CIDR notation (IPv4 or IPv6), such as 192.168.1.0/24; a single address counts as /32 or /128. sshd itself turns away logins from other addresses – the firewall stays as it is. Empty means: from all networks. Open sessions stay.
access.sshNoKeys: No owner or administrator has stored a key yet.
access.sshNotStarted: SSH is switched on, but the service is still not running after a minute. Check the log under Tools.
access.sshNotStopped: SSH is switched off, but the service is still running after a minute. Check the log under Tools.
access.sshNote: Whoever has a key gets in without a password and without a second factor and has full rights with sudo. The system image is fresh at every start: only what lies under /config and /mnt stays.
access.sshShort: Command line from another computer – owners and administrators only, with a key only.
access.sshText: For working on the command line from another computer. Only owners and administrators can log in, under their own name and with a key they stored under “My account” – never with a password and never as root. For commands with full rights there is sudo.
access.title: Access
account.beginText: Enter your password to confirm. TitanOS then shows the QR code for your authenticator app.
account.devicesNote: Logins end after 7 days without use, after 30 days at the latest, and with every restart of the NAS.
account.disableText: After that the password alone is enough again. Enter your password and a code to confirm.
account.endOthersText: {count} other logins of your account end, including open consoles there. This device stays logged in.
account.enterCode: Code from the app, as a check
account.passwordText: The password is for the web UI and for your SMB shares.
account.picture.hint: The picture of your account on the login page: a photo of your own or one of the built-in pictures.
account.picture.title: Picture
account.recoveryCopied: The codes are on the clipboard.
account.recoveryCopyFailed: Copying was not possible. The codes are selected – copy them by hand (Ctrl/⌘+C) or download them as a file.
account.recoveryText: Each of these codes gets you in once without your phone. They are only shown now: keep them in a safe place, not on the NAS.
account.renewText: Your current recovery codes stop working. Enter your password and a code to confirm.
account.scan: Scan the code with an authenticator app (for example Aegis, 2FAS or your password manager) or enter the secret by hand.
account.title: My account
account.twoFactorOff: Off. The password is enough to log in.
account.twoFactorOn: On. Logging in and confirming sensitive actions, such as opening VM consoles, also ask for a code from your authenticator app.
activity.do.dockerVolumeDelete: Docker volume deleted with its data
activity.do.fileContent: File saved from a browser program
activity.do.healthReport: Report about the NAS set up
activity.do.intelGuc: Changed the GuC/HuC setting of Intel graphics
activity.do.letsencryptFailed: Certificate from Let's Encrypt not obtained
activity.do.mcpSettings: MCP server switched on or off
activity.do.pushAdd: Notifications turned on for a device
activity.do.shareDataDeleteFailed: Deleting the data of a share failed
activity.do.sshLoginBlocked: SSH login turned away (network not allowed)
activity.do.vmSchedulePoweroff: VM switched off on schedule (waiting time exceeded)
activity.do.webappMigrate: Docker apps replaced by browser programs
activity.dropped: {count} entries were lost because no volume was available for a long time.
activity.hint: Who changed what and when: logins, settings, file actions, consoles and starts of apps and VMs. Request contents such as passwords, keys or file contents are never stored. The log lives on a data volume, not on the stick.
activity.memoryOnly: No data volume available. Only the latest entries from memory are shown; they are stored as soon as a volume is mounted.
activity.noVolume: No suitable volume is mounted. The latest entries stay in memory until a restart and are stored as soon as a volume is there.
activity.off: The activity log is off. No new entries are recorded.
agent.accountsHint: Owners may always use the agent. Choose further accounts here; each has its own chats and sees only its own shares.
agent.alwaysDenied: Always denied, cannot be switched on: passwords, tokens, 2FA, consoles and the settings of the agent and MCP.
agent.archive.title: Archive
agent.area.historyHint: Read only: the activity log, the history of CPU, memory, disks and network, and the forecast of when the volumes are full.
agent.area.nvrHint: Read only, without pictures: which camera saw what and when. Asks before every read from the factory, even with “Everything without asking”; reads without asking only when set so here expressly.
agent.area.photosHint: Read only: the agent searches each account's own photos and changes nothing there.
agent.areaHint.features: Switch single functions on and off
agent.areaHint.instruction: What the agent should always keep in mind
agent.areaHint.phone: As an app on the home screen, QR code
agent.areaHint.rights: What the agent may do without asking
agent.ask.title: Approval needed: {what}
agent.ask.update.rollback: Roll back to the previous system
agent.ask.whyOutside: Asks because outside content was read in this chat: no content it read can make the agent send data to the internet.
agent.ask.whyPim: Asks because mail, events or contacts were read in this chat: no content it read can make the agent send data to the internet.
agent.assist.addr.ddns: Dynamic DNS with a valid certificate
agent.assist.addr.domain: Own domain with a valid certificate (Let’s Encrypt)
agent.assist.addr.lan: Home network, without a certificate (not encrypted)
agent.assist.addr.tailscale: Tailscale, valid certificate – Home Assistant must be in the tailnet
agent.assist.addressesDesc: Enter one of them in the Ollama integration of Home Assistant.
agent.assist.addressesHttps: https only works under a name with a valid certificate (Tailscale or Let’s Encrypt); Home Assistant refuses TitanOS’s own certificate. In the home network http works – questions and answers are not encrypted there.
agent.assist.areaDesc.calendar: Reads the calendar of the account ‘Assist as’
agent.assist.areaDesc.contacts: Reads the contacts of the account ‘Assist as’
agent.assist.areaDesc.docker: See, start, stop and update containers
agent.assist.areaDesc.files: Search, read, write and delete in the shares
agent.assist.areaDesc.home: Lights, switches, sensors – only what is released under “Devices for the agent”
agent.assist.areaDesc.memory: Read only: use what the profile remembered. Also change: remember new things, write notes
agent.assist.areaDesc.shares: SMB and NFS shares and their rights
agent.assist.areaDesc.updates: Install updates, restart or switch off the NAS
agent.assist.areaDesc.web: Search the web and read pages (DuckDuckGo)
agent.assist.consent.desc: Questions from Home Assistant run with the rights of your account. Assist reads your calendar and your contacts only where you switch it on here yourself – no administrator can do that for you, and “Read only” above is not enough on its own. Keep in mind: with your consent, anyone who asks in Home Assistant with the Assist key can ask about your events or contacts; all owners and administrators can ask about them themselves in the Home Assistant profile of the AI agent and see its chats with the answers. You can withdraw it here at any time; it applies at once.
agent.assist.consent.notActor: Assist currently asks as {actor}, not as your account. Your consent applies again only when Assist asks as your account; you can withdraw it here.
agent.assist.consent.notGiven: Not agreed – Assist sees none of it
agent.assist.consent.title: Your consent: calendar and contacts for Assist
agent.assist.intro: The agent becomes a conversation agent in Home Assistant (app, voice devices).
agent.assist.keyDesc: Enter it in the Ollama integration of Home Assistant as the “API key”. Without it TitanOS does not answer.
agent.assist.keyNewText: The old key stops working at once. Home Assistant reaches the agent again only after you enter the new one there.
agent.assist.keyNone: No key yet: until then TitanOS only lets the Home Assistant address set up here in. With a key it also works as a Docker app and over other addresses.
agent.assist.lastNone: Home Assistant has not asked since TitanOS started.
agent.assist.lastOkNoQuestion: {when} from {from} · answered in {seconds} s (only the account Assist asks as sees the question)
agent.assist.onDesc: Home Assistant may ask the agent questions
agent.assist.profileDesc: Its own memory, chats, instruction and reminders – apart from every account. Owners and administrators see and look after it.
agent.assist.reason.address: not the Home Assistant address set up here
agent.assist.reason.key: the key is missing or wrong
agent.assist.rightsDesc: Only for questions from Home Assistant. Never more than “Rights” allow; what asks there waits for your approval in TitanOS.
agent.assist.setup: How to set it up in Home Assistant
agent.assist.setupDesc: Settings › Devices & services › Add integration › Ollama: address and key from above, model “titanos-agent”. Then choose it as the conversation agent under Voice assistants.
agent.attachDefault: Have a look at the attached files.
agent.attachTooBig: Too large to upload (at most 20 MB): {names}. Choose larger files with “Choose from the NAS”, the agent then reads them directly.
agent.autonomy.askHint: Every change waits for your approval
agent.autonomy.directHint: Works the task through and asks only where the rights of the NAS require it
agent.autonomy.planHint: Shows the plan first and works through it after your yes
agent.autonomy.title: Way of working
agent.busy.files.6: Looking for the needle in the haystack …
agent.busy.home.5: Seeing where a light is on …
agent.busy.system.3: Taking the pulse of the disks …
agent.busy.web.8: Out on the web for a moment …
agent.busyWait: The agent is still working. Wait until it is done.
agent.card.ask.details: Show me the details of {name}: image, version, ports, folders, load and since when it has been running
agent.card.ask.errors: Search the log of {name} for errors and warnings of the last hours and explain what they mean
agent.card.ask.logs: Show me the last lines of the log of {name} and tell me whether anything stands out
agent.card.ask.why: Why is the container {name} not running? Look into the log and tell me what to do
agent.cloudHint: The model runs at a provider on the internet: what the agent reads leaves your NAS.
agent.cmd.find.name: find
agent.cmd.findNoChat: There is no chat to search in yet.
agent.cmd.model.name: model
agent.cmd.new.name: new
agent.cmd.plan: Plan a task or a reminder
agent.cmd.plan.name: plan
agent.cmd.planAsk: Please plan this as a task or a reminder: {text}
agent.cmd.project: Put the chat into a project
agent.cmd.project.name: project
agent.cmd.remember.name: remember
agent.cmd.status.name: status
agent.cmd.title: Commands
agent.codeHint: The agent may run short Python or sh programs, e.g. to calculate, convert or sort. They run in a throw-away container without network, with a read-only system, as your account, and only see your folder in KI-Agent as /work. It asks before every run unless you set “Run code” under areas to “Without asking”. Needs Docker.
agent.contextHint: Without a value of its own, Ollama's setting applies (OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH). Below 16k long tasks break off.
agent.contextModel: The model can take up to {tokens} tokens.
agent.contextSmall: Ollama only uses {tokens} of context. Tasks with several steps need at least 16k (Settings › AI agent or OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH).
agent.contextUnknown: If the model is not loaded, the agent loads it at the start of a task and then reads the exact value.
agent.contextVram: More context needs much more graphics memory; if it does not fit, Ollama moves work to the CPU and gets slow.
agent.cronHint: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday, e.g. “0 7 * * 1-5” = Mon–Fri at 7:00.
agent.data.calendarDesc: Events in Calendar, all calendars of this account
agent.data.calendarReadDesc: Questions like “What’s on tomorrow?” – events read count as outside content (invitations from others)
agent.data.calendarWriteDesc: With asking, the chat shows the event before it is saved. Deleting a whole series or changing its repetition always asks, and so does deleting after outside content was read.
agent.data.contactsDesc: The account’s contacts; not the suggestions from Mail
agent.data.contactsReadDesc: Contacts read count as outside content; birthdays in the calendar need this
agent.data.contactsWriteDesc: With asking, the chat shows the contact before it is saved. Deleting after outside content was read always asks.
agent.delegateHint: For a broad look (many logs, many folders) the agent starts a helper with an empty context that only reads and reports back.
agent.deleteAllSub: {count} chats · you can keep pinned ones
agent.deleteAllText: {count} chats are deleted, also those in projects, with their attachments. Projects, memory and skills stay. Running tasks stay.
agent.deleteText: "{title}" is deleted with all its messages.
agent.editHint: The answers after it are generated again.
agent.f.adminOnly: Owners and administrators can switch it on.
agent.f.changedKept: Changed elsewhere in the meantime – reloaded. Your change was about something else and is saved on the new state.
agent.f.changedLost: Changed elsewhere in the meantime – reloaded. The same function was changed there too, so your change is not saved. Check the new state and make it again if needed.
agent.f.docs.deadlinesSub: Finds notice, warranty and payment deadlines · suggest first
agent.f.docs.deadlinesSubRemind: Finds notice, warranty and payment deadlines · as reminders right away
agent.f.docs.filingHint: When unsure the agent always asks (Assign). Everything filed can be undone.
agent.f.docs.findHint: Notice, warranty, payment and due dates, with the source
agent.f.docs.inboxCounts: {ask} to assign · {waiting} wait for the picture model
agent.f.docs.inboxSub: Scanner over SMB or drop files in
agent.f.docs.leadHint: Days before the deadline, separated by commas (at most three)
agent.f.docs.mailHint: PDF and picture attachments go to the inbox folder, the mail text as a document of its own (for bills without attachment). A mail already read elsewhere is not fetched.
agent.f.docs.mailSub: IMAP; the agent only marks mails read, it never deletes or moves
agent.f.docs.memorySub: Reads chosen folders at night and answers questions with the source
agent.f.docs.nightly: Read at night from {at}, when the disks are awake anyway
agent.f.docs.paperLooking: The agent looks into the inbox folder.
agent.f.docs.paperOwn: Inbox folder and own mailbox for your account
agent.f.docs.paperSub: Inbox folder and mailbox · names and files by itself
agent.f.docs.paperSubAsk: Inbox folder and mailbox · suggests the filing every time
agent.f.docs.pending: {count} scans wait for the picture model
agent.f.docs.pickRead: Only shares your account may read.
agent.f.docs.pickWrite: Only shares your account may write to.
agent.f.docs.scansSub: With the agent's picture model in Ollama · waits while Ollama cannot be reached
agent.f.docs.unsure: Unsure: sender or type not recognised
agent.f.docs.unsureError: Could not be filed – please assign
agent.f.docs.waitingModel: Scan waits for the picture model
agent.f.family.buddy.address: Address of this NAS for the partner
agent.f.family.buddy.addressHint: Tailscale address or name, e.g. nas-eva.tail1234.ts.net. Partners reach this NAS on port 8752 (firewall service "Backup-Buddy").
agent.f.family.buddy.codeHint: Enter this code on the other TitanOS (valid for 10 minutes):
agent.f.family.buddy.endData: Also delete the backups of {name} on this NAS
agent.f.family.buddy.endText: The schedule to {name} ends and {name} can no longer store anything here. What this NAS backed up at {name} stays there until {name} deletes it.
agent.f.family.buddy.enterHint: Or enter the code of the other TitanOS here:
agent.f.family.buddy.footer: Backups are made with restic and a password only this NAS knows. Nothing is overwritten at the partner; deleted data stays in quarantine for {days} days.
agent.f.family.buddy.intro: Two TitanOS back each other up, encrypted with the sender's key: the partner cannot read anything. The partner reaches this NAS over Tailscale.
agent.f.family.buddy.jobError: Paired, but the backup job could not be saved: {error}
agent.f.family.buddy.mine: What I back up at the partner
agent.f.family.buddy.noJob: nothing chosen to back up yet
agent.f.family.buddy.probeNone: None yet; runs after the next backup
agent.f.family.buddy.problem.address: The address of this NAS is not set; without it no partner can pair.
agent.f.family.buddy.problem.tailscale: Tailscale is not connected; partners cannot reach this NAS right now.
agent.f.family.buddy.problem.volume: No volume for the partners' backups is mounted.
agent.f.family.buddy.protectHint: What partners delete here stays in quarantine for this many days and can be brought back, even if a partner was taken over.
agent.f.family.buddy.sub: Back each other up with a second TitanOS
agent.f.family.buddy.title: Backup buddy
agent.f.family.buddy.volumeHint: Kept under .titanos/buddy/<partner>; each partner gets its quota.
agent.f.family.catalog.askHint: The skill itself changes nothing. Tools that change something ask first as always.
agent.f.family.catalog.empty: The app store sources hold no skills yet.
agent.f.family.catalog.intro: The skills come from the app store sources: the folder skills/ in TitanOS-Apps and in own sources. They are loaded like the apps, after the start and once a day. You see the whole content before installing.
agent.f.family.catalog.lead: Skills of other TitanOS users from the app store sources. You see the whole content before installing.
agent.f.family.catalog.offHint: Owners and administrators switch it on.
agent.f.family.catalog.secret: The skill contains something that looks like a password or key; it cannot be installed.
agent.f.family.catalog.shareHint: Downloads a skill as a package to submit as skills/<name>/skill.yaml to TitanOS-Apps or an own source.
agent.f.family.catalog.sub: Skills from the community app store
agent.f.family.catalog.title: Skill catalog
agent.f.family.catalog.unknown: This account does not have these tools: {tools}. It cannot be installed.
agent.f.foresight.a.addSpareSub: Then the rebuild starts by itself.
agent.f.foresight.a.checkCableSub: CRC errors mostly come from the cable or port.
agent.f.foresight.a.mirror: Consider a volume with a mirror
agent.f.foresight.auto: Starts by itself with the spare.
agent.f.foresight.c.cable: CRC errors rising: check the cable or port, not the disk
agent.f.foresight.c.cpuBusy: {percent} % on average, {hours} hours of the last day under heavy load
agent.f.foresight.c.gpuFull: Graphics memory full: {used} of {total} · a smaller model or more graphics memory
agent.f.foresight.c.noSmart: No SMART values, asleep since the start
agent.f.foresight.c.sectorsStable: {to} reallocated sectors, the same for weeks
agent.f.foresight.c.smartFailed: The disk itself reports a failure (SMART)
agent.f.foresight.c.volumeFilling: {percent} % full · at the current growth full in about {days} days
agent.f.foresight.c.wornOutDays: {percent} % worn, at the end in about {days} days
agent.f.foresight.e.agentStops: The AI agent can no longer save anything
agent.f.foresight.empty: No report yet. The first run comes at night, or check now.
agent.f.foresight.failHead: {disk} will probably fail in the coming months
agent.f.foresight.footer: Computes at night only with values that are there without waking the disks.
agent.f.foresight.footerNoPrices: Replacement with price is switched off (needs the web search).
agent.f.foresight.footerWhatIf: Computed only; nothing on the NAS was changed.
agent.f.foresight.full.days: At the current growth ({perDay} a day) full in about {days} days; {free} free.
agent.f.foresight.full.head: Volume {volume} is {pct} % full
agent.f.foresight.gap.days: “{share}”{size} has had no backup for {days} days
agent.f.foresight.gap.never: “{share}” has no backup outside the volume
agent.f.foresight.gap.unknown: “{share}”: state of the backup not known right now
agent.f.foresight.lv.head: {to} instead of {from}
agent.f.foresight.lv.newVolume: Only via a new volume and copying; back up first.
agent.f.foresight.lv.noFit: The {used} in use do not fit.
agent.f.foresight.lv.toleranceSub: Today the volume survives {a} failed disk(s), with {to} {b}
agent.f.foresight.noHistory: Computed without the SMART history, with today’s values only (the volume with the history was asleep).
agent.f.foresight.o.alreadyFailedSub: Volume {volume} waits for a replacement disk.
agent.f.foresight.o.cacheLost: {disk} is the read and write cache of {volume}
agent.f.foresight.o.cacheLostSub: What was not yet written to the disks would be lost.
agent.f.foresight.o.cacheNoLossSub: It gets slower; nothing is lost.
agent.f.foresight.o.lostSub: {level}: if {disk} fails, the {bytes} only come back from a backup.
agent.f.foresight.o.noRedundancySub: {level} with {n} disks: if {disk} fails, all {bytes} depend on the remaining disks.
agent.f.foresight.o.possiblyLostSub: RAID 10 with a disk failed already: whether the {bytes} stay depends on which disk fails.
agent.f.foresight.o.redundantSub: {level} with {n} disks: if {disk} fails, there is still a copy of all data.
agent.f.foresight.o.spareSub: Nothing is lost, but the spare is gone afterwards.
agent.f.foresight.offers: Replacement from the web search (foreign pages, not checked)
agent.f.foresight.r.longRebuild: The rebuild takes more than a day
agent.f.foresight.r.unknownSmart: There are no SMART values of {disk}
agent.f.foresight.rebuildBtrfs: Spread {size} of data again, about {time} ({how}: {speed} MB/s)
agent.f.foresight.rebuildSub: With a new {size} disk about {time} ({how}: {speed} MB/s)
agent.f.foresight.set.atHint: Waits while disks sleep and makes the run up during the day.
agent.f.foresight.set.bottlenecksSub: Memory, volumes, CPU, graphics card, temperatures
agent.f.foresight.set.monthlySub: Once a month a message over the notifications set up
agent.f.foresight.set.predictSub: From the SMART history: reallocated and pending sectors, read errors, wear, time in service
agent.f.foresight.set.pricesNoWeb: The web search is blocked in the agent’s rights; without it there are no prices.
agent.f.foresight.set.pricesSub: Searches the web for a replacement of disks at risk, with model and size only
agent.f.foresight.snapshots: Snapshots lie on the same disks and do not protect against their failure.
agent.f.foresight.whatIfData: Only values titand knows anyway are used: volumes and disks, cached SMART values, the measured rebuild speed and the last success of every backup. No disk is woken.
agent.f.foresight.whatIfIntro: Plays through on a model of the NAS what happens when a disk fails, a volume runs full or another RAID level were chosen. It only computes; nothing on the NAS changes.
agent.f.foresight.whatIfSub: In the chat and as “Play through” on disks
agent.f.foresight.whatIfWhere: Found under Storage › disk or volume › “Play through” and in the chat, e.g. “What happens if sdb fails?”
agent.f.intro: Everything is off by default. Tap a function for its settings.
agent.f.notThere: This function is not switched on on this NAS.
agent.f.protect.adminOnly: Owners and administrators set up the protection functions.
agent.f.protect.e.codeLabel: One-time code (if you have a printed one)
agent.f.protect.e.codeText: Print it and keep it safe. With this code the emergency access opens without waiting. It works once and is shown only now.
agent.f.protect.e.declineConfirm: {name} gets no access to {shares} and the emergency handbook. The person sees that the request was declined and can ask again later.
agent.f.protect.e.endConfirm: {name} loses the read access to {shares} and the emergency handbook at once. Exactly what the emergency access gave is taken back.
agent.f.protect.e.explain: In an emergency you can request read access to {shares} and the emergency handbook here. The owners are told at once and may decline; without an answer you get access after {days} days.
agent.f.protect.e.footer: Every access is in the activity log. The access ends by itself after 30 days.
agent.f.protect.e.grantConfirm: {name} gets read access to {shares} and the emergency handbook at once, for 30 days.
agent.f.protect.e.mineGrantedText: You can read {shares} until {until} (Files or the Windows share).
agent.f.protect.e.mineWaitingText: If nobody declines, the access opens on {when}.
agent.f.protect.e.noPersons: Nobody registered yet. Add persons in the settings below.
agent.f.protect.e.notRegistered: You are not registered for the emergency access.
agent.f.protect.e.rowSub: Request with {days} days of waiting time
agent.f.protect.e.without: Without an answer the access opens on {when}: read-only on
agent.f.protect.g.confirmText.dismiss: “{share}” is opened again and nothing is restored. The share raises no alarm for an hour.
agent.f.protect.g.confirmText.reopen: Everyone gets their previous rights on “{share}” back. If the device is still infected, it can go on encrypting.
agent.f.protect.g.confirmText.restore: The {count} affected files in “{share}” come back from the snapshot. What is there now goes to the share's recycle bin. The share stays read-only until you open it.
agent.f.protect.g.didLock: I set the share to read-only and cut the device off. There is no snapshot from before.
agent.f.protect.g.didRestore: {count} files are restored, {bin} changed files are in the share's recycle bin.
agent.f.protect.g.didSnap: I set the share to read-only, cut the device off and held the snapshot from {time}.
agent.f.protect.g.noBtrfs: Without Btrfs there is no snapshot. Btrfs snapshots protect better.
agent.f.protect.g.noSnapshot: There is no snapshot from before the incident.
agent.f.protect.g.notListed: {count} more are not listed one by one
agent.f.protect.g.notWatching: The guard is not watching right now: {error}
agent.f.protect.g.onlyTold: Reported only: the share stays writable (setting “Report only”).

agent.f.protect.g.restoreSub: {count} files; the changed files go to the recycle bin
agent.f.protect.g.starting: The guard starts with the next round (within a minute).
agent.f.protect.g.wantedSub: e.g. your own encryption; open the share, restore nothing
agent.f.protect.g.watching: The guard watches the shares on all mounted volumes.
agent.f.protect.g.what.notes: {when} ransom notes appeared in several folders ({count} files)
agent.f.protect.g.what.rewrite: {when} {count} files were rewritten with content that looks encrypted
agent.f.protect.g.what.unknown-extension: {when} {count} files were renamed to unknown extensions ({ext})
agent.f.protect.h.nightly: Made again at night when something changed.
agent.f.protect.h.rowSub: Build of the NAS and “What to do when …”
agent.f.protect.s.codeHint: Grants without waiting; one printable code per person
agent.f.protect.s.contactsHint: Your own entries, e.g. who helps in an emergency
agent.f.protect.s.excludeHint: e.g. a share that receives encrypted backups
agent.f.protect.s.modeHint.auto: Like “Lock and report”, and restore by itself once it stops.
agent.f.protect.s.modeHint.lock: Share read-only, device cut off, snapshot held; restore after you confirm.
agent.f.protect.s.modeHint.report: Tell owners and administrators; the share stays writable.
agent.f.protect.s.pre: Hourly snapshot to go back to (Btrfs)
agent.f.protect.s.preHint: Only while data is written anyway, kept two days; wakes no disk.
agent.f.protect.s.probesHint: From the monthly probes of the backups
agent.f.protect.s.quiet: Quiet seconds until it counts as stopped
agent.f.protect.s.readOnly: The emergency access never gives write access and never more than the person has; when it ends it takes back exactly what it gave.
agent.f.protect.s.title: Settings
agent.f.title: Functions
agent.folderHint: Applies to all file tools and the search; the stricter rule wins. "Denied" also hides the folder in listings.
agent.greet.night.4: Good evening, {name} – or is it morning?
agent.haAssistAs: Questions from Home Assistant run as
agent.haAssistHint: The agent becomes a conversation agent in Home Assistant (app, voice devices). Only the Home Assistant address set up may reach it this way.
agent.haAssistSetup: In Home Assistant: Settings › Devices & services › Add integration › Ollama, URL {url}, model "titanos-agent". Then choose it as conversation agent under Voice assistants.
agent.haIntro: The agent uses the connection under Settings › Home Assistant: read and switch devices, history, diagnostics, automations.
agent.haKindsHint: For each kind: may the agent look at it, and may it switch it – yes, only after asking, or no.
agent.haNoConnection: There is no active connection to Home Assistant; the agent has no tools there.
agent.haNotify: Messages through the Home Assistant app
agent.haNotifyHint: Notify services, separated by commas. Results of scheduled tasks and own initiative also go there.
agent.haReleaseHint: A list of its own, apart from 'Release devices for MCP'. The agent can only read what it sees; whether it may switch it is set per kind of device.
agent.haRights: What the agent may do in Home Assistant
agent.haRightsHint: Applies to the chat and to planned tasks. The same switches are under Rights › Home Assistant.
agent.haRules: Exceptions for single devices and rooms
agent.haRulesHint: entity:… for a device, area:… for a room. An exception comes before the kind of device: 'Without asking' switches without asking even where the agent would ask; 'Denied' also keeps the device from being looked at. Locks, alarm systems and automations ask before switching unless set otherwise – looking at them never asks.
agent.haScopeAllHint: Every device of this connection, also ones added later.
agent.haScopeNoneWarn: The agent sees no device of Home Assistant and so cannot read or switch anything. Choose “Selection” or “Everything”.
agent.haSwitchHint: Call services, save automations and scripts. Applies to every kind of device where nothing else is chosen below.
agent.head.title: Project, model and thinking level
agent.heroDown: Switched on, Ollama cannot be reached right now
agent.home.approvalDesc: The agent has been waiting since {time}. The chat shows what it wants to do.
agent.inbox.askText: Please look into this: “{title}”. What is behind it, and what should I do?
agent.inbox.title: Suggestions
agent.init.backgroundHint: watch, night and forecast never wake a disk
agent.init.forecastHint: e.g. “Data is full in about 23 days”
agent.init.gpu: Graphics card at night at most
agent.init.knowHint: It looks at the NAS and asks what matters to you
agent.init.levelHint.act: Acts itself: on messages it looks itself and fixes within its rights; you read it in the chat.
agent.init.levelHint.hints: Hints: it collects what it notices under “Suggestions”.
agent.init.levelHint.quiet: Quiet: it only speaks when you ask.
agent.init.levelHint.suggest: Suggestions: it comes with ideas but changes nothing without your yes.
agent.init.memoryAuto: Remember on its own in the chat
agent.init.morningNote: Say in the morning what it learned
agent.init.name: Name
agent.init.quietHint: then it starts nothing by itself, only suggestions
agent.init.reflectHint: picks out facts, preferences and open points
agent.init.searchHint: Where it searches for files. Nothing chosen: everywhere you have access. Other places only when you name them in the chat (“search the backup too”).
agent.init.watchHint: without the model while all is calm; a suggestion on warnings
agent.inputIdle: Task for the agent – e.g. "How much space do the movies take?"
agent.inputPending: Answer the approval above first – or write something else (declines).
agent.instructionHint: Besides this, the agent knows the NAS map, its skills and its memory. Every account can add an instruction of its own.
agent.instructionIntro: Applies in every chat of all accounts, before everything else: what this NAS is, what the shares mean, how the agent should answer and work.
agent.instructionTemplate:
This is our NAS at home.

Shares:
- Photos: all phone photos, sorted by year/month
- Documents: invoices, contracts, taxes
- Backup: backups of Home Assistant and the PCs

Important:
- Home Assistant is the VM HAOS, the container is for testing only.
- Always back up before updating Home Assistant.
- Answer briefly, tables for comparisons.
- Never delete anything in Photos.
agent.keepAliveHint: When the agent opens, TitanOS loads the model in advance. Keeping it longer means fast answers, but the graphics memory stays in use.
agent.know.docsNone: This account has no place the agent could look things up in.
agent.know.lead: What the agent knows besides its memory: your instructions, its procedures and the picture of this NAS.
agent.know.mapDesc: Volumes, shares, apps, VMs and where things are
agent.know.projectsNone: No project has an instruction yet
agent.knowAsk: Get to know me and my NAS: look at the NAS map (shares, apps, VMs, backups, Home Assistant) and sum up briefly what you found. Then ask me with choice buttons what matters most to me (e.g. keeping photos and documents safe, smart home, media, security, saving power) and who uses the NAS. Afterwards suggest three fitting planned tasks or reminders and create them only when I agree.
agent.lazyToolsHint: The model first gets only the main tools and loads further areas itself. Saves a lot of context; off: all tools at once.
agent.locationsHint: Names you use in the chat ("put it with the Home Assistant backups"). The agent knows shares, apps and VMs by itself.
agent.logIntro: What the agent changed in the last 30 days (from the activity log).
agent.mapIntro: What the agent knows about your NAS: shares with folders, apps, VMs, system containers, backups, rooms. Descriptions help it find everything.
agent.maxMinutesHint: Then it reports where it stands and asks whether to go on.
agent.maxStepsHint: Then it stops and asks whether to go on.
agent.mcp.hint: MCP servers whose tools the agent may use as well, for example n8n. Every call asks first unless the area “Connections (MCP)” under Rights is set to “Without asking”. What such a server answers counts as outside content. Owners and administrators only.
agent.mcp.name: Name
agent.mcp.title: Connections to other programs (MCP)
agent.mcp.token: Token (if the server asks for one)
agent.mcp.tokenKept: A token is stored – leave empty to keep it
agent.meHint: e.g. "Answer briefly, always ask before deleting."
agent.meIntro: Only for your account, in addition to the top instruction: how you want to be addressed, how detailed, what to watch for.
agent.mem.clearDesc: Forgets everything except what is pinned
agent.mem.clearSure: The agent forgets everything that is not pinned. This cannot be undone.
agent.mem.lead: This is what the agent remembered – from your corrections and what you told it. It gets it in every chat.
agent.membersHint: These accounts see the project, its instructions and the chats in it and can start chats of their own. Each chat stays with whoever writes it and runs with their rights.
agent.membersNone: No other accounts may use the agent.
agent.memoryIntro: What the agent remembered on its own – from your corrections and statements. It gets this in every chat.
agent.memoryNewHint: e.g. "My Home Assistant is the VM HAOS"
agent.modelNameHint: A name of your own for this model, e.g. “Jarvis”. The chat shows it instead of the model's name; the list of models keeps the real name in small below it. Empty: the model's name.
agent.morningExtraHint: e.g. “and tell me if the bins are collected today”
agent.morningIntro: A short overview in the morning as a message and a chat. You choose what goes in.
agent.morningToday: Reminders and tasks of the day
agent.nasRights: Only what you also see in the file manager
agent.noToolModel: No model with tools found. Pull e.g. gpt-oss:20b or qwen3 in Ollama.
agent.noVolume: The agent needs a mounted data volume for its chats.
agent.nodesIntro: Nodes that want to use the model of this agent. They get only the model; chats and rights stay on each node.
agent.notAllowed: An owner can allow it for your account under Settings › AI agent.
agent.notAllowedTitle: The AI agent is not allowed for your account
agent.noteEdited: Changed in the file in the folder KI-Agent – the agent reads the text as content
agent.noteInterrupted: Interrupted – TitanOS was restarted or updated.
agent.noteLoop: Stopped: the same step came again and again.
agent.noteNotDone: Note from TitanOS: this has not happened yet. There is only the card above – only with it is something sent, saved or moved.
agent.noteSummary: Older parts of the chat summarised
agent.notes.conflict: The note was changed elsewhere (another device or the file manager). Your change is not saved.
agent.notes.deleteFolderText: The folder “{name}” is deleted with {count} notes and all subfolders.
agent.notes.empty: No notes yet. Make one with the pen, or tell the agent “write me a note …”.
agent.notes.heading: Heading
agent.notes.name: Name
agent.notes.pick: Pick a note or make a new one.
agent.notes.title: Notes
agent.nvrNamesHint: The agent gets the names of recognised people and the plates read. Off from the factory; it never gets pictures.
agent.offAdmin: Switch it on under Settings › AI agent and enter your Ollama.
agent.offUser: An owner can switch it on under Settings › AI agent.
agent.ollamaDownLong: Ollama is not reachable ({error}). Scheduled tasks and reactions to notifications run again once it answers.
agent.ollamaHint: Address of your Ollama server on the home network, e.g. http://192.168.10.5:11434.
agent.phoneAppIntro: The KI-Agent as an app of its own on the home screen. First choose how the phone reaches the NAS, then scan the QR code.
agent.phoneHttpsHint: Notifications on the phone and the home screen icon need HTTPS. Ways that are not set up appear once they run.
agent.phoneNoUrl: Enter an address with http:// or https://.
agent.photos.desc: Let the agent search your photos in Immich
agent.photos.immichOff: Not installed or stopped. Without Immich the agent has no photos.
agent.photos.intro: With the API key of your own Immich account the agent searches your photos – for example “pictures from the 2025 holiday”. It sees only the photos of that Immich account and changes nothing there.
agent.photos.key: API key of your Immich account
agent.photos.keyHow: In Immich: Account Settings › API Keys › New API Key. The permissions asset.read, asset.view, person.read and user.read are enough. The key stays encrypted on the NAS and is never shown here again.
agent.photos.missing: The key lacks these permissions: {list}. Without them part of the search is missing (e.g. by person).
agent.photos.noSmart: Searching by what is in the picture (smart search) is off in Immich. The agent then searches only by date, place and person.
agent.photos.privacy: Thumbnails come only through TitanOS and only for photos of your own Immich account. With a provider on the internet, date and place of the photos found go to it, the pictures do not.
agent.photos.removed: Key removed. The agent has no photos any more.
agent.photos.saved: Saved. The agent now searches the photos of “{name}”.
agent.photos.title: Photos (Immich)
agent.picturesMain: The main model {model} sees pictures itself (photos, screenshots, type plates in the chat).
agent.picturesNone: The main model sees no pictures. Choose a main model with pictures (e.g. gemma4:12b) or a model of its own for pictures.
agent.plus.title: Add to the chat
agent.presetHint: Sets all areas at once. Then you can change each area and tool on its own.
agent.profile.assistHint: You see the chats, the memory and the plans of the questions from Home Assistant – apart from your account.
agent.projectEmpty: No chats in this project yet.
agent.projectInstructionsHint: e.g. "My Home Assistant is the VM HAOS. Always back up before updates."
agent.projectRemoveHint: The chats stay, just without a project.
agent.projectShared: Project shared by {name} – only {name} can change it.
agent.providerHint: From the factory the agent asks an Ollama server of yours. Without a graphics card of your own you can use a provider on the internet instead.
agent.providerKeyClaude: The API key from the Claude Console (console.anthropic.com). It stays on the NAS and is never shown again.
agent.providerKeyHint: The key from your account at the provider. It stays on the NAS and is never shown again; for another address you have to enter it again. Leave empty for a server on the home network without a key.
agent.providerKeySet: stored – leave empty to keep it
agent.providerUrlHint: The address of the API, with https:// and the path up to /v1 – for example https://api.openai.com/v1, https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, https://api.groq.com/openai/v1, https://api.mistral.ai/v1. A server on the home network (LM Studio: http://192.168.1.20:1234/v1) may be http and counts as local.
agent.providerWarn: With a provider on the internet everything the agent reads leaves your NAS: your questions, contents of files, names of devices, logs. The provider's terms and prices apply; every answer costs money there. Your rights for the agent apply unchanged. The chat then shows “Cloud” next to the model.
agent.pullHint: Downloads a model from the Ollama library onto your Ollama server, e.g. qwen3:8b. Big models take a while.
agent.pushHint.text: Then the KI-Agent tells you on this device when a task is done or waits for you, and a tap opens the chat here.
agent.pushHint.title: Allow notifications?
agent.quickHint: TitanOS carries out short, unambiguous sentences itself, without asking the model: “floor lamp on”, “turn off the living room light”, “set the floor lamp to 40 percent”, “open the awning”, “is the TV on?”, “timer 10 minutes”, “remind me in 20 minutes about the pizza”. The same rights and released devices apply as otherwise; whatever would be asked about or is not unambiguous goes to the model. Locks, alarms and heating are never quick commands.
agent.react: Look into notifications of the NAS and act on its own
agent.reactHint: On warnings and errors (disk, temperature, backup …) the agent analyses and fixes within its permissions. At most once an hour per kind; every action shows as a chat "On its own: …" and in the activity log.
agent.runs.limitMany: {n} chats are already running. The setting “Runs at once per account” allows no more at the same time. Wait until one is done, or stop one.
agent.runs.limitOne: A chat is already running. The setting “Runs at once per account” allows no more at the same time. Wait until it is done, or stop it.
agent.runs.ollamaHint: For {n} runs to really work at once, Ollama must run with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL={n} or more, otherwise they wait for each other. A single answer does not get faster, and every run takes memory of its own for its context. TitanOS does not manage Ollama and does not set this there itself.
agent.runs.ollamaHintAny: Several chats only work at the same time in Ollama when it runs with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL set high enough, otherwise they wait for each other there. A single answer does not get faster, and every run takes memory of its own for its context. TitanOS does not manage Ollama and does not set this there itself.
agent.runs.providerHint: The same limit applies with a provider. Every run sends its own requests; the provider's limits and costs apply to each of them.
agent.runs.settingHint: How many chats of one account may work at the same time. From the factory there is no limit, as up to 1.00. A chat always has only one run. Planned tasks, reactions to notifications and questions from Home Assistant do not count and always start.
agent.scheduleButton: Offer as a button in Home Assistant (MQTT, group "AI agent" under Settings › Home Assistant)
agent.scheduleWakeHint: Only for this task. “Ask first” holds the task until you agree.
agent.schedulesEmpty: Nothing planned yet. Say in the chat e.g. “Remind me tomorrow at 9 about the doctor” or “Run a health check every Monday”.
agent.schedulesIntro: Tasks and reminders: once, again and again or on a state in Home Assistant. Just say it in the chat (“remind me tomorrow at 9”) or add it here. Missed times (NAS off) run once after the start.
agent.searxHint: Enter the whole address of your SearXNG, with http:// in front and the port at the end – for the Docker app “SearXNG” on this NAS that is {example} (port 8580). Add nothing behind it, no /search either. The agent then searches there instead of through DuckDuckGo's page; when the address does not answer, it uses DuckDuckGo. Leave empty for DuckDuckGo.
agent.set.chatWidthHint: On the computer; on the phone the chat always uses the whole width.
agent.set.colorLowContrast: ⚠ Hard to read: too little contrast to the background.
agent.set.gesturesDesc: Swiping chats, swiping from the edge, vibration
agent.set.initiativeDesc: Watch, thinking at night, quiet hours, sleeping disks
agent.set.keepAwake: Keep the screen on while it works
agent.set.lead: For your account. What only applies to this device is under “This device”.
agent.set.lookDesc: Text size, animations, showing the thinking steps
agent.set.modelsDesc: Default for new chats and for pictures
agent.set.modelsHint: Which model a chat uses you choose at the top of the chat. The owner sets the models of the NAS.
agent.set.nasDesc: Ollama server, rights per area, accounts – in the control panel
agent.set.noChats: There are no chats of your own.
agent.set.personalityDesc: Name, tone and length of the answers, learning skills
agent.set.pushHint: Switch on notifications for this device here and choose per device what comes: messages of TitanOS and of the AI agent. On an iPhone the agent from the home screen is an app of its own and so a device of its own: it is enough to add one of the two apps and switch on both there. While a chat is open on a device, no notification comes for it.
agent.set.readAutoHint: Off: a “Read aloud” button at each answer
agent.set.swipeLeft: Swipe a chat to the left
agent.set.swipeRight: Swipe a chat to the right
agent.set.textColor: Colour of the text beside the dots
agent.set.title: Settings
agent.set.whisperNas: through the speech services of this NAS
agent.settingsIntro: An agent that does tasks on this NAS on its own. It uses the same tools as the MCP server, with permissions of its own.
agent.shareNoCluster: This node is no longer in a cluster.
agent.shareNotAsked: No request to {node} yet. Save first, then ask.
agent.shareOff: {node} does not share its agent yet: send a request. The agent there has to be switched on.
agent.shareOld: {node} runs an older version without a shared agent. Update {node} first.
agent.sharePending: The request is with {node}. Release it there under Settings › KI-Agent › Other nodes of the cluster.
agent.sheetNoFiles: The agent has not made files in this project yet.
agent.sheetNoInstructions: No instructions – add them under "Edit project".
agent.sideResizeHint: Drag or use the arrow keys to change the width; a double click resets it.
agent.skillsIntro: Procedures the agent follows for matching tasks. It writes its own when something repeats.
agent.snapshotsHint: Before the agent updates or removes an app, or moves, renames or replaces files, TitanOS takes a snapshot of the volume (Btrfs only, at most one in 10 minutes, kept 7 days). Deleted files go to the recycle bin of the share anyway. Single files come back on the storage page.
agent.sourceHint: With the agent of the admin node only the model comes from there. Chats, memory, rights and folders stay on this node. The admin node has to release this node.
agent.suggKnowSub: It looks at your NAS and asks what matters to you
agent.suggNasSub: Find the cause and fix it
agent.suggestApps: How are my apps, VMs and containers doing? Any crashes or errors in the logs?
agent.suggestClean: Where can I free up space? Show me big and duplicate files with their size.
agent.suggestDocument: 📝 Make a Word overview of all Docker apps
agent.suggestEnergy: How much power does the NAS use today, and do the disks sleep when they have nothing to do?
agent.suggestHome: Is everything closed at home? Check windows, doors, locks and the alarm in Home Assistant.
agent.suggestNas: What is behind the message “{title}”? Find the cause and tell me what to do.
agent.suggestNight: What happened on the NAS since last night? Backups, messages, updates, anything unusual – in short.
agent.suggestUpdates: Which updates are there for the system, apps and containers, and what do they bring? What would you install?
agent.tabs.label: Sections of the AI agent
agent.tabs.noProjects: No project yet. A project bundles chats, instructions and files on one topic.
agent.talk.hint: Just start talking. After a short pause it is sent, the answer is read aloud, then the agent listens again. You can talk over it at any time.
agent.talk.hintWake: Start with “{word}”, for example “{word}, how is the NAS?”. Anything else is not sent. After an answer you can go on for a few seconds without the word – and talk over the agent at any time.
agent.talk.notSent: That did not get through. Please say it again.
agent.talk.pending: A step waits for your approval. End talk mode and decide in the chat.
agent.talk.title: Talk mode
agent.thinkHint: The model reports its levels itself (Ollama thinking.values); other models show more, finer or only on/off. Changeable per message in the chat.
agent.unsavedLeave: The changes to the settings of the AI agent are not saved yet. If you discard them, everything stays as it was.
agent.untrustedHint: Written after the agent had read files or web pages. Check that it is right.
agent.visionHint: Loaded only when a picture is in the chat. If it does not fit into the graphics memory together with the main model, Ollama switches between them (a few seconds).
agent.visionOwn: Use a model of its own for pictures
agent.voiceHint: Easiest through the speech services of this NAS (Settings › Speech services, “In the KI-Agent”). Or a Whisper service of your own with the OpenAI interface, e.g. on the Ollama computer; the recording goes there through the NAS and is not kept.
agent.voiceNas: The microphone uses the speech services of this NAS
agent.voiceNasHint: Speech input runs through Whisper in the speech services of TitanOS. A Whisper service of your own is not needed for it.
agent.voiceNoMic: No access to the microphone. Allow it in the browser (on the iPhone only over HTTPS).
agent.vol.chooseText: Choose the volume for the agent's chats, memory, notes, scripts and documents. It can be moved later.
agent.vol.chooseTitle: Where does the agent keep its data?
agent.vol.cleanup: Leftovers on {from} could not be deleted.
agent.vol.failed: Move stopped: {error} The data stays on {from}. If something changed in the folder meanwhile, just move again.
agent.vol.hint: An SSD is better: the agent writes often, hard disks could not sleep then.
agent.vol.intro: Everything the agent needs lives here: chats with thoughts and steps, memory, notes, scripts, documents and skills. The language models stay with Ollama.
agent.vol.missing: Not mounted – the agent waits until the volume is back.
agent.vol.moveText: Everything is copied from {from} to the chosen volume and checked. Only then the new volume counts and {from} is cleaned up. While it moves, the agent pauses; running tasks must be finished first.
agent.vol.noneMounted: No volume is mounted. First create a volume under Storage.
agent.vol.oldConfirm: The old copy of the agent's data on {volume} is deleted for good. The data on the new volume stays.
agent.vol.oldText: After a move the old state stays, so nothing written over SMB at the last moment is lost.
agent.vol.title: Storage location
agent.vramNow: Graphics memory of the loaded models: {gb} GB
agent.webFree: Internet without asking also after content was read
agent.webFreeHint: Off from the factory: once a chat has read files, devices of Home Assistant, logs or attachments, the agent asks before every web search and every web page – content it read could tell it to send something out. Switched on, what is set under “Internet” always applies – also with skills from the catalogue and with memories from such chats, which otherwise make every web search ask. Research that only reads the web no longer asks at every step either way.
agent.weeklyReport: Send a weekly report on Mondays: what the agent changed (through notifications)
agent.whereCluster: Runs on the model of another cluster node
agent.whereLocal: Runs locally on this NAS through Ollama
agent.whereOwn: Runs on your own Ollama server
agent.whisperSetupHint: Whisper runs in the speech services of this NAS (with a graphics card if there is one); an app of its own is not needed for it.
agentpim.act.calendar.day.prompt: Give me a short overview of today: events and reminders due.
agentpim.act.calendar.free.prompt: When do I have an hour free in the next seven days (weekdays 8 am to 6 pm)?
agentpim.act.calendar.week.prompt: Give me a short overview of this week: events, free time and reminders due.
agentpim.act.contacts.complete.prompt: Complete the missing details of the open contact from my mail and events, where they are clear there.
agentpim.act.contacts.duplicates.prompt: Find contacts that may be duplicates and name them. Merge nothing.
agentpim.act.contacts.fromText.prompt: Add a contact from this signature or text:
agentpim.act.mail.contact.prompt: Add the sender of the open mail as a contact, with name, address and the details of the signature. Check first whether they exist already.
agentpim.act.mail.event.prompt: Add an event from the open mail if it names one (date, time, place).
agentpim.act.mail.folder.prompt: Suggest a fitting folder for the open mail (mail_folders) and move it there.
agentpim.act.mail.reply.prompt: Draft a short, friendly answer to the open mail (mail_send with reply). Send nothing without me.
agentpim.act.mail.summarize.prompt: Summarize the open mail briefly: what it is about, what is expected of me and by when.
agentpim.action.contact.create.desc: A new contact in the address book.
agentpim.action.contact.update.desc: Change numbers, addresses and other details.
agentpim.action.event.create.desc: A new event in one of your calendars.
agentpim.action.event.update.desc: Repeating a whole series anew always asks.
agentpim.action.mail.draft: Keep a draft in the drafts folder
agentpim.action.mail.draft.desc: Write a mail without sending it.
agentpim.action.mail.move.desc: Into another folder; into the trash or junk always asks.
agentpim.action.mail.read.desc: Off: the AI agent does not see Mail at all – no reading, no draft, no sending.
agentpim.action.mail.send.desc: “Do it itself” only here, on its own; once the chat has read a mail, an event or a contact, sending still always asks.
agentpim.action.task.complete.desc: Mark it done or open it again.
agentpim.action.task.create.desc: A new reminder in a list.
agentpim.action.task.update.desc: Change title, notes, due date or list.
agentpim.cloud.settings: If the model runs at a provider on the internet (Connection and models), the mail, contacts, events and reminders the AI agent reads go to that provider. With Ollama in your home network they stay on your devices.
agentpim.cloud.text: What the AI agent reads here – mail, contacts, events and reminders – goes to that provider. With Ollama in your home network everything stays on your devices (Settings › AI agent › Connection and models).

appaccess.adminAlways: Owners and administrators may always use every app; their ticks cannot be cleared.
appaccess.autoNames: Automatically for all apps with a WebUI
appaccess.autoNamesHint: Every Docker app with a WebUI gets an HTTPS name of its own (home network only), so that it opens in a window on the desktop. An app's own settings come first; switching off or editing an automatic name makes it the app's own.
appaccess.caAndroid: Download the .crt file › Settings › Security › More security settings › Encryption & credentials › Install a certificate › CA certificate. Menu names differ between makers.
appaccess.caIntro: Without a certificate from Let's Encrypt or Tailscale, TitanOS issues the certificates of its own addresses and of the HTTPS names itself. Install the certificate authority once on every device: browsers then stop warning, and apps open in windows too.
appaccess.caIos: Load the .crt file in Safari and allow it › Settings › “Profile Downloaded” › Install. Then switch on full trust for the TitanOS certificate authority under Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings.
appaccess.caKey: The private key stays on the stick in /config. TitanOS never hands it out, not even in the diagnostic bundle.
appaccess.caLinux: Copy the .crt file to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run “sudo update-ca-certificates”. Firefox and Chromium keep lists of their own: import it there under Settings › Certificates › Authorities.
appaccess.caMac: Open the .crt file; Keychain Access adds it to the “System” keychain. Double-click the TitanOS certificate authority › “Trust” › “When using this certificate”: “Always Trust”.
appaccess.caNotNeeded: With Let's Encrypt (own domain or IPv64) or a Tailscale name nothing needs to be installed.
appaccess.caUnavailable: The certificate authority is not available right now. Can the stick be read?
appaccess.caWindows: Open the .crt file › “Install Certificate” › “Local Machine” › “Place all certificates in the following store” › “Trusted Root Certification Authorities”. Restart Firefox afterwards.
appaccess.certCa: Issued by the TitanOS certificate authority. Once it is installed on your device, the browser does not warn.
appaccess.gate: Check the login in the browser
appaccess.gateFor: Check the login in the browser for {app}
appaccess.gateHint: Page loads in a browser then need the TitanOS login and the right to the app. Apps on phones and TVs that only use the app's API (e.g. the Immich or Bitwarden app) keep signing in on their own and are not affected. Apps that show the app's web page (e.g. the Jellyfin app for Android or the Home Assistant app) are locked out at the HTTPS name: switch the check off for that app or connect them through the app's port.
appaccess.gateLimit: The lock guards the app's pages in the browser. Its API stays guarded by the app's own login.
appaccess.intro: Who sees and may open which Docker app on the desktop. Without a tick the app is also locked at its address in the browser.
appaccess.newAppsHint: Who gets a newly installed app right away.
appaccess.noNameHint: Apps without an HTTPS name do not open in a window. Switch on the automatic names under “HTTPS names for apps” or give the app a name of its own.
appaccess.noUsers: There are only owners and administrators, and they may use every app. Add normal users under Users.
appaccess.title: Programs

applications.reviewHint: The current job selection may differ from the historic snapshot. New backups also contain the original application journal. The copy is not started and system configuration is not imported into the live NAS.

applications.testCopy: Set up a separate test instance with its own data paths and no public ports, and verify it before replacing existing data.

apps.correctFields: Please correct the highlighted fields in the form.

apps.discardText: The install form for {name} has changes. Switching or closing discards them.
apps.dockerOff: Docker has to be switched on and running to install apps.

apps.missingDevices: Left out because this NAS does not have these devices: {devices}. With them the container would not start.
apps.name: Name of the app
apps.nameExists: An app with this name exists already.
apps.nameInvalid: Only a–z, 0–9, - and _, at most 32 characters.
apps.none: No app found. Missing one? Add a source of your own or import a compose file.
apps.note.appdata: In the app's data folder on the Docker volume.
apps.note.generated: Generated at random. Stored apart from the compose file, in the app's .env.
apps.note.gid: The group all accounts are in, so the app can read and write in shares.
apps.note.noShare: No matching share found – for now the folder lives in the app's data folder. Enter the path of a share here if the app should see existing files.
apps.note.share: Share “{name}”. Append a subfolder if the app should only see a part of it.
apps.note.timezone: Taken from the time zone of the NAS.
apps.note.uid: Your account – files the app creates in shares then belong to you.
apps.officialOffline: The official app catalog could not be loaded (no internet connection?). Apps that are already installed keep running. TitanOS tries again every 15 minutes; “Refresh now” under “App sources” does it right away.
apps.ownVarInvalid: Only letters, digits and _; not starting with a digit
apps.ownVarReplaces: Exists in the template already – your value replaces it
apps.pathInvalid: Give a path on the NAS and a path in the container (starting with /).
apps.pathVolatile: This folder is not on a volume. What the app stores there is gone after the NAS restarts.
apps.portMoved: {port} from the template is in use ({by}) → {free} suggested
apps.risk.capabilities: It gets additional system rights, for example for network settings.
apps.risk.dockerSocket: It may control Docker and can start, change and delete other containers.
apps.risk.hostNetwork: It uses the network of the NAS directly; all its ports are reachable as they are.
apps.risk.privileged: It runs privileged and so has full access to the NAS.
apps.risk.rootMount: It sees the whole file system of the NAS.
apps.risks: This app gets more rights than an ordinary container:

auth.codeHint: This account is protected with a second factor. Enter the six-digit code from your app – or one of your recovery codes.
auth.name: Name
auth.nameHint: You log in with this name. Lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter.
auth.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
auth.passwordTooShort: The password needs at least {min} characters.
auth.rateLimited: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {seconds} seconds.
auth.setupIntro: Create the owner's account. It has all rights on this NAS; you add further accounts later under “Users”.
backup.bandwidthHintCopy: Applies to writing to the destination and reading it back to compare. A copy follows the window while it runs: when the window opens or closes, the new limit holds within a second. The window may pass midnight.
backup.bandwidthHintRestic: Applies to what restic sends and receives during the backup and while clearing out old states. restic keeps the limit that holds at the start for the whole run, even when it runs past the end of the window. Checks and restores run without a limit. The window may pass midnight.
backup.bandwidthWindow: A different limit within a time window
backup.catchUp: If the NAS was off at the planned time, it catches up after the start. The first backup begins right after setting it up.
backup.checkText: restic checks whether the destination of the backup is complete and readable. This runs in the background; reading data downloads it from the destination, which may cost money with cloud storage.
backup.col.name: Backup
backup.copy.dated: Put each run into a dated folder (e.g. 2026-10-31_0300) – simple versions. On exFAT/FAT32 each folder is a full copy; on ext4, NTFS, Btrfs and XFS unchanged files take no extra space.
backup.copy.datedDeleted: With dated folders each folder holds exactly the state of its run; deleted files are in the older folders.
backup.copy.keepDeletedHint: Only new and changed files are added; nothing is deleted. Files deleted by mistake stay on the target.
backup.copy.mirror: Delete them on the target too (mirror)
backup.copy.mirrorHint: The target shows exactly what the NAS holds. Deleted files first go to the folder _gelöscht on the target and are removed for good after
backup.copy.noVersions: Without dated folders there are no versions and nothing “oldest”: when the target is full, the job stops and reports how much space is missing.
backup.copyMirror: mirror; deleted files stay in _gelöscht for a while
backup.copyPatterns: File or folder names, e.g. *.tmp. No paths or **.
backup.copyRestore: Copy files back using the file manager.
backup.extra.configHint: The settings hold accounts, password hashes and 2FA secrets. The backup is encrypted; the job's password protects them.
backup.filesCut: This folder has more than 50,000 entries; not all are shown.
backup.filesSelected: {count} chosen. They are restored into a new folder, never over existing files.
backup.format.encryptedHint: Encrypted with a password. Only the first run writes everything, then only what is new or changed – still every version restores completely. Readable only through TitanOS or restic.
backup.format.fixed: An existing job cannot change its kind; create a new job for that.
backup.format.readableHint: Files lie 1:1 on the target and open on any PC (e.g. exFAT). Each run copies only what is new or changed. Not encrypted – whoever has the target can read everything.
backup.intro: A RAID protects against the failure of a disk, not against deleting, ransomware, fire or theft. A backup copies your shares to another place at regular times – encrypted, so that nobody there can read along, and with the states of the last days, weeks and months.
backup.keepsRolling: continuously, until the target is full
backup.kindHint.local: A folder on another volume of this NAS. Protects against the failure of a volume and against deleting by mistake, not against fire or theft.
backup.kindHint.local-copy: Readable copy in a folder on another volume of this NAS.
backup.kindHint.rest: A server that runs the REST server of restic.
backup.kindHint.s3: Storage in the cloud that speaks the S3 protocol: Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Hetzner Object Storage, a MinIO of your own and others.
backup.kindHint.sftp: Another machine that can be reached over SSH – a second NAS, a server or a storage box. The NAS logs in there with a key of its own.
backup.kindHint.smb: Encrypted versions on an SMB share.
backup.kindHint.smb-copy: Copies selected folder trees to a second NAS. New and changed files are transferred; files deleted at the source remain at the destination. No version history: changed files replace the previous copy.
backup.kindHint.titanos: A second NAS running TitanOS takes the backup, preferably over Tailscale. The backup is encrypted; the other NAS cannot read it.
backup.kindHint.usb: Encrypted versions on an external drive.
backup.kindHint.usb-copy: Directly readable, unencrypted copy. Changed files are replaced; deleted source files are retained. No version history. The selected drive is mounted when needed and left mounted afterwards. Links and special files are not copied and reported as errors.
backup.minute: Minute of the hour (the hour is ignored)
backup.name: Name
backup.nameHint: Letters (A–Z, a–z), digits and hyphens. Cannot be changed later.
backup.neverSaved: Always left out: .titanos, recycle bins and snapshot folders.
backup.nextUnknown: Not known – for example because the volume of the shares is not mounted.
backup.noShares: There is no share on a mounted volume that could be backed up.
backup.note.case_conflict.text: The destination's file system does not tell upper from lower case; only one of the names was saved.
backup.note.changed.many: {count} files changed while they were copied
backup.note.changed.one: 1 file changed while it was copied
backup.note.changed.text: The file changed while it was copied; the copy of the run before stays. The next run tries again.
backup.note.folder_unavailable.text: The folder is chosen in the job but was not there.
backup.note.link_unsupported.text: The destination's file system cannot hold links.
backup.note.mirror_failed.text: Files deleted on the NAS could not be moved at the destination and are still there.
backup.note.name_not_allowed.many: {count} names not allowed at the destination
backup.note.name_not_allowed.one: 1 name not allowed at the destination
backup.note.name_not_allowed.text: The destination's file system does not allow these names (characters like : ? * or a dot at the end).
backup.note.other.text: These entries were not saved for another reason; the system log has the details.
backup.note.read_error.text: These entries could not be read and are missing in the copy.
backup.note.source_unavailable.text: The share or volume was not there during the run and was not saved.
backup.note.too_large.many: {count} files too large for the destination
backup.note.too_large.one: 1 file too large for the destination
backup.note.too_large.text: The destination's file system does not take files this large (FAT32: 4 GB at most).
backup.note.vm_disk_backing_chain.many: {count} VM disks not saved: own snapshots
backup.note.vm_disk_backing_chain.one: 1 VM disk not saved: own snapshots
backup.note.vm_disk_backing_chain.text: The image has snapshots of its own or builds on another image. The earlier copy stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_busy.many: {count} VM disks not saved: VM busy
backup.note.vm_disk_busy.one: 1 VM disk not saved: VM busy
backup.note.vm_disk_busy.text: Another operation of the VM was running, or it was paused. The earlier copy stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_changed.many: {count} disks of running VMs not saved reliably
backup.note.vm_disk_changed.one: 1 disk of a running VM not saved reliably
backup.note.vm_disk_changed.text: The disk changed while it was copied and could not be read from a snapshot. The earlier copy at the destination stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_choice_needed.many: {count} disks of running VMs: choice missing
backup.note.vm_disk_choice_needed.one: 1 disk of a running VM: choice missing
backup.note.vm_disk_choice_needed.text: The job does not say yet how disks of running VMs are saved. Until then they are read as they are.
backup.note.vm_disk_crash_consistent.man: {count} VM disks saved without guest agent
backup.note.vm_disk_crash_consistent.one: 1 VM disk saved without guest agent
backup.note.vm_disk_crash_consistent.tex: From a snapshot of the VM management but without freezing in the guest: the copy is like the disk after a power cut. With the QEMU guest agent in the VM it becomes clean.
backup.note.vm_disk_no_space.many: {count} VM disks not saved: not enough space
backup.note.vm_disk_no_space.one: 1 VM disk not saved: not enough space
backup.note.vm_disk_no_space.text: There was no room next to the disk for the overlay that takes changes during the copy. The earlier copy stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_passthrough.many: {count} VM disks not saved: passed-through disk
backup.note.vm_disk_passthrough.one: 1 VM disk not saved: passed-through disk
backup.note.vm_disk_passthrough.text: The VM has a whole disk of the NAS; its state cannot be frozen. The earlier copy stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_pause_failed.many: {count} VM disks not saved: pause refused
backup.note.vm_disk_pause_failed.one: 1 VM disk not saved: pause refused
backup.note.vm_disk_pause_failed.text: The VM could not be paused. The earlier copy stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_pause_timeout.many: {count} VM disks not saved: pause too long
backup.note.vm_disk_pause_timeout.one: 1 VM disk not saved: pause too long
backup.note.vm_disk_pause_timeout.text: The copy was not done when the longest allowed pause was reached; the VM runs again. The earlier copy stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_paused.many: {count} VM disks saved while the VM was paused
backup.note.vm_disk_paused.one: 1 VM disk saved while the VM was paused
backup.note.vm_disk_paused.text: The VM was paused for the copy and runs again.
backup.note.vm_disk_raw_image.text: A raw image cannot be frozen; it was not saved in this run.
backup.note.vm_disk_skipped.text: The VM was running and the job says “Skip” (for all disks of running VMs or for disks without snapshot). The disk was not read, the earlier copy at the destination stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_snapshot_failed.many: {count} VM disks not saved: snapshot refused
backup.note.vm_disk_snapshot_failed.one: 1 VM disk not saved: snapshot refused
backup.note.vm_disk_snapshot_failed.text: The VM management refused the snapshot. The earlier copy stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_snapshot_unproven.ma: {count} VM disks without snapshot not saved
backup.note.vm_disk_snapshot_unproven.on: 1 VM disk without snapshot not saved
backup.note.vm_disk_snapshot_unproven.te: The snapshot of the VM management is not switched on in the job; the disk was not read, the earlier copy stays.
backup.note.vm_disk_undo_failed.many: {count} VMs not back to normal after the backup
backup.note.vm_disk_undo_failed.one: 1 VM not back to normal after the backup
backup.note.vm_disk_undo_failed.text: The VM is still paused or still writes to the overlay. Its data are complete; TitanOS tries again. Check under VMs whether it runs.
backup.notes.legacy: The backup was made but not everything could be read (message of the NAS as it is):
backup.pairCodeHint: Make the code on the other NAS under Settings › Backups › “Accept backups of other TitanOS”.
backup.pairCodeInvalid: This is not a valid pairing code.
backup.passwordReason: With this password the backup can be read. Enter your own password once more to see it.
backup.passwordText: The backup is encrypted with this password. TitanOS knows it; but if the NAS itself is lost, you need it to get at your data.
backup.passwordWarn: Write it down now or put it into your password manager – apart from the NAS. Without the password the backup is worthless, and nobody can reset it.
backup.patterns: Leave out files (one pattern per line)
backup.patternsHint: For example *.tmp or node_modules. The recycle bin and half-finished uploads are always left out. Disks of running VMs are saved crash-consistent only.
backup.pick.hint: Click a field and choose the folder you want to back up – a share, a subfolder or a whole volume.
backup.pick.title: Choose folder
backup.placeHint.local: A folder on another volume of this NAS. You decide whether the backup is readable or encrypted.
backup.placeHint.smb: Backs up to a share of another NAS or PC (SMB3). You decide whether the backup is readable or encrypted.
backup.placeHint.usb: Backs up to an external drive. You decide whether the backup is readable on a PC or encrypted.
backup.publicKeyHint: Put this line into the file authorized_keys of the user on the server. At the first connection TitanOS remembers the server; if another one answers under the same name later, the backup stops.
backup.removeHint: TitanOS forgets this job and its password; the backups at the target stay where they are.
backup.removeText: TitanOS forgets this job and its password. What was backed up already stays where it is and can still be read with restic and the password – write it down first if you still need the data.
backup.restoreFailed: The last restore failed (the backup itself is not affected):
backup.restoreLoading: Reading the states that are there …
backup.restoreNone: There is no state yet that something could be restored from.
backup.restoreStarted: The restore is running. The files end up here:
backup.restoreText: The chosen state is copied into a new folder. What lies in your shares now is not touched – you take from there what you need.
backup.restoreWhere: You find the folder under Files › Volumes. The progress shows on this page.
backup.secretAgain: Server or account changed: the stored secret is not used for it. Please enter it again.
backup.smb.credentialsHint: The password is stored in the protected system configuration and is never shown again. The write test creates and removes a temporary file. Destination folders are created as needed.
backup.smb.first: If no destination is available, close this dialog and configure an SMB destination above first. Files are stored under the job folder, share name and full relative source path.
backup.smb.intro: Optional Beta feature for directly readable folder copies. Connect the destination first, then create a job with the source folders you want.
backup.smb.keepPassword: Leave blank to keep the stored password
backup.smb.name: Destination name
backup.smb.noShares: No suitable shares found. Check the SMB user on the second NAS.
backup.smb.removeHint: Only the connection is removed. Previously copied files remain. Remove or change jobs that use this destination first.
backup.smb.save: Test write access and save destination
backup.smb.setup: First create a user and a writable SMB share on the second TitanOS/NAS. Enter its address and credentials here and discover shares. SMB3 encryption is required.
backup.smb.title: Second NAS as SMB backup destination
backup.targetCodeOnce: The code holds the access and is not shown again. If it is lost, remove the NAS here and pair it again.
backup.targetCodeText: Paste this code into a backup job on the sending NAS under “Another TitanOS”.
backup.targetDeleteData: Also delete the stored backups of this NAS

backup.targetDesc: This NAS can store the backups of other TitanOS. It is reached over Tailscale only, not in the home network and not on the internet.
