backup.targetPairHint: The name only appears here and names the folder. The code is shown once.
backup.targetProblem.tailscale: Tailscale is not connected. Set it up under Plugins; without it this NAS accepts nothing.
backup.targetProblem.volume: The chosen volume is not mounted.
backup.targetRemoveText: The NAS can send nothing afterwards. Its stored backups stay unless you delete them on purpose.
backup.vm.choiceNeeded: Nothing is chosen for this job yet. Until then disks of running VMs are read as they are – such a copy may not start.
backup.vm.count.many: {count} VM disks in the sources of this job
backup.vm.count.one: 1 VM disk in the sources of this job
backup.vm.intro: The disk of a running VM changes while it is copied. So that the copy can still be started, TitanOS freezes a state for the time of the copy. You decide whether that should happen.
backup.vm.libvirt: Use the snapshot of the VM management
backup.vm.libvirt.desc: For qcow2 disks on volumes without Btrfs: the VM keeps running, changes go to an overlay during the copy and are merged back afterwards. The method is new and tested only to a limited extent. Tested on a test VM: snapshot, copy, merging back, abort and restart in between. Not tested: a VM that writes a lot meanwhile, freezing with the guest agent, several or large disks. Switched off, the choice “Disks without snapshot” applies to these disks.
backup.vm.loadFailed: The VM disks in the sources could not be determined right now.
backup.vm.raw.desc: Raw images and disks no snapshot is used for. Applies to the whole job and to all disks of such a VM. “Skip and report”: the disks are not read in this run, the earlier copy at the destination stays, the result names them. “Pause briefly”: the VM stands still for the time of the copy (15 minutes at most).
backup.vm.reason.vm_disk_backing_chain: the image has snapshots of its own
backup.vm.reason.vm_disk_busy: another operation of the VM is running
backup.vm.reason.vm_disk_no_space: not enough space next to the disk ({need} needed, {free} free)
backup.vm.reason.vm_disk_passthrough: the VM has a whole disk of the NAS
backup.vm.reason.vm_disk_snapshot_failed: the VM management refuses a snapshot
backup.vm.reason.vm_disk_snapshot_unprov: the snapshot of the VM management is not switched on
backup.vm.skipNote: Choice “Skip”: disks of running VMs are not read in this job. The earlier copy at the destination stays, the result names the skipped disks.
backup.vm.title: Running VMs
backup.vm.way.copy: VM is off · copied like any file
backup.vm.way.libvirt_snapshot: Snapshot of the VM management · without guest agent
backup.vm.way.libvirt_snapshot.agent: Snapshot of the VM management · frozen cleanly
backup.warning: The backup was made, but not everything could be read:

backup.windowHint: A backup that is due outside the window waits until the window opens. The window may pass midnight. A running backup is not cut short when the window ends.

bell.storageErrors: The bell always shows errors on volumes and disks, so that a risk of data loss is never missed.

cluster.alertHint: Also reports “reachable again”. Short restarts for app updates do not count. Only nodes that manage report.
cluster.backupWayHint: Backups between the nodes. With “Only …” they wait while that way is missing instead of taking another.
cluster.clockHint: Warns when the clock of a node is off by more than a minute. From two minutes, nodes can no longer sign in to each other.
cluster.createHint: This NAS becomes the first node. Afterwards this page shows the join information for the others.
cluster.extraHint: One per line, e.g. a DDNS name, an address in a VPN of your own or name:port of a port forwarding. Can be chosen as the way “Own address”.
cluster.fallback: – {way} not reachable, checks regularly whether it works again
cluster.fallbackStays: – {way} not reachable, stays on this way
cluster.handOverConfirm: {name} becomes the admin node: it then hands out the accounts and admits new nodes. This NAS may still manage.
cluster.internet: Reach nodes over the internet as well
cluster.internetHint: Also allows public addresses. Port 443 must then be reachable from the internet.
cluster.internetWarn: Port 443 of this NAS then has to be reachable from the internet (router, firewall). TitanOS opens nothing itself. The connection stays encrypted and bound to the certificate of the node.
cluster.intro: Join several TitanOS into a cluster, as in Proxmox: the admin node manages all others and its accounts apply on every node. Other nodes may manage too only when the admin node allows it. No failover: each node keeps working on its own while the others are away.
cluster.joinConfirm: This NAS becomes a member: the admin node (and nodes it allows) can then fully control it; this NAS itself controls no other node. The accounts of the cluster replace those of the same name here; the own accounts of this NAS stay here only.
cluster.joinHint: The join information is on the cluster page of the admin node (or of a node allowed to manage). Paste and check it here; before joining, TitanOS shows what changes for the accounts.
cluster.joinInfoHides: Hidden again after five minutes and when you leave the page.
cluster.joinInfoHint: Paste it on the NAS that is to join, under Settings › Cluster. Whoever has it can join the cluster – do not pass it on.
cluster.leaveConfirm: This NAS leaves the cluster. Another node makes a new key for the rest. Accounts and data stay here.
cluster.leaveHint: This NAS then works on its own again. The accounts stay as they are now.
cluster.local.confirm: The account {name} becomes an account of the cluster and is handed out to every node. Where a node already has an account of this name, it is replaced by this one (password, role, two-factor sign-in). This cannot be undone.
cluster.local.hint: Only this NAS had these accounts when it took over managing the cluster. They are valid here only and are not handed out.
cluster.local.title: Accounts on this NAS only
cluster.manageWayHint: Applies to all nodes. Per node differently under “⋯ › Way to this node”.
cluster.memberHint: This NAS is a member: the admin node manages it, the other nodes cannot be managed from here. Accounts of this NAS do not go to the cluster.
cluster.name: Name of the cluster
cluster.newKeyConfirm: The join information of before stops working. Nodes in the cluster stay.
cluster.noticesDeleteText: {count} messages are deleted on {name}, for all sessions and all administrators.
cluster.noticesNone: No warnings or errors from the last 24 hours left.
cluster.noticesShow: Show the messages of the last 24 hours
cluster.onlyOff: Off – if the way fails, titand takes the next one
cluster.onlyOn: On – if the way fails, the node is not reachable
cluster.ownerOnly: Only an owner can do this.
cluster.pairHint: The node creates the source itself; the data goes through the cluster, on any way that reaches it.
cluster.previewLocal: These accounts exist on this NAS only; they stay here and do not go to the cluster: {names}
cluster.previewReplaced: The cluster has these accounts already; they are replaced by those of the cluster (password, two-factor, role): {names}
cluster.previewTaken: These accounts come from the cluster to this NAS: {names}
cluster.probeChecked: Checked {time}. All ways are encrypted and bound to the node's certificate.
cluster.probing: Asking every node on every way …
cluster.removeConfirm: Remove {name} from the cluster? The key of the cluster and the join information are made anew; {name} can no longer reach the others. Its accounts and data stay on it. A node that is not reachable right now has to join again afterwards.
cluster.restarting: The node is restarting and will be back shortly. TitanOS keeps trying by itself.
cluster.returnWayHint: While a node is reached on a fallback way, titand switches back as soon as the preferred way answers again.
cluster.runningParallel: Updating the nodes all at once …
cluster.runningSerial: Updating the nodes one after the other …
cluster.tailscaleNameHint: The Tailscale name is passed on as well and outlives a new IP.
cluster.takeOverConfirm: The admin node {name} does not answer. This NAS takes its role. If {name} comes back, it becomes a node that may manage.
cluster.title: Cluster
cluster.trust: The admin node manages all nodes; others only with its permission. Every node proves itself with its own certificate. Network and firewall changes are confirmed on the node itself only.
cluster.tunnelHint: TitanOS builds a WireGuard tunnel between the nodes itself, a key per node. For nodes at other places, port {port}/UDP must be forwarded on the router.
cluster.updateAllHint: Each node checks the signature itself and falls back after a failed start as usual.
cluster.updateParallelHint: Faster; meanwhile all chosen nodes are briefly not reachable. This NAS still last.
cluster.updateSerialHint: The next one only when the previous one answers with the new version. Stops at an error. This NAS last.
cluster.versionMismatch: The node speaks another cluster protocol (version {version}). Update it under Settings › Updates.
cluster.versions: {name} runs {version}, this NAS {own}. Everything can be managed; what only a newer version has, the page itself says.
cluster.versionsLimited: {name} runs {version}, this NAS {own}. The versions speak different cluster protocols: only updates, logs and restarting work.
cluster.wayAuto: Automatic (home network, then VPN, then internet)

digest.enabled: Send once a day as a summary instead of every message on its own
digest.hint: Applies to all ways below and to notifications on devices; the bell still shows everything at once. Messages are collected in memory: a restart of the NAS before the time loses them.
dnsProvider.dyndns2Placeholders: Without placeholders TitanOS sends hostname and myip (dyndns2). With placeholders as routers use them: <domain>, <ipaddr>, <ip6addr>, <username>, <passwd>, e.g. https://dyndns.strato.com/nic/update?hostname=<domain>&myip=<ipaddr>,<ip6addr>.
dnsProvider.help.cloudflare: API token under My Profile › API Tokens with the permissions Zone › Zone › Read and Zone › DNS › Edit.
dnsProvider.help.desec: Token under Token Management at desec.io; also for dedyn.io names.
dnsProvider.help.duckdns: Token from duckdns.org. DuckDNS keeps one TXT record per name; name and wildcard are checked one after the other.
dnsProvider.help.dyndns2: Update address of the service with user and password, as routers use it too.
dnsProvider.help.hetzner: API token of a project in the Hetzner Console (Security › API tokens, read and write). The old DNS console (dns.hetzner.com) is not supported.
dnsProvider.help.inwx: User name and password of INWX. Accounts with two-factor sign-in do not work; best use a sub-account just for DNS.
dnsProvider.help.ionos: API key from developer.hosting.ionos.de in the form prefix.secret.
dnsProvider.help.ipv64: IPv64.net: DynDNS names like nas.ipv64.de or own domains. Access with API key or domain update token.
dnsProvider.help.netcup: Customer number, API key and API password from the Customer Control Panel (Master data › API). Changes take a few minutes at Netcup.
dnsProvider.help.rfc2136: Dynamic updates to the primary name server (BIND, Knot, PowerDNS) with a TSIG key allowed to update the zone.
dnsProvider.ipv64KeysAddress: The API key of the account (Account › API) can do everything: addresses over the API without daily limit, domains, records and reachability. The domain update token may only change the addresses of that domain (least privilege); then the daily limit of the plan applies (usually 48 updates), of which TitanOS uses at most half. Either one is enough.
dnsProvider.ipv64KeysChallenge: The DNS challenge needs the API key of the account (Account › API); the domain update token is not enough.
dnsProvider.missing: Sign-in details for the provider are missing.
dnsProvider.secretsNotMoved: Stored credentials only hold for the same provider and account; please enter them again here.
dnsProvider.title: DNS provider
energy.diskSleepHint: When idle HDDs go to sleep is set in one place: as the default, per volume or per disk. The same setting is also on the storage page.

energy.platformHint: The manufacturer’s profile may adjust performance, cooling and energy use together.
energy.powerButtonDesc: What a short press of the button does

fileIndex.clearThumbsText: All stored thumbnails on {volume} are deleted and made again when viewed. Files stay unchanged.

fileIndex.truncated: More than two million entries: not everything was covered, nothing was removed.

files.chooseRoot: No data volume available. Choose a location from the list.
files.compareCopyHint: Select individual files. Subfolder paths are preserved and missing destination folders are created. File/folder conflicts are excluded. Changes since the comparison stop the job.
files.compareHint: Without checksums, comparison uses size and modification time. SHA-256 reads equal-sized files completely. No files are changed.
files.conflictHelp: These names already exist at the target. Folders are merged; for files the chosen rule applies.
files.conflictHint.individual: Choose for each existing name: skip, replace or keep under a new name.
files.conflictHint.missing: Files with the same size and modification time (±2 seconds) are left alone, changed ones replaced, missing ones copied. Folders are merged.
files.conflictHint.rename: Existing files stay; the new one gets “(2)” in its name. Folders are merged.
files.conflictHint.replace: Existing files are replaced by the new ones. Where a file meets a folder, it is left out and reported.
files.conflictHint.skip: Existing files stay unchanged. When moving, the source of skipped files stays where it is.
files.conflictTruncated: More than 200 conflicts; the first 200 are listed. Replace, Rename and Skip apply to all of them; choosing one by one works up to 200.

files.formatFatTooLarge: FAT32 only goes up to 2.2 TB. Choose exFAT or NTFS.

files.formatFsHint.btrfs: For Linux, with checksums for all data. At least 269 MB.
files.formatFsHint.exfat: For sticks, memory cards and external disks used on different computers. No file size limit.
files.formatFsHint.ext4: For disks used only with Linux or the NAS. Windows and macOS do not read it without extra software.
files.formatFsHint.ntfs: For external disks on Windows computers. macOS only reads NTFS.
files.formatFsHint.vfat: Read by almost every device: TVs, car radios, cameras, consoles, printers. A file can be at most 4.2 GB.
files.formatFsHint.xfs: For large disks on Linux. Cannot be shrunk later. At least 315 MB.
files.formatIntro: All connected disks, sticks and memory cards that are not part of a NAS volume appear here, new and empty ones too. Formatting gives the whole disk a new partition table with one partition; whatever was on it is gone afterwards.
files.formatLabelChars: The name contains characters the filesystem does not allow.
files.formatLabelFat: A FAT32 name may only contain A–Z, digits, spaces and !#$%&'()-@^_`{}~, no accented letters.
files.formatLabelLong: The name is too long: at most {n} characters.
files.formatMbrTooLarge: MBR only goes up to 2.2 TB. Choose GPT.
files.formatNone: No drive found. Disks of volumes, the TitanOS stick and empty card readers do not appear here.

files.openWith.mountUndo: Remove it again under Docker › {app} › Edit › Shares.
files.openWith.notMounted: {share} is not mounted in it yet
files.openWith.outside: The file is in no folder of the app.
files.openWith.title: Open with
files.operationPartial: File job finished with errors – check the list
files.partitions.action.label: Rename
files.partitions.deleteConfirm: Partition {part} ({size}, {fs}) on {disk} ({device}) is deleted. All data on it are lost; the other partitions stay as they are.
files.partitions.empty: No partitions and no free space.
files.partitions.extendedHint: This MBR table has logical partitions. Creating, deleting and growing are not possible here; formatting and renaming are.
files.partitions.failed: Failed. Check the partitions before going on.
files.partitions.formatConfirm: Partition {part} ({size}) on {disk} ({device}) is formatted with {fs}. All data on it are deleted; the other partitions stay as they are.
files.partitions.gone: The drive is gone or was changed. Go back to the drives.
files.partitions.growHint: The partition grows into the free space right after it, then the filesystem. Shrinking is not possible. XFS and Btrfs are mounted briefly for this; an NTFS that was not shut down cleanly (Windows fast startup) is left unchanged.
files.partitions.growNoSpace: There is no free space right after the partition.
files.partitions.growSize: The new size must be larger than now and fit into the free space.
files.partitions.intro: Partitions of a disk that belongs to no volume. Changes run in the background; right before writing, TitanOS checks the disk again. Mounted partitions are left alone – eject them first.
files.partitions.label: Rename …
files.partitions.labelHint: Only changes the name of the filesystem; the data stay.
files.partitions.mbrFull: An MBR table holds at most four partitions.
files.partitions.rest: Use all of the free space
files.partitions.sizeHint: Rounded down slightly so that start and end line up cleanly on the disk.
files.partitions.sizeInvalid: Please enter a size of at least 2 MB.
files.partitions.sizeTooLarge: There is not that much free space there.
files.partitions.tableConfirm: {disk} ({size}, {device}) gets a new, empty {scheme} partition table. All partitions and all data on the disk are deleted. This cannot be undone.
files.partitions.tableHint: GPT fits every disk. MBR goes up to 2.2 TB and four partitions, but older devices read it too.
files.partitions.tableNone: No partition table. Create a new partition table first.
files.partitions.tableUnknown: The partition table is unknown or cannot be read. Only a new partition table is possible.
files.partitions.title: Partitions: {name}
files.pathCopyFailed: Could not copy the path. Select and copy it from the input field.
files.pdfFallback: This browser cannot display the PDF here. You can download it.
files.photoEmpty: This folder has no pictures or videos.
files.photoLimited: Only the first 5,000 pictures and videos are shown.
files.preferencesLoadFailed: File manager settings could not be loaded.
files.preferencesSaveFailed: Changes have not been saved to your account. Please retry.
files.previewFailed: Preview unavailable. The file is inaccessible, too large, damaged or unsupported by this browser.
files.previousConfirm: I want to replace the current file with this previous version.
files.previousHint: The previous version is on the left, the current saved file on the right. Restoring makes the current version the previous one. Save or discard unsaved changes first.
files.previousMissing: No previous version is available for this file yet.
files.problemSummary: Not transferred: {failed} · left at the source: {kept}
files.queueHint: Copies and moves run in order per account, higher priority first. Pause takes effect after the current block. 0 MB/s means unlimited. Jobs targeting data volumes save checkpoints; other jobs remain in RAM. Removing a job only removes its record, never files.
files.quickKeys: Space closes, the arrow keys go to the previous and next file.
files.quickNone: There is no preview for this file.
files.quickOfficeNone: This document carries no preview picture. “Open” shows it in its program.
files.quickOfficePage: Preview picture stored in the document
files.rebootedHint: The NAS was restarted since this job. It cannot be retried; a new job copies only what is missing or changed at the target.
files.renameBatchHint: The preview follows selection order. Changes affect the name before the extension; letter case is preserved.
files.renamePartial: {count} items were renamed. An intervening change or filesystem error stopped the operation. Completed changes are listed under Undo.
files.replaceFinal: There is no recycle bin here: replaced files are gone for good.
files.replaceToBin: Replaced files go to the share’s recycle bin and can be restored from there.
files.requestedRootUnavailable: The requested location is unavailable or not accessible.
files.restoreCreated: Destination folder created: {path}. If starting the copy fails, this folder remains.
files.restoreHelp: Files are copied into a new, separate folder. The USB backup is preserved. An existing destination folder will not be used.
files.restoreInvalid: Enter a new folder name without slashes; the names “.” and “..” are not allowed.
files.retryHint: Files already finished are kept; source files changed or added meanwhile are transferred as well. Retrying is possible until the NAS restarts.
files.reviewConflicts: {count} names already exist at the target. Please check the list below, then click the button again.
files.rightReason.protected: This path is managed by a virtual machine and protected against changes.
files.rightReason.readOnly: This location does not allow changes by your account.
files.rightReason.share: Your account has read-only access to this share. Writing, renaming and deleting are blocked. An owner or administrator can change the share permissions.
files.rightReason.stick: The system stick is protected. Only supported text files can be edited; deleting, renaming and uploading remain blocked.
files.rightReason.usb: Changes are blocked by USB backup protection. Explicitly unlock the drive to modify files.
files.rightsHint: These are the TitanOS permissions for your signed-in account. Unix permissions are listed separately above. Filesystem errors, a read-only drive or subsequent permission changes can also prevent an action.
files.scopeDeferred: Calculating the size is taking longer. When you start, the full size will be calculated and checked against free space before any files are copied.
files.searchContentHint: Finds words in PDF, Word, Excel, OpenDocument, PowerPoint and text files using the full-text index. New or changed files appear after the next index pass.
files.searchContentOff: The full-text index is off for this location (Settings › File search).
files.searchLimited: The result or scan limit was reached. Narrow the folder or filters.
files.sha256Invalid: A SHA-256 checksum has 64 hexadecimal characters.
files.shortcutsHint: Arrow keys, Enter and Space apply to the active file list. Text fields and media controls retain their normal keys. Other actions are available in the left pane.
files.stickNote: The stick is for looking only. Accounts, certificates, keys and passwords are hidden. Text files can be edited.
files.summaryHint: Size and free space may change. Conflicts and write permissions are checked again when starting.
files.summaryNested: A folder cannot be transferred into itself or one of its subfolders.
files.summarySameCopy: Source and target are the same folder. Copying here only works with “keep both” (new name).
files.summarySameMove: Source and destination are the same folder. Choose another destination to move.
files.summarySpaceWarning: Selected contents exceed the reported free space. Moves within the same filesystem may avoid an additional copy.
files.targetUnavailable: This destination is protected or not writable.
files.thumbnailHint: The NAS makes thumbnails of pictures, PDFs and videos; they load when they become visible.
files.title: Files
files.transferProblem.blocked: This address or a redirect to it is not allowed.
files.transferProblem.changed: The source or destination changed during the operation.
files.transferProblem.connection: The connection was interrupted or timed out.
files.transferProblem.hash: The SHA-256 checksum does not match. The downloaded data was discarded.
files.transferProblem.http: The server did not deliver the file.
files.transferProblem.missing: A file or folder is no longer available.
files.transferProblem.other: The job could not be completed. Files already transferred are retained.
files.transferProblem.permission: Access is no longer permitted or the destination is read-only.
files.transferProblem.space: The destination does not have enough free space.
files.trashAllocated: Allocated file data blocks: {size} (hard links counted once)
files.trashChoose: Recycle bins of the shares on this volume
files.trashChooseHint: Files deleted or replaced in {name} are in the recycle bin of the share their folder belongs to.
files.trashDisabled: The recycle bin is disabled for this share. It can be enabled in the share settings.
files.trashEmptyAccount: Empties the whole recycle bin of the account {account} in {share}, not just the open folder.
files.trashEmptyAll: Empties the recycle bins of all {count} accounts in {share} completely, not just the open folder.
files.trashHint: This is what you deleted in this share, in the file manager or over the network. After {days} days TitanOS deletes it for good. Restoring puts it back where it was; if something with the same name is there now, the time is added to its name.
files.trashHintAdmin: This is what was deleted in this share, by account. After {days} days TitanOS deletes it for good. Restoring puts it back where it was; if something with the same name is there now, the time is added to its name.
files.trashRestoreConflict: Name already exists – restore with a timestamp in the name.
files.trashRestoreHint: The selection will be restored to these original locations.
files.trashSizeHint: Sum of file contents in the accessible account scope, excluding directory metadata. Actual reclaimed space may differ. Older entries may use the modification date.
files.trashSizeSummary: File size in the recycle bin: {total} · Filtered: {shown} in {count} files
files.undoHint: Available for up to 30 minutes and until the NAS service restarts. Changed files or occupied original names prevent undo. Replacing, merging and permanent deletion cannot be undone.
files.undoKind.trash: {count} items moved to the recycle bin
files.unlockBackupHelp: This also allows deleting, moving, editing and uploading on this backup drive. Access stays unlocked until you change storage locations or leave this page.
files.unreadableFolders: {count} source folders cannot be read. They are skipped and reported in the job:
files.uploadChecking: Checking destination, free space and name conflicts …
files.uploadDuplicate: The upload contains this path more than once
files.uploadNoSpace: There is not enough free space for this selection.
files.uploadReplaceConfirm: I confirm replacing the selected existing files.
files.urlConflict: “{name}” already exists in this folder. Nothing is overwritten: change the name or keep both (the new file gets a number).
files.urlDownloadHint: TitanOS downloads the file straight into this folder, even if you close the page. It only appears once it is complete and, if given, verified; existing files are never overwritten.
files.urlDownloadPublicOnly: Your account only reaches internet addresses, not the home network.
files.urlInvalid: Enter a complete http or https link without credentials.
files.urlNameExists: A file with this name already exists in this folder.
files.urlTooLarge: The file is larger than the free space ({free}).
files.usbBackupMissing: The backup folder does not exist yet. Check whether the first backup completed successfully.
files.windowsCopyHint: For long folder trees: enter the local source folder and run the generated command in PowerShell. Robocopy copies all contents including subfolders. Changed destination files may be overwritten; extra destination files are retained.
files.windowsLimits: This does not shorten subfolders within your source. Robocopy supports long paths; individual filename limits still apply. TitanOS does not change names or share permissions.
files.windowsLoadFailed: Could not load shares. Please open this dialog again.
files.windowsMapHint: Choose an unused drive letter. Copy the command into PowerShell on your Windows PC. The drive points directly to this folder, shortening the visible destination path. Windows uses your SMB login.
files.windowsSource: Full source folder on your Windows PC
files.windowsUnavailable: Open an existing SMB share folder. USB devices, the system stick and names containing invalid Windows characters cannot be mapped here.
firewall.addPolicyHint: Pick a source zone and a destination above first.
firewall.always: Always allowed: existing connections, loopback, DHCP answers, ICMP errors (path MTU), IPv6 neighbour and router discovery. While a change is on trial, your own address as well.
firewall.appsText: Published ports of Docker apps. Docker forwards them; the firewall checks them by their port on the NAS.
firewall.autoBlockSources: Counted are failed logins at the web UI, over SSH (unknown accounts, refused keys, networks not allowed) and over SMB (wrong password, unknown account). NFS has no login. What happens while titand is not running is not counted.
firewall.autoBlockText: Whoever fails to log in too often cannot reach the NAS at all for the chosen time, not even other services. This works with the firewall off, too. IPv6 senders are blocked with their whole /64 network.
firewall.bypassText: Docker apps with an address of their own in the LAN (macvlan/ipvlan) and VMs and LXC containers on LAN bridges bypass the NAS. They can only be caught as senders by their addresses (source networks of an own zone).
firewall.cellText: Policies are checked in order; the first that matches decides. If none matches, the default applies.
firewall.confirmed: The new rules now apply for good.
firewall.dockerError: Docker networks could not be opened to each other (DOCKER-USER): {detail}
firewall.dockerText: all Docker bridge networks (docker0, br-…) not in an own zone, new ones too
firewall.exempt: Never block (addresses or networks, one per line)
firewall.exemptLocal: Never block the home network and the VPN
firewall.groupEmptyVm: None. TitanOS VMs use the user-mode network or a LAN bridge; NAT bridges (virbr…, lxcbr…) show up here if there are any.
firewall.hostNetworkHint: Apps in the host network ({apps}) publish no ports; their ports are the NAS's own. Allow them with port policies in the cell to the NAS.
firewall.internetText: all other addresses, including public IPv6 addresses outside the own network
firewall.intro: When on, the firewall lets a new connection in only if the cell of the sender's zone and the destination allows it. Established connections, loopback, DHCP and the ICMP IPv4/IPv6 need are always allowed. When off, everything stays open as before.
firewall.loadError: The rules could not be loaded: {detail}
firewall.matrixText: Rows: where a new connection comes from. Columns: where it goes – to the NAS itself, to published ports of Docker apps or, from networks behind the NAS, into another zone. Click a cell to see its policies.
firewall.networksNoZones: To assign a network differently, first create an own zone under “Zones”.
firewall.networksText: All networks TitanOS knows on the NAS, and their zone. New Docker networks land in the default zone Docker by themselves; networks that disappear stay noted in their zone.
firewall.noRecent: Nothing was dropped since titand started.
firewall.notThroughNasText: Grey: traffic between home network, VPN, internet and own zones without networks behind the NAS does not pass the NAS (it is no router) and cannot be filtered here. Only Docker networks and VM/LXC NAT networks go to other zones.
firewall.permanent: Block permanently, until the block is lifted by hand
firewall.policiesText: All policies of all cells. Within a cell the order counts; the first that matches decides.
firewall.policyDestination: Enter an IPv4 or IPv6 address or a network like 192.168.1.0/24 as destination.
firewall.recentText: The last 200 dropped packets, in memory only and at most five per second and zone. Broadcasts and multicasts of other devices are dropped quietly. For Docker apps this shows the port inside the container.
firewall.releaseText: {address} can reach the NAS again afterwards. Further failed attempts are counted anew.
firewall.ruleComment: The note may have at most 80 characters and no quotes.
firewall.rulePorts: A port is a number from 1 to 65535, a range two of them with a dash (8000-8100).
firewall.ruleSource: Enter an IPv4 or IPv6 address or a network such as 192.168.1.0/24.
firewall.svcText.apps: Same port as the web UI; TitanOS tells them apart by name
firewall.svcText.nfs: NFSv4 and NFSv3 with fixed helper ports
firewall.svcText.ping: Echo requests over IPv4 and IPv6
firewall.svcText.ssh: Only matters while SSH is on
firewall.svcText.ups: For devices that watch the UPS through this NAS
firewall.svcText.vpn: Tailscale and NetBird; direct connections from the internet, checked by the VPN itself
firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.trial: The new rules are on trial: {time} left
firewall.trialHint: Check that you reach everything you need, then confirm. Without confirmation the previous rules come back after two minutes. Your own address stays allowed until then.
firewall.unsaved: Unsaved changes. The firewall stays off; the settings apply once it is switched on.
firewall.unsavedTrial: Unsaved changes. Applying loads the new rules on trial for two minutes.
firewall.you: You are connected from {address} (zone: {zone}). TitanOS refuses rules that would lock you out of the web UI.
firewall.zoneName: The name needs 1 to 40 characters without quotes.
firewall.zoneOrder: Own zones are checked before Docker, VPN and home network, in the order of this list.
firewall.zoneRemoveHint: Removes the zone and its policies; its networks return to their default zone.
firewall.zoneRemoveText: The zone “{name}” and its policies are removed; its networks go back to their default zone. This takes effect once applied.
firewall.zoneSources: Source networks (addresses or networks, one per line)
firewall.zoneSourcesHint: Senders from these networks belong to the zone, whichever interface they come in on. Networks of the NAS are matched by their interface and subnet.
firewall.zoneText.docker: Docker networks without an own zone
firewall.zonesHint: The home network is the private ranges (RFC 1918, fc00::/7, link-local) and the networks of the NAS's own interfaces, including the home network's public IPv6 prefix. VPN is Tailscale, NetBird, the WireGuard server of the NAS (titanoswg) and the IPv64 tunnel (ipv64wg).
ha.accountIntro: Buttons and switches in Home Assistant act as this account, with its rights; every press is logged. Without an account, TitanOS creates no buttons.
ha.allDevices: All devices, including newly discovered devices
ha.command.agent: Start tasks of the AI agent (one button per task)
ha.command.power: Restart and shut down the NAS
ha.commandGroups: Buttons and switches in Home Assistant
ha.commandsNoAccount: Choose an account above; without one TitanOS creates no buttons.
ha.commandsWarning: Anyone allowed to write to your MQTT broker can press these buttons. Protect the broker with users and access rules. TitanOS refuses to restart or shut down while copies, backups, disk tests or a volume rebuild are running.
ha.conn.addHint: Then enter the address and token of the new connection below. Every connection has its own releases, storage and MQTT.
ha.conn.hint: The sections below belong to the chosen connection (✓).
ha.conn.name: Name
ha.conn.removeText: “{name}” is removed from TitanOS with its settings and storage entries. What was entered in Home Assistant stays there; accounts and shares on the NAS stay as well.
ha.conn.title: Connections
ha.evicted: Transitions evicted from the bounded event buffer
ha.fingerprintHint: Only needed when Home Assistant uses HTTPS with a self-signed certificate. Then exactly this certificate is accepted, no other.
ha.gaps: Outages are not replayed. Buffer eviction does not necessarily mean an automation missed an event.
ha.group.cameras: Cameras (NVR: online, person, vehicle, animal, license plate, known face)
ha.intro: Connects TitanOS to your Home Assistant: storage for backups and media, sensors and buttons over MQTT, released devices for AI clients through the MCP server, and notifications to your phone through the Home Assistant app.
ha.mqttConnected: Connected to the broker; values are sent every {seconds} seconds.
ha.mqttIntervalHint: How often TitanOS sends the values, 5 to 3600 seconds. Empty = 30.
ha.mqttIntro: TitanOS reports its values to Home Assistant through MQTT; they appear there as the device “TitanOS” by themselves. Home Assistant needs no access to the NAS for this. You need an MQTT broker, for example the Mosquitto add-on of Home Assistant, and the MQTT integration.
ha.releaseIntro: AI clients on the MCP server only see and switch what is released here: whole domains such as all lights, or single devices. Locks, covers, alarm panels and similar devices count as dangerous: they need dangerous calls allowed on the MCP page and a confirmation in the client.
ha.services: Allowed services (commas; empty: inherit existing permission)
ha.title: Home Assistant
ha.tokenHint: Create one in Home Assistant under Profile › Security › “Long-lived access tokens”. The token stays on the NAS and is never shown again. TitanOS only connects to exactly this address and does not follow redirects.
hardware.alsoIn: Also assigned: {vms}. Only one of them can run at a time.
hardware.autoGPU: Automatically switch NVIDIA between this VM and containers
hardware.autoGPUHint: Starting the VM stops containers using its NVIDIA GPU. Once the VM exits and the driver has reclaimed the GPU, TitanOS restarts exactly those containers. Without this option, running GPU containers block VM startup.
hardware.containerHint: Select an Intel/AMD GPU, NPU or NVIDIA GPU. Selections persist across restarts; devices used by a running VM are blocked. The app needs compatible libraries inside its container.
hardware.coralUSBWarning: Gives the app access to the whole USB device bus; use only with trusted apps. The app must include an Edge TPU runtime.
hardware.duplicate: Several of the same are plugged in. The VM gets one of them.
hardware.how: For a graphics card assigned to several VMs: only one of them runs at a time.
hardware.intro: Devices for VMs and NVIDIA power limits. Devices assigned to a VM belong to it while it runs and return to the NAS afterwards. Select container devices when installing an app or editing a Compose service.
hardware.noIommu: This machine does not isolate devices (no IOMMU). Switch Intel VT-d or AMD-Vi on in the BIOS/UEFI; without it cards cannot be passed through to VMs. USB devices still work.
hardware.nonePci: No graphics card or accelerator found.
hardware.reason.no_iommu: Needs IOMMU (Intel VT-d or AMD-Vi), which is not active on this machine.
hardware.reason.npu: NPUs are not passed through to VMs; they are available to containers.
hardware.reason.shared_group: Shares its IOMMU group with other devices and cannot be separated on its own.
hardware.stick: TitanOS runs from this stick. It goes to no VM.
hardware.title: Hardware
hardware.warnIgpu: Passing integrated graphics through is often unreliable with current Intel CPUs.
hardware.warnPrimary: This is the display of the NAS itself: while the VM runs, the screen at the NAS stays dark.
hastore.accountMissing: The account {account} no longer exists. The next “Set up storage” or “Enter in Home Assistant again” makes it anew with a new password and gives it back its access to the shares above.
hastore.backupNone: No backup of Home Assistant on the NAS yet.
hastore.backupUnknown: Home Assistant did not give the list of backups (2025.1 and later). So there is no notice.
hastore.existingHint: The account for Home Assistant gets access to this share; everyone keeps their rights. Home Assistant sees only the folder chosen.
hastore.intro: Shares of this NAS (or folders in them) that Home Assistant OS mounts as network storage: for backups, for media or as a share for add-ons. All use one account of their own; TitanOS enters them in Home Assistant right away if you like.
hastore.maxAge: Notify when no new backup arrived for
hastore.maxAgeHint: TitanOS asks Home Assistant once a day; the disks of the NAS are not woken for it.
hastore.noSupervisor: This installation of Home Assistant has no Supervisor. Network storage needs Home Assistant OS or Supervised.
hastore.noVolume: No volume is mounted. Create one under Storage first.
hastore.passwordOnce: The password is shown only now. TitanOS does not keep it; “Enter in Home Assistant again” gives a new one.
hastore.passwordSame: The password of the account stays as it is. “Enter in Home Assistant again” gives a new one and enters everything with it.
hastore.readOnly: Read only (Home Assistant cannot change anything there)
hastore.register: Enter it in Home Assistant right away
hastore.registerAgainText: The account {account} gets a new password, and TitanOS enters all entries in Home Assistant with it; existing ones are updated.
hastore.registerHint: Through the connection above. This needs Home Assistant OS or Supervised and a token of an administrator.
hastore.registerHintMore: The account gets a new password for it; TitanOS updates all other entries in Home Assistant with it too.
hastore.registerOff: Without Home Assistant connected TitanOS shows the values to enter by hand.
hastore.removeHAFailed: The entry could not be removed from Home Assistant: {error}
hastore.removeText: {place} is removed from Home Assistant, and the account {account} loses access to it unless another entry uses the share. Share and data stay. Should nobody have access then, you get it.
hastore.title: Storage for Home Assistant
hastore.usageHint.backup: Home Assistant puts its backups here; TitanOS keeps an eye on new ones arriving.
hastore.usageHint.media: Music, photos and videos for the media browser and speakers.
hastore.usageHint.share: A folder for add-ons, such as camera recordings.
hastore.valuesHowTo: In Home Assistant, enter these values under Settings › System › Storage › Add network storage:
hastore.valuesKept: For backups, choose the storage in Home Assistant under Settings › System › Backups as a location. The values for reference:
help.bitmap.text: A small list inside the RAID of the areas currently being written. If a disk drops out only briefly (cable, restart), the NAS resyncs just those areas when it returns instead of the whole disk. It costs a little write speed.
help.bitmap.title: Write-intent bitmap
help.bridge.text: A virtual network switch inside the NAS (br0). It connects VMs, LXC and Docker containers to the network port so they get their own addresses on the home network, like separate devices.
help.bridge.title: Bridge
help.cache.text: An SSD in front of the hard disks makes frequent access faster. As a read cache it is safe; as a write cache it holds data for a while that exists only there.
help.cache.title: SSD cache
help.cdi.text: A standard through which Docker hands a device to a container. TitanOS describes the NVIDIA card this way; the container gets exactly that card with its driver files and needs no driver of its own.
help.cdi.title: CDI (Container Device Interface)
help.checks.text: Disks often lose data unnoticed where nobody reads for a long time. The checks read everything calmly, so errors show up and get repaired while a second copy is still there.
help.checks.title: Regular checks
help.cron.text: Five fields: minute, hour, day of the month, month, weekday (0 or 7 = Sunday). * means every value, */15 every 15, 1-5 a range, 1,15 a list, L in the day the last day of the month. Example: “30 2 * * 1-5” runs on weekdays at 2:30.
help.cron.title: Cron expression
help.filesystem.text: Decides how files are stored on the disks. ext4 is proven and robust, XFS strong with large files. Btrfs checks every file with checksums, has snapshots and uses disks flexibly.
help.filesystem.title: File system
help.level.text: How many disks may fail without losing data: RAID 1 and 5 one, RAID 6 two, RAID 10 one per pair, RAID 0 none.
help.level.title: RAID level
help.luks.text: The disks hold only encrypted data. Whoever removes or steals a disk cannot read anything. After every start someone has to enter the password; without it the data is lost.
help.luks.title: Encryption (LUKS2)
help.mcp.text: The Model Context Protocol is an open standard through which AI programs such as Claude use tools. TitanOS offers its functions as such tools; the AI acts only with the rights of the token you give it.
help.mcp.title: MCP
help.psi.text: How much time programs had to wait because memory was short (some: some waited, full: all waited). 0 % is good; values above a few percent slow the NAS down noticeably.
help.psi.title: Waiting for memory
help.raid.text: Several disks work as one. RAID 1 mirrors everything, RAID 5 survives one failed disk, RAID 6 two, RAID 10 mirrors pairs, RAID 0 has no protection. RAID is no backup: deleting, malware or fire hit all disks at once.
help.raid.title: RAID
help.scopes.text: Decide what a token may do, for example only read or also change files. Without the scope the NAS refuses the call, and a token can never do more than your account. Give a program only the scopes it needs.
help.scopes.title: Token scopes
help.scriptTrigger.text: By button, the script runs only when you start it. On a schedule it runs at fixed times, at start once after the volume is mounted, and at shutdown before the apps are ended. Failed automatic runs show up as notifications.
help.scriptTrigger.title: Trigger
help.scriptsVolume.text: The scripts and their log live on this data volume in the folder .titanos/scripts, not on the stick. Choosing another volume moves nothing: the scripts stay on the old volume and come back when you choose it again.
help.scriptsVolume.title: Volume of the scripts
help.shebang.text: If the script starts with #! and a program (such as #!/bin/bash or #!/usr/bin/python3), it runs with that, otherwise with bash. It runs as root in its own folder; output and error messages appear together in the output.
help.shebang.title: First line
help.slot.text: The stick has two places for TitanOS, A and B. An update goes into the other place; if it does not start, the NAS takes the old one again by itself.
help.slot.title: System slot
help.smart.text: The self-monitoring of a disk: it counts reallocated sectors, read errors, temperature and wear. Rising values often announce a failure weeks ahead.
help.smart.title: SMART
help.snapshot.text: A frozen state of the volume at one moment. It takes hardly any space while little changes, and single files can be restored from it. A snapshot lives on the same disks and is no backup.
help.snapshot.title: Snapshots
help.sysext.text: How a plugin becomes part of the system: its image lies on a data volume and is laid over /usr when activated, without changing the base system. Removing it takes it out completely again.
help.sysext.title: sysext (system extension)
help.vlan.text: Splits one wired network into several separate networks. Every packet carries a number, the VLAN ID (1 to 4094). This only works if the router or managed switch knows the same VLANs.
help.vlan.title: VLAN
hwcheck.exportFailed: The report could not be saved.
hwcheck.exportNote: The report contains no serial numbers and no MAC addresses. Read it anyway before you pass it on.
hwcheck.exportSnapshotHint: Device data, kernel log and driver list as an archive, for a hardware bug report. Without serial numbers, MAC and IP addresses.
hwcheck.finding.hw_raid: {subject}: hardware RAID controller – IT or HBA mode recommended.
hwcheck.finding.intel_raid_mode: {subject}: SATA is in RAID mode – AHCI recommended.
hwcheck.finding.no_iommu: The IOMMU is off – devices cannot be handed to VMs.
hwcheck.finding.no_virtualization: Hardware virtualization is off or missing – VMs do not start.
hwcheck.finding.old_cpu: The processor does not meet x86-64-v2 – many current apps do not run on it.
hwcheck.finding.smr: {subject}: SMR disk – not recommended for RAID 5/6.
hwcheck.finding.uas_quirk: {subject}: USB enclosure with known UAS problems.
hwcheck.finding.unbound_driver_failed: {subject}: the driver is present but did not take the device.
hwcheck.finding.unbound_kernel: {subject}: no driver, only a newer kernel supports the device.
hwcheck.finding.unbound_plugin: {subject}: no driver loaded, a plugin fits.
hwcheck.firmwareIntro: Drivers asked for these firmware files at start and did not find them. The device then often works only partly or not at all. Please report it with the diagnostic bundle so the file gets into the image.
hwcheck.hint.driverVmd: Intel VMD (RST): TitanOS does not see NVMe SSDs behind this controller. If no Intel RAID is needed, switch VMD off in the BIOS/UEFI; back up first if an Intel RAID is on it.
hwcheck.hint.driver_failed: The driver {driver} is present but did not take the device. What the kernel says about it is shown below.
hwcheck.hint.hw_raid: Hardware RAID controller. TitanOS builds the RAID itself (mdadm or Btrfs) and needs the disks directly: switch the controller to IT or HBA mode in its BIOS or firmware. Back up first – switching can make existing controller arrays unreadable.
hwcheck.hint.intel_raid_mode: The SATA controller is in RAID mode (Intel RST). Switch to AHCI in the BIOS/UEFI; back up first if an Intel RAID is on it.
hwcheck.hint.kernel: Supported only from kernel {version} on (driver {driver}). It runs with the optional newer kernel (6.16 or newer).
hwcheck.hint.newKernelFixes: The kernel “New” of the newest version ({kernel}) has it; choose it under Settings › Updates.
hwcheck.hint.newKernelLacks: Neither “Stable” nor “New” ({kernel}) has it yet; it only comes with a newer kernel.
hwcheck.hint.not_needed: System part, usually needs no driver of its own.
hwcheck.hint.pluginInstalled: The plugin {plugin} is installed but has not taken the device. Is it switched on? After switching it on, a restart sometimes helps.
hwcheck.hint.sas_standby: SAS disk: disk sleep sends it to standby with SCSI power condition 3; it wakes up by itself on the next access.
hwcheck.hint.smr: SMR disk ({how}). In RAID 5/6, rebuilds and checks take very long and the disk may drop out of the array. Better use CMR disks for RAID 5/6.
hwcheck.hint.uas_quirk: This USB enclosure has known problems with UAS (drop-outs under load). Remedy: set the kernel parameter {setting}. It then uses the slower but more stable usb-storage driver. TitanOS only sets it when you click “Apply remedy” below.
hwcheck.hint.uas_quirk_active: USB enclosure with known UAS problems; it already runs via usb-storage.
hwcheck.hint.unclassified: Unclassified Intel chipset function. The kernel reports no error for it; such a function usually needs no driver.
hwcheck.hint.unsupported: Not supported: neither the kernel nor a known plugin knows this device.
hwcheck.intro: Sums up processor, memory, disk controllers, disks, network, graphics, sensors and driver status in one report. The check only reads: it changes no disk and does not wake sleeping disks.
hwcheck.iommu.off.amd: The IOMMU is off. To hand PCI devices to VMs, switch on “AMD-Vi” or “IOMMU” in the BIOS/UEFI.
hwcheck.iommu.off.intel: The IOMMU is off. To hand PCI devices to VMs, switch on “Intel VT-d” in the BIOS/UEFI.
hwcheck.iommu.off.other: The IOMMU is off. To hand PCI devices to VMs, switch it on in the BIOS/UEFI.
hwcheck.iommu.ok: The IOMMU is active: graphics cards and other PCI devices can be handed to VMs.
hwcheck.iommu.table.amd: The BIOS/UEFI offers an IOMMU, but the kernel does not use it. Remedy: set the kernel parameter amd_iommu=on. TitanOS never sets boot parameters itself.
hwcheck.iommu.table.intel: The BIOS/UEFI offers an IOMMU, but the kernel does not use it. Remedy: set the kernel parameter intel_iommu=on. TitanOS never sets boot parameters itself.
hwcheck.title: Check hardware
hwcheck.uas.pendingOff: Remedy taken out, takes effect after the next restart.
hwcheck.uas.pendingOn: Remedy written, takes effect after the next restart.
hwcheck.unboundHidden: Show {count} system parts without a driver of their own
hwcheck.unboundIntro: No driver has taken these PCI and USB devices. Many system parts need no driver of their own; network, storage and graphics cards matter most.
hwcheck.virt.byFirmware: The kernel reports: switched off in the BIOS/UEFI.
hwcheck.virt.off.amd: AMD-V is off or missing, VMs do not start. Switch it on in the BIOS/UEFI, usually under “Advanced › CPU Configuration › SVM Mode”, then save and restart.
hwcheck.virt.off.intel: Intel VT-x is off or missing, VMs do not start. Switch it on in the BIOS/UEFI, usually under “Advanced › CPU Configuration › Intel Virtualization Technology”, then save and restart.
hwcheck.virt.off.other: The processor offers no hardware virtualization, VMs do not start. If it can: switch it on in the BIOS/UEFI.
hwcheck.virt.ok: VT-x/AMD-V is active, VMs run at full speed.
hwcheck.virt.title: Virtualization
idleLock.hint: After how many minutes without use your login locks and asks for the password. “never”: no lock. Applies to your account; how long a login lasts at all is set by “Stay logged in”.
idleLock.title: Lock when idle
intelGuc.afterRestart: The setting is in the boot entries and takes effect after the next restart.
intelGuc.confirmText: From the next restart the GuC schedules the work on the Intel GPU (i915.enable_guc=3). This is not the kernel default on this generation and can make graphics and transcoding unstable. You can go back here at any time, with another restart.
intelGuc.deferred: The running system slot is still on trial. Its boot entry follows once the start is confirmed; then the setting takes effect after a restart.
intelGuc.gucWarn: GuC submission is not the kernel default on these generations and Intel does not recommend it there. Graphics and transcoding may become unstable. If it does not help, go back to “Load HuC”.
intelGuc.gucWarnGen9: Gen9/Gen9.5 has no GuC submission: the kernel reports “Incompatible option enable_guc=3” and only loads the HuC. Intel and the kernel do not recommend GuC submission on these generations; choose “Load HuC”.
intelGuc.intro: On Intel graphics from Skylake (6th generation) to Tiger/Rocket Lake the kernel does not load the HuC firmware by itself. Without HuC, apps such as Jellyfin or Plex lack low-power (VDEnc) encoding with bitrate control. The setting puts the kernel parameter i915.enable_guc into the boot entries on the stick; it is kept across updates and rollbacks and takes effect after the next restart.
intelGuc.manual: The command line holds i915.enable_guc={value} without it being set here. TitanOS only changes that once you save here.
intelGuc.missingFirmware: The HuC firmware for this GPU is missing from the system. Without it the setting has no effect.
intelGuc.mode.auto.hint: No parameter. On these generations GuC and HuC stay off. Recommended unless something is missing.
intelGuc.mode.guc.hint: i915.enable_guc=3: in addition the GuC schedules the work on the GPU. For testing only.
intelGuc.mode.huc.hint: i915.enable_guc=2: the GuC loads and authenticates the HuC firmware; the driver keeps scheduling the work. This is what the Jellyfin documentation recommends for low-power encoding.
intelGuc.newer: From Alder Lake on the kernel loads GuC and HuC itself; the setting does not apply to this GPU.
intelGuc.notI915: The setting only works while the i915 driver has the GPU (not while it is in a VM).
intelGuc.notWritable: The boot entries cannot be changed here (development mode or not started from the stick).
intelGuc.source.none: none (debugfs not readable, no kernel messages)
intelGuc.title: Intel graphics: GuC/HuC
intelGuc.xe: xe driver: the kernel always loads GuC and HuC itself here; nothing to set.
ipv64.autoPauseHint: Shutting down through TitanOS (menu, schedule, updates) pauses the healthcheck so that no alarm comes; after the start it carries on. A shutdown by the UPS counts as a failure and does not pause.
ipv64.autoPauseLabel: Pause before planned shutdowns and restarts
ipv64.createText: {name} is created in the account at IPv64 and entered here as a name. It counts against the domains of your plan.
ipv64.forAppsText: {domain} becomes the own domain under Settings › HTTPS names for apps. Apps are then reachable as <app>.{domain} once the wildcard is on. A domain already set there is replaced.
ipv64.forAppsTitle: Domain for the HTTPS names of apps
ipv64.heartbeatHint: Optional: TitanOS checks in with a healthcheck of IPv64 regularly. If the check-ins stop (NAS off, internet gone), IPv64 notifies through the channels chosen there. Off by default; nothing is created at IPv64 before.
ipv64.intro: Account, domains, DNS records and reachability at IPv64. Every call counts against the limits of the account; that is why TitanOS loads only on a click.
ipv64.needsKey: This needs the API key of the account (enter it above; it is stored only with “Save”).
ipv64.noDomains: The account has no domain yet.
ipv64.offText: TitanOS no longer checks in with {check}. Should the healthcheck at IPv64 be paused or deleted? If it stays active, IPv64 will soon report the NAS as unreachable.
ipv64.onText: TitanOS creates a push healthcheck at IPv64 (or takes an existing one) and checks in there regularly.
ipv64.pausedForShutdown: TitanOS paused the healthcheck before the shutdown; it is resumed after the start.
ipv64.periodHint: IPv64 usually allows 72 check-ins a day, hence at least 20 minutes. Alarm after interval plus grace without a check-in.
ipv64.proxyDone: {domain} is now the domain of the app HTTPS names.
ipv64.testSent: Test message sent (at most one every 30 seconds).
ipv64.title: IPv64.net
ipv64.wildcardHint: Wildcard points *.name at the same addresses, so that the HTTPS names of apps (<app>.name) resolve.
keep.lastHint.backups: When a new backup is done, the oldest is deleted.
keep.lastHint.snapshots: When a new snapshot is done, the oldest is deleted.
keep.rolling.drive: Keep until the drive is full
keep.rolling.replica: Keep until space runs short on the other NAS
keep.rolling.share: Keep until the share is full
keep.rolling.storage: Keep until the storage is full
keep.rolling.volume: Keep until the volume is full
keep.rollingHint.backups: Every backup stays. Only when space runs out is the oldest deleted.
keep.rollingHint.replica: Every state stays. When less than 10 % of the volume on the other NAS is free, the oldest go before the next run; the newest always stays.
keep.rollingHint.snapshots: Every snapshot stays. Only when space runs out is the oldest deleted.
lang.label: Language
letsencrypt.apps: Also cover the HTTPS names of apps
letsencrypt.appsHint: Adds {wildcard}; the certificate then holds for all app names under this domain.
letsencrypt.appsNoDomain: This needs an own domain under
letsencrypt.challengeDnsHint: TitanOS briefly creates a TXT record at the DNS provider. No open port needed, wildcard certificates possible.
letsencrypt.challengeHttpHint: Port 80 must be forwarded from the internet to the NAS (router, firewall). No wildcards, no names for apps.
letsencrypt.devMode: Development mode: settings are saved, but no certificate is fetched.
letsencrypt.directoryHint: Address of the ACME directory, e.g. an own step-ca in the home network. Empty is Let's Encrypt.
letsencrypt.emailHint: Given to the account at the certificate authority. Let's Encrypt no longer sends expiry mails; TitanOS tells you itself.
letsencrypt.enable: Use a certificate from Let's Encrypt
letsencrypt.enableHint: Switched off, the own or self-signed certificate is used again.
letsencrypt.expiring: The certificate expires in {days} days and has not been renewed yet.
letsencrypt.firewallHttp: The firewall is on: port 80 belongs to the web UI and is allowed from the home network and VPN only. Let's Encrypt checks the HTTP challenge from the internet, so it fails.
letsencrypt.firewallHttpWays: Choose the DNS challenge (no open ports needed) or add the policy “Allow, TCP, port 80” without a sender to the cell “Internet → NAS” under Firewall › Policies. The web UI then answers plain HTTP from the internet too (it redirects to HTTPS). TitanOS never opens port 80 by itself.
letsencrypt.intro: TitanOS fetches a certificate that browsers trust without an exception and renews it by itself about 30 days before it runs out. It is used for the names entered; by IP address or .local the previous certificate stays.
letsencrypt.lastError: The last attempt failed ({count} in a row). Until one succeeds, the previous certificate is used.
letsencrypt.namesHint: Names that point at this NAS in public DNS or whose DNS you manage, e.g. nas.example.org. Wildcards like *.example.org only with the DNS challenge.
letsencrypt.namesInvalidHttp: Not usable (wildcards need the DNS challenge): {names}
letsencrypt.noCert: No certificate yet. Until there is one, the previous one is used.
letsencrypt.noHttpPort: titand does not listen on port 80 (option -http). The HTTP challenge cannot succeed like this.
letsencrypt.phase.propagation: Waiting until the name servers know the records
letsencrypt.propagationHint: Some providers take minutes until all name servers know the record (Netcup up to ten). Empty keeps the default.
letsencrypt.stagingCert: This certificate comes from the staging environment and is not trusted by browsers.
letsencrypt.stagingHint: For trying out: generous limits, but browsers do not trust these certificates.
letsencrypt.title: Let's Encrypt
lock.activity.unlockBlocked: Unlock slowed down (too many failed attempts)
lock.error.invalid_code: The code is wrong or was used already.
lock.error.passkey_expired: The request expired. Please try again.
lock.error.rate_limited: Too many failed attempts. Please try again in {seconds} seconds.
lock.error.second_factor_required: Please also enter the code from your authenticator app.
lock.error.unreachable: The NAS cannot be reached right now.
lock.lockedHint: This session is locked. Enter the password to unlock it.
lock.setting.label: Lock automatically
lock.title: Locked
loginLook.contrastWarning: Text on the login card only has a contrast of about {ratio} on this background – at least 4.5:1 reads well. Darken more, use less transparency or pick “Flat”.
loginLook.enter.curtain: Curtain – the login slides away upwards
loginLook.enter.split: Split – the login opens to the sides
loginLook.enter.zoom: Zoom – the desktop comes from the depth
loginLook.glassHint: Transparency is limited so that text stays readable. Anyone who asked their system for less transparency sees a solid card.
loginLook.imageHint: JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 5.2 MB. The NAS saves the image anew (without metadata such as location or camera) and shows it without login – do not use anything private.
loginLook.imageRemoved: The saved own image is removed when saving.
loginLook.imageTooLarge: The image is larger than 5.2 MB.
loginLook.intro: Applies to the whole NAS, not only to your account: everyone sees this login page, also before logging in. Only owners and administrators can change it. Without settings of its own it shows the desktop wallpaper with clock and a glass card.
loginLook.movingHint: Northern lights and Mountain lake move (aurora, water, clouds). With “reduce motion” in the system the picture stays still.
loginLook.positionHint: On phones the card is always in the center.
loginLook.previewBadge: Preview – logging in has no effect here
loginLook.previewForbidden: Only owners and administrators can open the preview of the login page.
loginLook.showHost: Show the name of the NAS
loginLook.showStatus: Show the state of the NAS (“titan is ready”)
loginLook.showStatusHint: At the bottom right of the login page: ready or still starting. Off by default.
loginLook.textsHint: Plain text, one line. If a text is missing in one language, the other language's text appears. An empty heading stays “Log in”.
loginLook.themeInheritHint: As before: the appearance last used in this browser, otherwise Graphite. Accent and glass can only be picked with a fixed theme.
loginLook.title: Login page
loginPick.eachHint: Which accounts the login page shows. New accounts show until you switch them off here.
loginPick.externalHint: By default, over the internet, a tunnel or a proxy only the accounts of the own device appear – strangers see no account names.
loginPick.note: Locked accounts never appear. Logging in still needs the password.
loginPick.showAllHint: Off: only accounts that have logged in on this browser
loginPick.styleHint: How the accounts appear to pick
loginPick.title: Accounts on the login page
look.autosave: Changes apply at once and are saved.
look.cornersHint: Rounding of windows, cards and buttons
look.densityHint: Compact shows more rows at once
look.detailsHint: Spacing, edges, glow and motion. Like everything here it applies at once.
look.dimHint: How much the page behind a dialog is darkened
look.dock.appsHint: Change the order by dragging or with the arrows.
look.dock.intro: The dock at the edge of the desktop. Every change applies at once.
look.dock.link: Show, position, size and kept programs
look.dock.rightClickHint: On the desktop too: right-click a free spot of the dock to open “Edit dock”.
look.dock.title: Dock
look.fileHint: Save the theme as a file or take it over from another NAS
look.glassHint: How much windows, menus and bars let through
look.intro: Applies to your account everywhere: desktop, all windows and phone. Every change shows at once.
look.languageHint: Language of the interface for this account.
look.liquidHint: How opaque bars, dock, widgets and menus are: “See-through” lets more of the background through, “Opaque” covers it. Content stays readable.
look.liquidSample: This is how opaque the surfaces look
look.motionHint: Bars and rings glide to new values
look.saturationHint: Saturation of the accent colour and the wallpaper
look.shineHint: Bright top edge of glass surfaces
look.wallpaperHint: Picture behind the desktop; also on the login page unless it has a picture of its own
lxc.creatingText: The container is being created: {phase}. This can take a few minutes; the page may be closed.
lxc.delete.data: Delete the data as well (root filesystem and snapshots)
lxc.delete.dataWarning: The root filesystem of “{name}” is deleted for good. NAS folders that were mounted in the container are not touched.
lxc.delete.text: “{name}” is removed from TitanOS. Without the checkbox its folder {path} stays.
lxc.delete.title: Remove container
lxc.dev: Development mode: containers are shown, but not created, started or changed.
lxc.emptyText: Create the first one: an image of images.linuxcontainers.org, stored on a volume.
lxc.failedHint: Creating the container failed. Remove it (with its data) and create it again.
lxc.form.autostart: Start automatically after the NAS has started
lxc.form.badMac: This is not a valid unicast MAC address.
lxc.form.badTarget: Every folder needs a folder on a volume and a place of its own in the container: an absolute path without spaces, not /proc, /sys, /dev, /run or a system folder itself.
lxc.form.imageSource: Images of images.linuxcontainers.org. Image, volume and kind are fixed once created; the root filesystem lies in /mnt/<volume>/lxc.
lxc.form.imagesError: The list of images of images.linuxcontainers.org could not be loaded.
lxc.form.mountHint: Unprivileged containers write to shares through their group “users” (GID 100); other accounts in the container see the files as “nobody”.
lxc.form.name: Name
lxc.form.privilegedWarning: Privileged: root in the container is root of the NAS. Only for software that really needs it; cannot be changed once created.
lxc.form.restartHint: Changes apply from the next start of the container.
lxc.intro: Whole Linux systems that share the kernel of the NAS – lighter than a VM, closer to a server than a Docker app.
lxc.jobCode.delete_failed: The data of the container were not deleted completely. It can no longer be started; remove it again.
lxc.jobCode.interrupted: Creating did not finish because TitanOS stopped meanwhile. Remove the container and create it again.
lxc.jobCode.timeout: Stopped: downloading and unpacking the image did not finish within 30 minutes. Remove the container and try again.
lxc.killText: “{name}” is ended right away, without shutting down. Whatever is not saved inside the container is lost.
lxc.notInstalled: LXC is not part of this system image. Containers are available after the next full system update.
lxc.removeHint: Removes the container from TitanOS; its data can be deleted as well in the dialog. A running container has to be stopped first.
lxc.snap.notBtrfs: Snapshots are available for containers on Btrfs volumes.
lxc.snap.restoreText: The root filesystem of “{name}” is set back to the state of {time}. The current state is lost.
lxc.snap.stoppedOnly: Restoring only works while the container is stopped.
lxc.snap.title: Snapshots
lxc.title: LXC
mail.all.failed: Not reachable, missing in the list: {names}
mail.attachment.title: Attachments
mail.bar.moveOne: Moving works within one mailbox only
mail.box.hint: Drag mailboxes and folders by the grip. The top mailbox is your main one: new mails are sent from it. A folder without a tick is hidden; the star makes it a favourite.
mail.box.title: Mailboxes
mail.bulk.deleteText: The messages are in the trash. They are deleted for good at the provider and cannot be brought back.
mail.bulk.label: Actions for the selection
mail.compose.discardDraft: What you wrote is lost, and the saved draft goes to the trash.
mail.compose.draftAuto: The draft is saved every 30 seconds while you write.
mail.compose.invalidHint: At least one address is not valid. Remove it or type it again.
mail.compose.noAccount: Choose the mailbox you write from.
mail.compose.subject: Subject
mail.compose.title: New e-mail
mail.compose.tooLarge: The attachments add up to {size}; at most {max} are allowed.
mail.delete.forever: It is deleted for good at the provider and cannot be brought back.
mail.delete.text: The message “{subject}” is in the trash.
mail.delete.title: Delete for good?
mail.disabled.text: An owner or administrator enables Mail for your account under Users › Account › Apps.
mail.disabled.title: Mail is not enabled for your account
mail.drop.other: Only into folders of the same mailbox
mail.empty.text: Set up a mailbox with its address and password. Only your account sees it.
mail.empty.title: No mailbox yet
mail.fav.title: Favourites
mail.filter.label: Show
mail.hint.app_password: {name}: create an app password for Mail in your account at the provider and enter it here.
mail.hint.app_password_2fa: {name}: with two-step sign-in you need an app password, which you create in your account at the provider.
mail.hint.imap_enable: {name}: allow access through IMAP/POP3 in your mailbox settings at the provider.
mail.hint.mail_password: {name}: use the separate password for e-mail programs, not that of your customer account.
mail.hint.oauth_only: {name} requires signing in with the provider (OAuth), which Mail cannot do yet.
mail.images.blocked: External images blocked – they would tell the sender that and when you open the message.
mail.keys.global: The other keys of TitanOS, such as Ctrl+K, still work here.
mail.keys.note: The keys do nothing while you type in a field.
mail.keys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
mail.limit.wait: Too many attempts with new servers or connection checks – Mail waits another {seconds} s; “Check connection” works again after that.
mail.link.someWarn: Careful: a link leads somewhere other than its text says
mail.link.title: Link targets in this message ({count})
mail.link.warn: The text names another address – the link leads to {host}
mail.list.heading: {folder} · {account}
mail.live.down: No live connection to the NAS – new e-mail shows up again once it is back. Mail reconnects by itself.
mail.move.title: Move to …
mail.noneOpen: No message open. Choose one on the left.
mail.overview.hint: Choose a message in the list to read it here.
mail.overview.live: New mail in the inbox arrives by itself.
mail.overview.poll: The list reloads every 2 minutes while Mail is open.
mail.overview.title: Overview
mail.quick.label: Quick actions
mail.rawText: This mail is too large in structure to be prepared (for example a digest with a great many posts). Mail shows the beginning of its content as it came – without formatting and without attachments.
mail.resize.hint: Drag or use the arrow keys to change the width; a double click resets it.
mail.rule.removeText: The rule “{rule}” is deleted once you save.
mail.rule.subject: Subject contains
mail.scope.label: Search in
mail.search.attachmentHint: Finds mail with attached files. A mail that is a file and nothing else is not found.
mail.search.fromHint: Name or address of the sender
mail.search.label: Search this folder
mail.search.needCriteria: Type a search or choose a filter to search all folders.
mail.search.truncated: Not every folder was searched. Narrow the search, for example with a period.
mail.settings.authFailed: The login at the provider failed. Mail tries again only after you change the password, user name or server.
mail.settings.notifyDesc: Bell and push for new e-mail in the inbox, per mailbox.
mail.settings.passwordAgain: Server or user name changed: enter the password again. A stored password never goes to another server.
mail.settings.passwordHint: Leave empty to keep the stored password.
mail.settings.passwordKeep: leave empty: stays as it is
mail.settings.pushContent: Sender and subject in push messages
mail.settings.pushContentDesc: Off: push messages only say “New e-mail in <mailbox>”. The bell never names sender or subject.
mail.settings.removeHint: Removes the mailbox from Mail. Nothing changes at the provider.
mail.settings.removeKeeps: Your e-mail stays at the provider; you can set the mailbox up again at any time.
mail.settings.removeText: Mail forgets “{name}” with its servers, password and the rules for this mailbox.
mail.settings.rulesDesc: Run on the NAS for new e-mail in the inbox, in order.
mail.settings.rulesNew: Rules apply only to e-mail that newly arrives, not to existing mail.
mail.settings.signaturesDesc: Text below your e-mails. Which one a mailbox uses by default is set at the mailbox.
mail.settings.threadsDesc: Replies show as one entry with their count in the list. Applies to this device.
mail.settings.title: Settings
mail.setup.appPassword: This provider wants an app password: a password only for Mail that you create in your account settings at the provider. Your normal password does not work here.
mail.setup.badAddress: That is not a complete e-mail address.
mail.setup.intro: Mail connects through IMAP and SMTP, always encrypted (TLS). The password is kept encrypted on the NAS and never shown on a page again.
mail.setup.known: {name} is known; the servers are already filled in.
mail.setup.name: Name of the mailbox
mail.setup.nameHint: What Mail calls the mailbox, e.g. “Personal”. Empty: the address.
mail.setup.senderNameHint: Shown to recipients before your address, e.g. “Alex Example”. Empty: the address alone.
mail.setup.title: Set up mailbox
mail.setup.tlsOnly: Encrypted connections only; the server's certificate must be valid.
mail.setup.unknown: Mail knows no servers for {domain}. Enter them as your provider names them.
mail.setup.unsupported: {name} no longer accepts a password, only signing in with the provider (OAuth). Mail cannot do that in this version.
mail.signature.name: Name
mail.signature.removeText: The signature “{name}” is deleted once you save.
mail.truncated: The message is very large: parts are shortened or left out. The attachments are above.
mcp.bridgeHint: titanosctl reads the token from a private file (chmod 600) and relays stdio to the address above.
mcp.enabled: Switch on the MCP server for this NAS
mcp.pageIntro: AI clients such as Claude work with the NAS through the Model Context Protocol – with exactly the rights of their token and account.
mcp.placeholder: Replace <TOKEN> with your token. With a self-signed certificate set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS to the certificate file for mcp-remote, or pass --ca-file to titanosctl.
mcp.title: MCP for AI clients
mcp.tokenHint: A token needs the permission “AI clients via MCP”. Its other permissions decide which tools the client gets; write permissions are off by default.
mcp.tool.account_action: Change the role of an account or delete it
mcp.tool.backup_schedule: Change the schedule of a backup
mcp.tool.backup_status: Backup jobs with their last run
mcp.tool.disk_test: Start a disk test (write test erases)
mcp.tool.document_edit: Change an Excel or Word document
mcp.tool.document_read: Read PDF pages, also with OCR
mcp.tool.file_copy: Copy or move files (in the background)
mcp.tool.file_read: Read text, Word, Excel or PDF
mcp.tool.files_read_text: Read a text file with its version
mcp.tool.nas_info: Name and version of the NAS
mcp.tool.plugin_switch: Switch a plugin on or off
mcp.tool.power_action: Restart or shut down the NAS
mcp.tool.update_action: Check, install or roll back an update
mcp.tool.vm_action: Start, stop or remove a VM
mcp.tool.volume_action: Start/stop a check, delete a volume
mcp.toolsIntro: A tool is off, on (reading and normal changes) or on including dangerous calls (such as deleting or restarting). Dangerous calls also need a confirmation in the client. Which tools a token sees also depends on its scopes.
mcp.withToken: With this token for Claude Code:
memoryPolicy.hint: The budget follows available RAM after a system reserve. Browser uploads are saved and released from cache in sections; adjusted kernel thresholds trigger earlier SMB/NFS writeback. This is not a fixed percentage limit for read cache, VM memory or the system image.
memoryPolicy.intro: Linux uses free RAM as read cache and releases it on its own when needed – that cannot be configured and is not a problem. Here you set how much not-yet-written data (write cache) file transfers may keep in RAM before it has to reach the disk. Default: 20% of available RAM after the system reserve.
memoryPolicy.lowAvailable: Available RAM has been low for at least 30 seconds. Check running apps and VMs.
memoryPolicy.percent: Write buffer budget for file transfers
memoryPolicy.pressure: Time stalled on memory (some / all tasks)
memoryPolicy.pressureHint: PSI shows the share of the last ten seconds during which at least one task or all active tasks had to wait for memory. A large file cache alone does not mean a memory shortage.
memoryPolicy.title: Write cache
netbird.acceptDNS: Use the DNS settings of the NetBird network
netbird.acceptRoutes: Accept routes from other NetBird peers
netbird.activateHint: Enable the plugin to set up NetBird.
netbird.firewallHint: NetBird manages its own nftables tables for the wt0 interface, UDP port 51820 and forwarding; its access rules apply regardless of the general firewall opening. Next to Tailscale, wt0 is accepted before Tailscale's rules because both use the 100.64.0.0/10 range. NetBird SSH, remote jobs and self-updates are off.
netbird.keyHint: The key is only used to register with the management server, stored on the stick and never shown again. An empty field keeps the stored key.
netbird.keyNeeded: For its first login the NAS needs a setup key from the NetBird dashboard.
netbird.logout: Remove NAS from the NetBird network
netbird.logoutHint: The NAS deregisters from the management server and is deleted there as a peer. Remote access through NetBird ends; a new registration needs a setup key again.
netbird.managementHint: Leave empty for NetBird Cloud. For a self-hosted server enter its address with port, e.g. https://netbird.example.org:443. Another server needs a setup key from there.
