netbird.policyHint: Networks, exit nodes and who may access what are set in the NetBird dashboard. Access to the local network always stays available.
netbird.serveRoutes: Allow this NAS as routing peer or exit node
netbird.trial: Please check access and confirm by {time}. Without confirmation the previous settings are restored.
netcfg.bond.802.3ad: LACP (802.3ad) – needs a matching setting on the switch
netcfg.bond.active-backup: Failover – one port works, the other takes over
netcfg.bond.balance-alb: Load balancing – without a setting on the switch
netcfg.hostnameHint: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. The NAS shows up in the network under this name.
netcfg.lost: The NAS does not answer here right now – it probably has another address now. Open the web UI at the new address, log in and confirm the change there. Without confirmation the NAS is reachable at the previous address again after 2 minutes.
netcfg.notApplied: The stored network configuration could not be applied at start; the NAS runs on the basic setup (DHCP on all ports). Adjust the configuration here and test it.
netcfg.pending: New network setting on trial. Without confirmation it goes back to the previous one in {seconds} s.
netcfg.title: Network
netcfg.trial: The change is on trial at first. Unless you confirm it within 2 minutes, the NAS goes back to the present setting by itself. If the address changes, open the web UI at the new address, log in and confirm there.
netx.addressHint: DHCP comes from the external network. Static addresses and Docker pools must be outside its DHCP range. Only the preferred management network automatically accepts default routes and DNS.
netx.bondInUse: Used by {names}. Choose another connection there first.
netx.bondNameHint: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphen, at most 10 characters. Cannot be changed later.
netx.bondRemoveConfirm: Remove bond “{name}” from the draft? Its ports become free again.
netx.bondTwoPorts: A bond needs at least two ports.
netx.bridge: Provide a bridge for VMs and containers
netx.clash: “{name}” already uses this connection and VLAN ID.
netx.confirmHint: Open the new management address and confirm there. Without confirmation the previous configuration is restored.
netx.diagnosticsDraft: Only applied networks are checked. Check a draft after “Validate and test”, during the trial, over the new connection.
netx.diagnosticsPending: No diagnostics while a change is on trial. Confirm or revert it first.
netx.discardText: The changes to the draft will be lost.
netx.dnsHint: IPv64 and Cloudflare DNS update names and addresses. A DNS record creates neither a tunnel nor a port forward.
netx.dnsNote.management: Empty: name servers from the DHCP server or router. Separate several with spaces, commas or semicolons; at most three.
netx.dnsNote.other: Separate several with spaces, commas or semicolons; at most three. Only the preferred network takes name servers automatically.
netx.external: Router and DHCP remain external; the NAS firewall is under Settings › Firewall. Existing Docker and Tailscale rules are preserved.
netx.intro: Named networks for management, storage and applications.
netx.migrated: This setting comes from the former single-network view and keeps working unchanged. It is stored as a named network only once you test and confirm a change.
netx.name: Name
netx.needsAddress: The preferred management network needs IPv4 or IPv6.
netx.preferredHint: Exactly one network is preferred. To change it, mark another network as preferred.
netx.proxyHint: Public app URLs do not configure a tunnel. Tunnels and reverse proxies remain managed in their respective application.
netx.remoteUnknown: The plugin state could not be read.
netx.removeConfirm: Remove “{name}” from the draft? Applying checks whether containers or VMs still use it.
netx.removeManagement: The preferred management network cannot be removed. Mark another network as preferred first.
netx.routesHint: Routes need a gateway inside the network of a static address of this network.
netx.switchHint: LACP needs matching switch configuration. VLANs also need to be configured on the external switch and router.
netx.unsaved: Network changes have not been applied
netx.vlans.confirmLocal: If this is only about VMs, LXC or Docker, networks inside the NAS are enough (bridges and Docker networks as firewall zones). They need no VLANs. Every network change still runs on trial for two minutes.
netx.vlans.confirmText: VLANs only work if your router or a managed switch understands them. A simple router or switch drops tagged packets, and the NAS would not be reachable in that network.
netx.vlans.hint: Off by default. VLANs need a router or switch that understands tagged networks. While off, the network editor offers no VLAN ID.
netx.vlans.inUse: A network uses a VLAN. To switch this off, remove the VLAN IDs from the networks first.
netx.vlans.title: VLANs
notify.deleteAllText: {count} messages are deleted on the NAS – for all sessions and all administrators. Messages that arrive in the meantime are kept.
notify.discordHint: Create a webhook in the channel settings under Integrations and enter its address here.
notify.emailHint: Through the mailbox of a mail provider (SMTP). Many providers want an app password of its own for this.
notify.empty: No notifications. This is where you see when a volume or a disk needs attention.
notify.haHint: Sends messages through a notify service of Home Assistant, for example to the app on your phone. Set up the connection under Settings › Home Assistant.
notify.haNotSetUp: Home Assistant is not connected yet.
notify.intro: TitanOS tells you when a volume loses a disk, is being rebuilt or is almost full, and when a disk reports errors or gets too warm. The notifications always show in the header; here you set where else they are sent.
notify.kind.backup_check_failed.text: restic found errors in the destination of the backup {subject}. Details are under Settings › Backups.
notify.kind.backup_check_failed.title: Check of backup {subject} failed
notify.kind.backup_failed.text: The backup did not run through. Details are under Settings › Backups. Further failed attempts are not reported one by one.
notify.kind.backup_failed.title: Backup {subject} failed
notify.kind.backup_ha_overdue.text: Home Assistant has not put a backup on this share for longer than set. Check in Home Assistant under Settings › System › Backups whether the location is still chosen and reachable.
notify.kind.backup_ha_overdue.title: No new backups of Home Assistant on {subject}
notify.kind.backup_incomplete.text: Shares or places were missing because their volume is not mounted. The rest was saved; all older backups are kept until they are back.
notify.kind.backup_incomplete.title: Backup {subject} incomplete
notify.kind.backup_overdue.text: No backup has worked for at least two runs and two days. Check under Settings › Backups whether the target can be reached.
notify.kind.backup_overdue.title: Backup {subject} has not worked for a while
notify.kind.backup_probe_failed.text: The probe could not be fully verified. Details are under Settings › Backups.
notify.kind.backup_probe_failed.title: Restore probe for {subject} failed
notify.kind.backup_recovered.text: The backup ran through again after failed attempts.
notify.kind.backup_recovered.title: Backup {subject} works again
notify.kind.backup_space_freed.text: The oldest versions were removed, as set in the job.
notify.kind.backup_space_freed.title: Backup {subject}: target was full
notify.kind.certificate_expiring.text: The own certificate of the web interface is only valid until {subject}. Put a new one in place under Settings › Access.
notify.kind.certificate_expiring.title: The certificate is about to expire
notify.kind.cluster_node_joined.text: The node can now manage all nodes. If none of you did this: remove it under Settings › Cluster and create a new key.
notify.kind.cluster_node_joined.title: Node {subject} joined the cluster
notify.kind.cluster_node_removed.text: The key of the cluster was renewed.
notify.kind.cluster_node_removed.title: Node {subject} was removed from the cluster
notify.kind.config_backup_failed.text: The configuration could not be saved to the volume {subject}. Have a look at Settings › Backup of the stick.
notify.kind.config_backup_failed.title: Backup of the stick failed
notify.kind.config_backup_no_volume.text: The configuration has not been saved for more than a day because the volume for the backup is not mounted.
notify.kind.config_backup_no_volume.titl: Backup of the stick has been waiting for a day
notify.kind.ddns_failed.text: The address of {subject} could not be updated. TitanOS keeps trying.
notify.kind.ddns_failed.title: Dynamic DNS: update failed
notify.kind.disk_hot.text: The disk is warmer than 55 °C. Check the ventilation.
notify.kind.disk_hot.title: Disk {subject} is very warm
notify.kind.disk_test_failed.text: The test found errors. Do not put the disk into a volume; details are under Tools.
notify.kind.disk_test_failed.title: Disk {subject} failed the test
notify.kind.disk_test_passed.text: The test ran through without errors. The disk can go into a volume.
notify.kind.disk_test_passed.title: Disk {subject} passed the test
notify.kind.disk_test_waiting.text: A restart interrupted the test. It can be continued from its saved position under Tools.
notify.kind.disk_test_waiting.title: Test of disk {subject} is waiting
notify.kind.disk_unhealthy.text: The self-diagnosis (SMART) reports an error. Back up the data and replace the disk.
notify.kind.disk_unhealthy.title: Disk {subject} reports errors
notify.kind.disk_wear.text: The SMART values show new signs of wear or damage. Back up the data and plan a replacement. Details under Storage › SMART.
notify.kind.disk_wear.title: Disk {subject} shows wear
notify.kind.docker_auto_updated.title: App updated
notify.kind.docker_update_failed.text: The automatic update of {subject} could not be fully undone.
notify.kind.docker_update_failed.title: App update failed
notify.kind.docker_update_rolled_back.te: After the update {subject} did not run properly; the previous images run again.
notify.kind.fan_stopped.text: The fan {subject} was turning and stands now although it is driven. Check the cable and the fan, or the NAS gets too warm.
notify.kind.fan_stopped.title: Fan {subject} stopped
notify.kind.firewall_blocked.text: After several failed logins the firewall no longer lets this sender reach the NAS. The block can be lifted under Settings › Firewall.
notify.kind.firewall_blocked.title: Sender {subject} blocked
notify.kind.firewall_failed.text: TitanOS could not load the firewall rules. Details are under Settings › Firewall.
notify.kind.firewall_failed.title: Firewall rules not loaded
notify.kind.firewall_reverted.text: The new rules were not confirmed within two minutes. The previous ones apply again.
notify.kind.firewall_reverted.title: Firewall change undone
notify.kind.ha_power_refused.text: Home Assistant asked the NAS to {subject}. TitanOS refused because copies, backups, disk tests or a volume rebuild are running.
notify.kind.ha_power_refused.title: Home Assistant: power action refused
notify.kind.heat_shutdown.text: {subject} stayed at its limit for five minutes. As set in Settings › Temperatures, TitanOS shuts the NAS down in an orderly way (VMs and apps are stopped). Check the airflow and the fans before you switch it on again.
notify.kind.heat_shutdown.title: Overheating: the NAS shuts down
notify.kind.heat_shutdown_failed.text: TitanOS could not shut the NAS down: {subject}. Switch it off by hand.
notify.kind.heat_shutdown_failed.title: Overheating: shutting down failed
notify.kind.letsencrypt_expiring.text: The certificate from Let's Encrypt is only valid until {subject} and has not been renewed yet.
notify.kind.letsencrypt_expiring.title: Let's Encrypt: certificate about to expire
notify.kind.letsencrypt_failed.text: The certificate for {subject} could not be fetched or renewed. Until then the previous one is used.
notify.kind.letsencrypt_failed.title: Let's Encrypt: certificate not obtained
notify.kind.letsencrypt_renewed.text: The certificate for {subject} is new and in use.
notify.kind.letsencrypt_renewed.title: Let's Encrypt: certificate renewed
notify.kind.mail_new.title: New e-mail
notify.kind.mail_new_many.title: New e-mails
notify.kind.maintenance_failed.text: The maintenance job needs attention. Details are under Tools › Maintenance.
notify.kind.maintenance_failed.title: Maintenance {subject} failed
notify.kind.memory_corrected.text: ECC corrected errors in the memory. A few are harmless; if they pile up, a module is failing.
notify.kind.memory_corrected.title: Memory: corrected errors ({subject})
notify.kind.memory_uncorrected.text: The memory has errors ECC could not correct. Data can be corrupted: check and replace the memory module.
notify.kind.memory_uncorrected.title: Memory: uncorrectable errors ({subject})
notify.kind.nvr_camera_offline.text: The camera {subject} has sent no picture for five minutes. Nothing is recorded from it meanwhile. Check the camera's power and network.
notify.kind.nvr_camera_offline.title: Camera {subject} is not reachable
notify.kind.nvr_event_animal.text: The camera {subject} detected an animal. The event is in the NVR under Events.
notify.kind.nvr_event_animal.title: Animal at camera {subject}
notify.kind.nvr_event_face_known.text: The NVR recognised a known face ({subject}). The event is in the NVR under Events.
notify.kind.nvr_event_face_known.title: Recognised: {subject}
notify.kind.nvr_event_face_unknown.text: The camera {subject} saw a face the NVR does not know. The event is in the NVR under Events; the face can be assigned under Settings › Faces.
notify.kind.nvr_event_face_unknown.title: Unknown face at camera {subject}
notify.kind.nvr_event_person.text: The camera {subject} detected a person. The event is in the NVR under Events.
notify.kind.nvr_event_person.title: Person at camera {subject}
notify.kind.nvr_event_plate.text: The NVR read a license plate ({subject}). The event is in the NVR under Events.
notify.kind.nvr_event_plate.title: License plate read: {subject}
notify.kind.nvr_event_vehicle.text: The camera {subject} detected a vehicle. The event is in the NVR under Events.
notify.kind.nvr_event_vehicle.title: Vehicle at camera {subject}
notify.kind.nvr_failover.text: The device chosen for object detection did not work; TitanOS switched over ({subject}) and restarted the NVR. Recording goes on. The reason and “Try again” are in the NVR under Diagnosis.
notify.kind.nvr_failover.title: NVR: detection runs on another device ({subject})
notify.kind.nvr_purge_failed.text: The recordings of the removed camera {subject} could not be deleted completely. What was deleted stays deleted; you can try again under NVR › Cameras › Removed cameras.
notify.kind.nvr_purge_failed.title: NVR: recordings of {subject} not fully deleted
notify.kind.nvr_stopped.text: Object detection could not be started on any device (last: {subject}). The NVR does not record until you look under Diagnosis in the NVR and start it again.
notify.kind.nvr_stopped.title: NVR stopped
notify.kind.nvr_storage_cap.text: The recordings reached the set limit ({subject}). TitanOS deleted the oldest ones, as set in the NVR.
notify.kind.nvr_storage_cap.title: NVR: oldest recordings deleted
notify.kind.plugin_recommended.text: TitanOS found hardware the plugin {subject} is meant for. Have a look and install it under Plugins; nothing is installed on its own.
notify.kind.plugin_recommended.title: Plugin for your hardware: {subject}
notify.kind.power_postponed.text: The scheduled shutdown waits until the running work is done ({subject}); at most six hours.
notify.kind.power_postponed.title: Shutdown postponed
notify.kind.power_skipped.text: The scheduled shutdown was skipped because work has been running for six hours ({subject}).
notify.kind.power_skipped.title: Shutdown skipped
notify.kind.replication_failed.text: The Btrfs snapshot could not be sent to the other TitanOS. It is tried again in 30 minutes.
notify.kind.replication_failed.title: Replication {subject} failed
notify.kind.script_failed.text: An automatic run of the script ended with an error or was ended when its time was up. Output and log are under Tools › Scripts.
notify.kind.script_failed.title: Script {subject} failed
notify.kind.script_volume_missing.text: The volume holding the own scripts is not mounted. Scheduled scripts and scripts at start or shutdown do not run until it is back.
notify.kind.script_volume_missing.title: Volume {subject} of the scripts is missing
notify.kind.share_account_skipped.text: No Linux user could be made on the NAS for the account, its user ID may be taken already. All other accounts and shares are applied; TitanOS tries again every ten minutes.
notify.kind.share_account_skipped.title: Account {subject} without access to shares
notify.kind.share_data_delete_failed.tex: Deleting did not run through. Tools › Tasks gives the reason and whether the data is still there.
notify.kind.share_data_delete_failed.tit: Data of the share {subject} not deleted
notify.kind.share_data_deleted.text: The share and its folder were removed.
notify.kind.share_data_deleted.title: Data of the share {subject} deleted
notify.kind.share_guard_locked.text: Many files were renamed in a suspicious way within a short time. The share is now read-only. Check the device of the account before you unlock it.
notify.kind.share_guard_locked.title: Share {subject} locked: suspected ransomware
notify.kind.snapshot_restore_done.text: The folder was fully restored from the Btrfs snapshot.
notify.kind.snapshot_restore_done.title: Folder {subject} restored
notify.kind.snapshot_restore_failed.text: The folder could not be fully restored. Files already finished stay.
notify.kind.stick_error.text: The stick no longer reads or writes reliably. Check that the backup of the stick is up to date (Settings › Backups) and replace the stick with a new one soon.
notify.kind.stick_error.title: The boot stick {subject} shows errors
notify.kind.system_data_volume_back.text: The volume {subject} chosen for system data is mounted again; system data go there again.
notify.kind.system_data_volume_back.titl: Volume {subject} for system data is back
notify.kind.system_data_volume_missing.t: The volume {subject} chosen for system data has not been mounted for a quarter of an hour. The system log, the activity log, notifications and the SMART and monitoring history wait in memory until then and are lost with a restart; TitanOS does not switch to another volume by itself. Mount the volume or choose another one under Settings › Data and backup › System data.
Volume {subject} for system data is missing
notify.kind.temperature_critical.text: A sensor is getting close to its critical value. Check the airflow and the fans; when overheating, the hardware switches itself off.
notify.kind.temperature_critical.title: Critical temperature: {subject}
notify.kind.test.text: If you can read this, this way of notifying works.
notify.kind.test.title: Test message
notify.kind.unclean_shutdown.text: The previous start ended without a clean shutdown (power cut, crash or reset); last trace {subject}. Check the state of the volumes; the log of the previous start is under Tools › Logs.
notify.kind.unclean_shutdown.title: The NAS was not shut down properly
notify.kind.update_available.text: A new version of TitanOS is out. You find it under Settings › Updates.
notify.kind.update_available.title: TitanOS {subject} is available
notify.kind.update_failed.text: The new version did not start. The NAS runs the former one again.
notify.kind.update_failed.title: Update to TitanOS {subject} failed
notify.kind.update_installed.text: The update is installed and started. The former version stays on the stick as a fallback.
notify.kind.update_installed.title: TitanOS {subject} is running
notify.kind.update_rolled_back.text: The NAS runs this version again.
notify.kind.update_rolled_back.title: Back on TitanOS {subject}
notify.kind.ups_lost.text: The UPS does not answer any more. In a power failure the NAS cannot shut down in time like this.
notify.kind.ups_lost.title: No connection to the UPS
notify.kind.ups_low_battery.text: The UPS reports an almost empty battery. The NAS shuts down now.
notify.kind.ups_low_battery.title: Battery of the UPS almost empty
notify.kind.ups_on_battery.text: The UPS powers the NAS. If the power does not come back, the NAS shuts down in time.
notify.kind.ups_on_battery.title: Power failure: the NAS runs on battery
notify.kind.ups_online.text: The UPS is on mains power again.
notify.kind.ups_online.title: The power is back
notify.kind.ups_shutdown.text: The NAS ran {subject} minutes on battery and shuts down now, as set.
notify.kind.ups_shutdown.title: The NAS is shutting down
notify.kind.usb_format_failed.text: Files › Format drive says why. The disk may be empty or incomplete.
notify.kind.usb_format_failed.title: Formatting {subject} failed
notify.kind.usb_formatted.text: The new filesystem is ready under Files › Other drives.
notify.kind.usb_formatted.title: Drive {subject} formatted
notify.kind.usb_partitions_changed.text: The change under Files › Format drive › Partitions is done.
notify.kind.usb_partitions_changed.title: Partitions of {subject} changed
notify.kind.usb_partitions_failed.text: Files › Format drive › Partitions says why. Check the partitions before going on.
notify.kind.usb_partitions_failed.title: Changing the partitions of {subject} failed
notify.kind.usb_plugged.text: Mount it under Files › Other drives to copy files.
notify.kind.usb_plugged.title: USB drive {subject} plugged in
notify.kind.vm_backup_undo_failed.text: For the backup the VM {subject} was paused briefly or switched to an overlay; putting it back did not work. Its data are complete. TitanOS tries again at the next start, at the next backup and before the VM is started next. Check under VMs whether it runs.
notify.kind.vm_backup_undo_failed.title: VM {subject} not back to normal after the backup
notify.kind.vm_io_error.text: Accessing a disk of the VM failed on the NAS. Check volume and SMART values under Storage before you resume it.
notify.kind.vm_io_error.title: VM {subject} paused after a disk error
notify.kind.vm_schedule_forced.text: The guest of the VM {subject} did not shut down within the waiting time. TitanOS switched the VM off (like pulling the plug).
notify.kind.vm_schedule_forced.title: {subject} switched off
notify.kind.vm_schedule_start_failed.tex: The VM {subject} could not be started at the scheduled time. Details are under Tools › Log.
notify.kind.vm_schedule_start_power.text: The NAS shuts down shortly by its power schedule. The VM {subject} was therefore not started.
notify.kind.vm_schedule_start_skipped.te: The VM {subject} was not started: its volume was missing or a snapshot, clone or disk copy ran for 30 minutes.
notify.kind.vm_schedule_stop_failed.text: The VM {subject} could not be shut down at the scheduled time. Details are under Tools › Log.
notify.kind.vm_schedule_stop_skipped.tex: The VM {subject} was not shut down because a snapshot, clone or disk copy ran for 30 minutes.
notify.kind.vm_schedule_stop_timeout.tex: The guest of the VM {subject} did not react to the shutdown within the waiting time. “Switch off afterwards” is not set for this VM.
notify.kind.vm_schedule_stop_timeout.tit: {subject} still runs after the scheduled shutdown

notify.kind.volume_cache_removed.text: All data was written back. The SSD is free after the next start.
notify.kind.volume_cache_removed.title: Volume {subject}: write cache removed
notify.kind.volume_degraded.text: The volume goes on without redundancy. Replace the failed disk soon; if another one fails, the data is lost.
notify.kind.volume_degraded.title: Volume {subject}: a disk is missing
notify.kind.volume_disk_remove_failed.te: Btrfs could not move the data to the other disks. The volume can be used as before; the log has details.
notify.kind.volume_disk_removed.text: Btrfs moved the data to the other disks. The disk is free.
notify.kind.volume_disk_removed.title: Volume {subject}: disk removed

notify.kind.volume_mismatch.title: Volume {subject}: the check found differences
notify.kind.volume_missing.text: The disks of the volume are not there. Shares, apps and VMs on it stand still.
notify.kind.volume_missing.title: Volume {subject} was not found
notify.kind.volume_ok.text: The volume is complete and in sync.
notify.kind.volume_ok.title: Volume {subject} is in order again
notify.kind.volume_rebuilding.text: Until the rebuild is done the volume is not fully protected again.
notify.kind.volume_rebuilding.title: Volume {subject}: rebuild in progress

notify.testOk: Test message sent. Check whether it arrived.

nvr.account.mailHint: Cameras send messages to this address when an administrator adds you to a camera as a recipient by e-mail.
nvr.account.mailNoServer: The NAS has no mail server yet. Until an administrator sets one up, no e-mails are sent.
nvr.add.intro: Search the network for the camera or enter its address, check the connection and choose what it should recognize, record and report.
nvr.add.none: No camera found. Enter its address below by hand.
nvr.add.searchHint: Finds cameras that speak ONVIF. Takes about three seconds; no password is sent.
nvr.add.title: Add a camera
nvr.areas.addPoint: Add a point between point {a} and {b}
nvr.areas.drawing: Drawing a {kind}: tap or click into the picture to set points; from three points on, “Done” or a tap on the first point closes the area.
nvr.areas.editHint: Tap an area or choose it in the list: drag points to move them, “+” on an edge adds one, a chosen point can be removed (also with Delete) and moved with the arrow keys.
nvr.areas.hint: Zones are named areas: events and messages can be limited to them. Masks leave out places where no motion or nothing should be detected.
nvr.areas.kindHint.motion: The NVR looks for no motion here – trees in the wind or the time shown in the picture, for example.
nvr.areas.kindHint.objects: The NVR detects nothing here – the street with parked cars, for example.
nvr.areas.messagesWidened: Messages came only from the zone “{zone}”. Without it the camera reports for the whole picture once saved – another zone can be chosen under “Report only in zones” while one is drawn.
nvr.areas.name: Name of the zone
nvr.areas.newCamera: Areas can be drawn once the camera is saved and sends a picture.
nvr.areas.noPicture: The camera sends no still picture right now. Areas can only be drawn with a picture; those drawn stay.
nvr.areas.onlyHint: Only objects that enter a zone become events and messages; with “On detected objects” only they are recorded.
nvr.areas.onlyNeedsZone: Possible once a zone is drawn.
nvr.areas.picture: Still picture of the camera with the areas
nvr.arrange.hint: Grab a camera to move it, drag the bottom right corner to size it. “Done” saves the arrangement for your account.
nvr.arrange.hintPhone: Set the order with the arrows. “Done” saves it for your account.
nvr.arrange.tile: {name}: arrow keys move, Shift + arrow keys size
nvr.audio.hint: Records the camera's sound too and lets you listen live. Off by default.
nvr.audio.none: The check found no sound on this camera.
nvr.audio.title: Sound
nvr.audio.twoWayHint: Talk to the camera through the microphone in the live view. The camera needs a speaker for that.
nvr.audio.twoWayNeedsSound: Only works with sound switched on.
nvr.camera.checkFirst: Check the connection first: TitanOS then finds the camera's streams.
nvr.camera.enrichAvx: Plates and faces need a processor with AVX2.
nvr.camera.enrichMemory: Plates and faces need at least 4 GB of memory.
nvr.camera.enrichNo: Plates and faces do not work on this NAS.
nvr.camera.hostHint: IP address or name in the home network, and the ONVIF port (mostly 80 or 8000).
nvr.camera.kindHint: ONVIF finds the streams itself. With an RTSP address you enter them directly.
nvr.camera.loginHint: User and password of the camera, not of TitanOS.
nvr.camera.mainUrlHint: The RTSP address in full resolution; it is recorded.
nvr.camera.name: Name
nvr.camera.nameExists: A camera with this name exists already (upper and lower case do not count). Choose another name.
nvr.camera.public: Allow an address outside the home network
nvr.camera.publicHint: Switch on only if the camera really is there. Picture and password then travel over the internet.
nvr.camera.subUrlHint: A small stream for detection saves a lot of computing power.
nvr.cameras.many: The NVR is designed and tested for up to four cameras. More works but can overload weaker hardware.
nvr.cameras.removeRights: The shares of this camera for users are dropped.
nvr.cameras.removeText: Nothing more is recorded from this camera. Its recordings and events stay until their retention ends – administrators find them under “Removed cameras” and under Recordings. Exports stay.
nvr.decoder.hint: Which graphics unit decodes the cameras' videos for detection. “Automatic” uses the iGPU, without one another Intel or AMD graphics unit, else the CPU. An NVIDIA card decodes only if you choose it here. Without a graphics unit the CPU is loaded more.
nvr.decoder.reason.driver: The chosen graphics unit cannot be used right now: its driver is missing or Docker cannot attach it. The CPU decodes the videos.
nvr.decoder.reason.gone: The chosen graphics unit is no longer in the NAS. Until you choose another, the CPU decodes the videos.
nvr.decoder.reason.vm: The chosen graphics unit is assigned to a VM. Until it is back, the CPU decodes the videos.
nvr.decoder.title: Decode videos
nvr.detect.hint: What this camera should report and mark.
nvr.detect.singleHint: Plates need a vehicle, faces a person to be recognized first.
nvr.detect.title: Recognize
nvr.detector.coralPluginHint: Install the plugin “Coral USB” so that the NVR can use the Coral stick.
nvr.detector.cpuHint: The CPU is the slowest way: it gets noticeably loaded and detection reacts more slowly.
nvr.detector.title: Detection runs on
nvr.diag.accelHint: The device node through which the container reaches the NPU.
nvr.diag.containerTimes: Started: {started} · ended: {finished} · ends in the last 5 minutes: {ends}
nvr.diag.copyFailed: The browser did not allow copying.
nvr.diag.decodeNo: Video is decoded on the CPU (no graphics unit found for it).
nvr.diag.decodeYes: Video is decoded by the graphics unit.
nvr.diag.enrichYes: Plates and faces are possible on this NAS.
nvr.diag.firmwareNone: The kernel reported nothing about an NPU.
nvr.diag.inferenceHint: How long the device needs to analyse one picture. Below 50 ms is good.
nvr.diag.intro: Everything to see without a terminal why detection runs or does not. No passwords appear here.
nvr.diag.logContainer: The last lines of the container.
nvr.diag.logFrigate: The last lines of the detection software.
nvr.diag.restartHint: Tries the chosen detection device once more.
nvr.diag.shmHint: The pictures for detection live here. If it is almost full a sub stream delivers pictures that are too large.
nvr.diag.stateText.docker_off: Docker is switched off. The NVR cannot run like this.
nvr.diag.stateText.docker_starting: Docker is switched on but not ready yet.
nvr.diag.stateText.error: Docker refused something. TitanOS tries again after a minute.
nvr.diag.stateText.no_volume: The volume for the recordings is not mounted; the container was removed.
nvr.diag.stateText.off: The NVR is switched off; there is no container.
nvr.diag.stateText.pulling: The detection software (Frigate) is loading from the internet.
nvr.diag.stateText.running: The detection software answers, accepted the settings and the detection device works.
nvr.diag.stateText.starting: The container runs, the detection software does not answer yet.
nvr.diag.stateText.stopped: Nothing worked. The NVR waits for you and does not record.
nvr.events.autoplayMuted: The video plays without sound because the browser allows sound only after a tap. Tap the speaker in the video.
nvr.events.deleteKeptText: The event, its snapshot and the saved video are deleted. This cannot be undone.
nvr.events.deleteText: The event and its snapshot are deleted. The continuous recording of this time stays.
nvr.events.fromRecording: The event's clip is not ready yet; the video shows the recording from the event on.
nvr.events.keepRunning: Keeping is possible once the event is over and its recording is complete.
nvr.events.keptNoVideo: yes – event and picture stay until you delete them; there is no recording of this time
nvr.events.keptText: yes – event, picture and video stay until you delete them
nvr.events.keptVideo: The recording of this time cannot be played (for example because its days are over); the video is the saved copy of the kept event.
nvr.events.noMedia: This event has neither a clip nor a picture.
nvr.events.seenHint: A dot marks what you have not looked at yet. “Seen” counts for each account on its own.
nvr.events.unavailable: Events are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.events.unkeepText: The event then follows the camera’s retention again and is deleted after {days} days.
nvr.events.unkeepVideo: The saved video is deleted. If the recording of this time is gone already, no video is left afterwards.
nvr.export.deleteText: “{name}” is deleted. The recording itself stays as long as it is kept.
nvr.export.failedHint: The NVR could not make this clip – mostly because nothing was recorded in that period. Delete it and choose a period with a recording.
nvr.export.hint: Saves a stretch of “{name}” as an MP4 file to download. Exports are never deleted automatically.
nvr.export.missing: Exports are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.export.name: Name
nvr.export.title: Export a stretch
nvr.faces.deletePictureText: The picture of {name} is deleted and no longer counts for recognition.
nvr.faces.deleteText: The person and all their pictures are deleted. The NVR no longer recognizes them.
nvr.faces.hint: People the NVR should call by name.
nvr.faces.missing: Known faces are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.faces.name: Name of the person
nvr.faces.nameProblem.space: No spaces – write for example “Grandma_Erna” or “Grandma-Erna”.
nvr.faces.nameProblem.start: The name starts with a letter or a digit.
nvr.faces.nameProblem.train: “train” is taken by the faces not assigned yet. Choose another name.
nvr.faces.nameRule: Letters (accented ones too) and digits, plus - and _, at most 40 characters, no spaces.
nvr.faces.pictureHint: A picture has to show exactly one clearly visible face (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 8 MB at most). Several pictures per person improve recognition.
nvr.faces.title: Known faces
nvr.faces.unused: No camera recognizes faces yet. Switch faces on for a camera under “Recognize”.
nvr.failover.retryHint: “Try again” restarts the NVR and tries the chosen device once more (a gap of about a minute).
nvr.failover.title: Detection now runs on: {to} (chosen: {from})
nvr.ha.hint: Messages about events come only while entities in Home Assistant are as you choose here – for example only while the alarm is armed. “Camera offline” always comes. Recording and detection go on regardless.
nvr.ha.lastState: At least one state stays chosen.
nvr.ha.loadFailed: The entities of Home Assistant could not be loaded: {error}
nvr.ha.modeHint: Whether all conditions must hold or one is enough.
nvr.ha.none: Home Assistant is not connected. Set up the connection under Control panel › Home Assistant.
nvr.ha.ruleHint: Entity and the states in which messages come.
nvr.ha.title: Only with a state in Home Assistant
nvr.ha.unknownHint: If Home Assistant cannot be reached or a state is unknown, the message comes anyway and says so.
nvr.live.forbidden: This camera is no longer shared with you.
nvr.live.noneAdmin: Add your first camera: TitanOS searches the network for it or you enter its address.
nvr.live.noneUser: No camera is shared with you. An administrator can change that under Users › Cameras.
nvr.live.onlyRecordings: Live pictures are not shared with you, recordings are.
nvr.live.stillHint: Live video is not running here right now; the picture is renewed every two seconds.
nvr.notify.agentHint: The AI agent gets this camera's messages too.
nvr.notify.daysHint: The time window starts on these days.
nvr.notify.devicesOff: Push: the account's devices have camera messages switched off.
nvr.notify.faceUnknownNeedsFaces: Possible when the camera recognises faces.
nvr.notify.homeAssistantHint: Shows the camera in Home Assistant as a device with sensors (over MQTT, group "Cameras"). These are states, not messages; they go on even while the cameras' messages are off.
nvr.notify.legacy: This camera used to tell every administrator. They are chosen the way the camera told them so far; after saving, the choice here counts.
nvr.notify.legacyEmail: The e-mail used to go to the address of the NAS. Now it goes to each recipient's own address: choose "E-mail" at the accounts for that.
nvr.notify.mainOff: The messages of all cameras are switched off (NVR › Settings › Notifications). Until they are on again, this camera reports nothing.
nvr.notify.mainOffHint: Off: no camera reports anything – no bell, no push, no e-mail, nothing to the AI agent. Home Assistant still gets the cameras' states.
nvr.notify.mainOnHint: On: each camera reports as set for it. Below is who gets what.
nvr.notify.noAddress: E-mail: the account has not entered an e-mail address of its own.
nvr.notify.noDevice: Push: the account has no device signed up for notifications.
nvr.notify.noMailServer: E-mail: no mail server is set up (Settings › Notifications).
nvr.notify.noNames: Plates and faces: the account gets no messages about them, as it lacks the right "Names and plates" for this camera (at the account, under "Cameras").
nvr.notify.overviewGone: the account no longer exists or is locked
nvr.notify.overviewLegacyEmail: e-mail to the address of the NAS
nvr.notify.overviewNoNames: {name} gets no messages about plates and faces (no right "Names and plates")
nvr.notify.pauseHint: For this long the camera does not report the same kind (a person, say) again.
nvr.notify.recipientsHint: Who gets this camera's messages and how. The accounts that may see this camera can be chosen.
nvr.notify.recipientsNewHint: Who gets this camera's messages and how. For a new camera only administrators can be chosen: users come in once they have the right to the camera (at the account, under "Cameras").
nvr.notify.stale.gone: Gets nothing: the account no longer exists or is locked.
nvr.notify.stale.noRight: Gets nothing: the account may not see this camera.
nvr.notify.timeHint: In the time zone of the NAS. If "until" is before "from", the window runs across midnight into the next day. Equal times mean the whole day.
nvr.notify.userNoBell: User – has no bell in TitanOS, only push and e-mail.
nvr.notify.windowHint: Report persons, vehicles, animals, plates and faces at certain times only. "Camera not reachable" is always reported.
nvr.notify.zonesHint: Messages about events only when the object enters one of the chosen zones. “Camera not reachable” is always reported.
nvr.off.title: The NVR is switched off
nvr.off.user: An administrator can switch it on and share cameras with you.
nvr.plates.badPlate: “{plate}” does not work: a plate has 1–64 characters of letters, digits, spaces and -, plus * for any characters.
nvr.plates.hint: Plates with a name, such as “Our car”.
nvr.plates.missing: Known plates are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.plates.name: Name
nvr.plates.patternHint: Separate several plates per name with commas. A star stands for any characters, e.g. MAB12*.
nvr.plates.seenOld: “–” means: not among the newest 1000 vehicle events, count and time are not known.
nvr.plates.title: Known plates
nvr.plates.unused: No camera reads plates yet. Switch plates on for a camera under “Recognize”.
nvr.privacy.failed: The notice could not be hidden: {reason}
nvr.privacy.text: Point cameras only at your own property, not at the street or the neighbours. People who are filmed should know about it – for example from a sign. Faces and number plates are personal data: recognize them only where you are allowed to, and keep recordings no longer than needed.
nvr.privacy.title: Privacy notice
nvr.probe.hint: Checks address and login and shows which streams the camera delivers.
nvr.probe.locked: The camera locked the account, probably after too many wrong passwords. Wait a few minutes.
nvr.probe.no_stream: The camera answers but delivers no stream.
nvr.probe.not_found: The camera does not know this stream. Check the address.
nvr.probe.subUsed: Detection uses the small sub stream.
nvr.probe.title: Check the connection
nvr.probe.unauthorized: The camera refused the user or password.
nvr.probe.unreachable: No camera answers at this address.
nvr.ptz.hint: The camera can be moved in the live view.
nvr.ptz.needsOnvif: Moving only works with cameras connected over ONVIF.
nvr.ptz.notFound: The check found no controls on this camera.
nvr.ptz.title: Pan, tilt and zoom
nvr.reason.config_invalid.title: The detection software refused the settings.
nvr.reason.config_invalid.todo: Take back the last change to a camera and press “Try again”. If it stays: “Copy details” and report it as a bug.
nvr.reason.config_invalid.what: TitanOS made a configuration from cameras and settings that Frigate does not accept. The detection device is not to blame, so nothing was switched.
nvr.reason.coral_missing.title: The Coral stick was not found.
nvr.reason.coral_missing.todo: Plug the stick directly into the NAS (a USB 3 port if possible, without a hub), check the plugin “Coral USB” and press “Try again”.
nvr.reason.coral_missing.what: The detection software saw no Coral stick on the USB port.
nvr.reason.detector_unknown.title: Detection failed for an unknown reason.
nvr.reason.detector_unknown.todo: Read the line under “Detail” and the log below. “Try again” tries the chosen device once more.
nvr.reason.detector_unknown.what: The detection software ended or the detection device does not answer; the error line fits no known cause.
nvr.reason.engine.title: Docker did not start the container.
nvr.reason.engine.todo: TitanOS tries again every minute. Docker's message is under “Detail”.
nvr.reason.engine.what: Docker refused to create or start the container.
nvr.reason.not_healthy.title: The detection software did not answer after the start.
nvr.reason.not_healthy.todo: Look into the log below and press “Try again”. A very full NAS (memory) can be the reason.
nvr.reason.not_healthy.what: The container ran but Frigate could not be reached for five minutes.
nvr.reason.npu_firmware_old.title: The NPU firmware of the NAS is too old.
nvr.reason.npu_firmware_old.todo: Nothing to repair: detection runs on the next device meanwhile. A TitanOS update with newer firmware fixes it; then “Try again”.
nvr.reason.npu_firmware_old.what: The detection software ships a newer NPU driver than the firmware in the TitanOS image understands. The NPU itself is fine.
nvr.reason.npu_missing.title: The NPU was not found in the container.
nvr.reason.npu_missing.todo: Look below at “/dev/accel” and “NPU firmware”. If both are missing this NAS has no usable NPU: choose the iGPU.
nvr.reason.npu_missing.what: The device node /dev/accel is missing or the detection software sees no NPU through it – mostly the kernel driver or the firmware is missing.
nvr.reason.npu_turbo_unsupported.title: The NPU of this processor is not supported by the detection software yet.
nvr.reason.npu_turbo_unsupported.todo: Choose the iGPU under settings or keep “Automatic”. The NPU works with a newer Frigate version in a TitanOS update.
nvr.reason.npu_turbo_unsupported.what: A known bug of the built-in Frigate version on Core Ultra 200 processors (Arrow Lake): it asks the NPU for a setting that does not exist there.
nvr.rec.empty: There are no recordings of “{name}” on this day.
nvr.rec.missing: Recordings are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.rec.nextEventNone: No further event on this day
nvr.rec.noneUser: No recordings are shared with you. An administrator can change that under Users › Cameras.
nvr.rec.nothingAfter: There is no recording after this time on this day.
nvr.rec.pickHint: Choose a time on the time line.
nvr.rec.playFailed: The recording could not be played.
nvr.rec.unsupported: This browser cannot play the camera’s video format. Download a clip or use another browser.
nvr.record.aroundEvents: With “On detected objects” only stretches in which a detected object moves are kept, so the seconds before and after are often missing.
nvr.record.aroundHint: Seconds recorded before and after an event (60 at most).
nvr.record.eventDaysHint: The recordings around events and their pictures stay this long – also longer than the rest of the recording.
nvr.record.eventDaysOnlyHint: The recordings of events and their pictures are deleted after this many days.
nvr.record.hint.continuous: Around the clock. Needs the most room.
nvr.record.hint.events: Only while the camera recognizes something chosen above.
nvr.record.hint.motion: Whenever something moves in the picture.
nvr.record.hint.off: Live picture and notifications only, no recordings.
nvr.record.recordDaysHint: Continuous recording without an event is deleted after this many days.
nvr.record.recordDaysMotionHint: Parts with motion but no event are deleted after this many days.
nvr.record.retainHint: Older recordings of this camera are deleted.
nvr.record.title: Record
nvr.removed.groupHint: They record nothing and have no live picture. Their recordings and events stay until their retention ends or you delete them; only administrators see them.
nvr.removed.purgeNeedsRunning: Deleting works only while the NVR runs.
nvr.removed.purgeRestart: The NVR restarts once afterwards: the other cameras record nothing for about half a minute.
nvr.removed.purgeText: All recordings, events and pictures of this camera are deleted now, kept events too. This cannot be undone; the camera then leaves this list.
nvr.removed.purgingHint: The NAS deletes in the background, also when you close the window; with many recordings this takes a few minutes. If something fails, the bell says so.
nvr.removed.untilUnknown: Removed – recordings until their retention ends
nvr.rights.adminHint: Owner and administrators always see all cameras and recordings.
nvr.rights.hint: Which cameras of the NVR this account may see. Without a switch it does not see a camera at all.
nvr.rights.namesHint: "Names and plates": names of recognised faces, names of known plates and plates read by this camera – in events, the live picture and messages. Only together with "Recordings"; without the tick they are left out there.
nvr.rights.noCameras: No camera is set up in the NVR yet.
nvr.rights.title: Cameras
nvr.rtsp.hint: Opens port 8554: Home Assistant then fetches the pictures from the NAS instead of from each camera. With a login of its own; off by default.
nvr.rtsp.loginHint: Enter address, user and password in Home Assistant. The last part of the address is the camera's id.
nvr.rtsp.title: Offer camera pictures to Home Assistant
nvr.search.settings: NVR › Settings (storage, detection device, faces, plates)
nvr.settings.backupHint: Settings, cameras, camera rights, known plates and the pictures of known faces are part of the daily backup of the stick. Recordings, events and exports are not backed up.
nvr.settings.diagnosisHint: Why detection runs or does not run, with the log.
nvr.settings.offKeeps: Settings, cameras and all recordings so far are kept.
nvr.settings.offText: Then nothing is recorded and nothing recognized any more.
nvr.setup.dockerText: The NVR runs in a container that TitanOS manages itself. Docker has to be switched on for that.
nvr.setup.enrichNo: This NAS cannot recognize plates and faces: that needs a processor with AVX2 and at least 4 GB of memory.
nvr.setup.imageHint: When switched on, TitanOS loads about 1.5 GB from the internet once. You then see the progress on the live page; meanwhile you can already add cameras.
nvr.setup.intro: The NVR records your network cameras and recognizes people, vehicles and animals, and plates and faces if you like. You only choose here – you never write a configuration file.
nvr.setup.sleepText: The disks of “{volume}” may sleep so far. While the NVR records they stay awake all the time. Use this volume anyway?
nvr.setup.title: Set up the NVR
nvr.shrink.days: Recordings older than {days} days are deleted.
nvr.shrink.eventDays: Events older than {days} days are deleted with their recordings and pictures.
nvr.shrink.events: Of the existing recordings only the parts with detected objects stay; everything else is deleted.
nvr.shrink.generic: The change deletes recordings that exist already.
nvr.shrink.motion: Of the existing recordings only the parts with motion stay; everything else is deleted.
nvr.shrink.title: Delete existing recordings?
nvr.shrink.when: This happens about a minute after saving and cannot be undone.
nvr.state.dockerOffHint: The NVR needs Docker. Nothing is recorded while Docker is off.
nvr.state.error: The NVR could not be started
nvr.state.errorHint: Docker refused the start. TitanOS tries again in a minute.
nvr.state.noVolumeHint: The recordings live there. The NVR stands still until the volume is back or you choose another one.
nvr.state.starting: The NVR is starting … This takes about a minute.
nvr.state.stopped: The NVR is stopped – nothing is recorded
nvr.state.userDown: The NVR is not running right now. Live pictures and recordings come back once it runs.
nvr.storage.capCleaning: The limit is reached: TitanOS deletes the oldest recordings until there is room again. Exports stay.
nvr.storage.capExports: The exports alone already need more room than the limit. So TitanOS deletes nothing right now – no recordings either. Delete exports (under Recordings) or raise the limit.
nvr.storage.capHint: Once the limit is reached the oldest recordings are deleted first. 0 = no limit; then only the days to keep count.
nvr.storage.usedUnknown: The usage is not known yet.
nvr.storage.volumeHint: This volume stays awake while recording.
nvr.stream.currentHint: To choose other streams, check the connection first.
nvr.stream.detectHighHint: High resolution needs much more computing power. If the camera states its picture size when checked, the NAS scales the picture down to at most 1280 pixels wide for it.
nvr.stream.detectHint: Which stream detection searches for people, vehicles and animals. High resolution needs much more computing power.
nvr.stream.keepOpenHint: The live picture appears at once, even while nothing is recorded. For this the camera stays connected to the NAS all the time.
nvr.stream.keepOpenOffHint: The NAS connects to the camera only when it needs a picture. The live picture then takes a moment longer.
nvr.stream.liveHint: Automatic: small live pictures show the low-resolution stream, a large live picture the high-resolution one.
nvr.stream.lowHint: A small picture of the camera. It saves computing power for detection and small live pictures.
nvr.stream.single: The camera delivers only one stream. It is used for everything.
nvr.talk.camera_gone: This camera is gone, or you may no longer see it.
nvr.talk.denied: The browser did not hand out the microphone. Allow it for this page in the address bar.
nvr.talk.failed: The talk connection to the camera failed. Away from home it only works over VPN or Tailscale.
nvr.talk.forbidden: You may no longer watch this camera live, so you cannot talk to it either.
nvr.talk.insecure: Talking needs a secure connection: open TitanOS with https:// – without it the browser does not hand out the microphone.
nvr.talk.logout: You are logged out. Log in again to talk.
nvr.talk.no_microphone: No microphone was found on this device.
nvr.talk.no_picture: The camera does not answer. Check the camera’s power and network.
nvr.talk.not_running: Talking does not work right now: the NVR is not running, or two-way sound is not switched on for this camera.
nvr.talk.unsupported: This browser cannot talk to the camera.
nvr.view.hideBar: Hide the bar at the top in full screen
nvr.view.title: View
ops.allClear: No pending errors in the loaded task states.
ops.allowStop: Stop selected running containers and VMs for the backup.
ops.appHint: Cleanly stop selected applications for this backup or export PostgreSQL with pg_dumpall. Stopping requires explicit consent. Other running containers writing the same data block a cold copy.
ops.appJournalMissing: The journal of this application backup is no longer on its volume, for example because a stick backup taken during the run was restored. What was stopped then is not known and is not started. Check containers and VMs yourself; afterwards the entry can be removed so that application changes work again.
ops.cancelGrowthConfirm: The expansion of {volume} that has not started is cancelled and its new spare is removed from the array if present. Data already erased on the new disk does not come back.
ops.cancelGrowthHint: Cancels only an expansion that has not started and removes its new spare if present. Erased data on the new disk is not restored.
ops.cloneHint: The source VM must be stopped. Independent disks, firmware and TPM are copied. The clone gets a new UUID/MAC and no autostart. Passthrough devices, host folders, block disks and backing chains are unsupported.
ops.discardCloneHint: The unpublished copy of {vm} is deleted. The original VM stays as it is.
ops.eraseConsent: Erase all data on the selected new disk. A current external backup is available.
ops.err.budget: The space set aside for the measurements is used up.
ops.err.cycle: The predecessors of the jobs form a loop. Choose another predecessor.
ops.err.dependencyMissing: The chosen predecessor no longer exists.
ops.err.devMode: TitanOS does not run maintenance in development mode.
ops.err.gaps: Too many gaps in this range. Choose a shorter range.
ops.err.persist: The outcome of the run could not be saved on the volume.
ops.err.pruneConsent: Confirm that old snapshots of this job may be deleted.
ops.err.reviewFirst: Review the interrupted job before removing it or changing its target.
ops.err.running: Maintenance is already running. Wait for it to finish or stop it.
ops.err.unavailable: This service is not available right now – usually the chosen volume is not mounted.
ops.err.unknownOutcome: The last run was interrupted; its outcome is unknown. Check the target and confirm the review before the job runs again.
ops.err.volumeChanged: The maintenance volume changed. Reload the page and try again.
ops.err.waiting: The job is waiting for other work of the NAS.
ops.everyHoursHint: Counted from the time below. Runs only in the maintenance window; for around the clock set the start and end of the window to the same time (e.g. 00:00 to 00:00). While a run is still going, the next one waits.
ops.everyHoursLong: Note: a RAID check or SMART long test reads every disk completely and often takes many hours. At short intervals the disks are under load almost all the time and wear faster; once a month is recommended. While a run is still going, the next one waits.
ops.failed: The operation could not be completed.
ops.finishCloneHint: The verified copy of {vm} is registered as a new VM. A foreign folder of the same name is not touched.
ops.foldersHint: Restore whole folders with “Restore …” next to the folder; pick single files here.
ops.forgetHint: Removes only the saved record. Already copied files and remaining partial copies are unchanged.
ops.growEraseWarning: The new disk {disk} is erased and added to the RAID of {volume} as an additional member. All data on this disk is lost.
ops.growHint: Adds one disk to healthy RAID 5/6 with ext4 or XFS. The new disk is erased. The recovery file and journal require a healthy separate volume on other physical disks. Other storage changes are blocked during the operation.
ops.growNoBtrfs: Btrfs mirrors cannot be expanded by a disk. More space needs a new volume.
ops.growNoLevel: Only RAID 5 and RAID 6 can be expanded. This volume is {level}; that needs a new volume.
ops.growNotHealthy: Only a healthy volume can be expanded. Current state: {state}.
ops.growthPending: An expansion is pending. Keep the recovery volume connected and inspect the displayed state.
ops.importHint: Supports assembled mdadm arrays with ext4/XFS and native two-device Btrfs mirrors. Preview mounts read-only without journal replay. Registration does not import accounts or shares.
ops.importReady: Read-only preview succeeded. Registration mounts the volume normally with write access.
ops.incomplete: Incomplete scan — values are partial results.
ops.lockDaysHint: For this long a snapshot of this job can be deleted neither by hand nor by the retention. 0 = no lock.
ops.maintenanceHint: One maintenance job runs at a time. It waits for backups, storage, VM and file operations. History and checkpoints live on the selected volume. Equal window times allow the whole day.
ops.monitorHint: Optional minute samples on a data volume. This can wake sleeping data disks. Interruptions appear as gaps. Disk latency is the mean of completed I/O operations.
ops.name: Name
ops.noSamples: No samples in the selected range.
ops.probeHint: Restores a bounded selection of regular files from the latest backup into a private test directory and verifies against the same snapshot. The test directory is removed afterwards.
ops.pruneConsent: Delete older automatic snapshots of this schedule. Keep manual snapshots.
ops.restartPrevious: Restart only the original instances that were running before.
ops.resumeConfirm: The pending expansion of {volume} resumes from the displayed state. Keep the recovery volume connected; other storage changes stay blocked until it finishes.
ops.reviewHint: The previous outcome is unknown. Inspect the target before allowing another run. Reviewing does not immediately start the job.
ops.selectFolderFiles: Select all {count} files in this folder
ops.selectTooMany: {count} files selected; at most 200 can be restored at once.
ops.snapshotBtrfsOnly: ext4/XFS have no snapshots. Scheduled snapshots exist only for Btrfs volumes; for the others a data backup helps.
ops.snapshotHint: Single files: up to 200 files and 10.7 GB in total into a new folder. Whole folders: “Restore …” next to the folder, to the original place or as a new folder next to it. Internal data is left out.
ops.stale: Refresh failed. The last known state remains visible.
ops.transferBlocked: Unknown file outcome — inspect source and destination before a new transfer.
ops.unsavedHint: This draft has not been saved.
ops.usageHint: On-demand scan, limited to 30 seconds and 200,000 entries. Logical sizes and allocated blocks do not add up to reclaimable space with hardlinks, reflinks and snapshots. Private operational data is excluded.
ops.window: Catch up in the next maintenance window
passkeys.addText: The passkey will work for {host}. Confirm with your password first; then your device asks for fingerprint, face or PIN.
passkeys.browserError: The browser could not use the passkey.
passkeys.intro: A passkey logs you in without password and code: the fingerprint, face or PIN of a phone, computer or security key is enough. A passkey only works at the address it was created for.
passkeys.name: Name
passkeys.notHere: Passkeys only work under a name with a valid HTTPS certificate (for example from Let's Encrypt), not through an IP address or a self-signed certificate.
passkeys.removeText: Nobody can log in to this account with “{name}” afterwards. Password and two-factor login stay as they are.
passkeys.title: Passkeys
personal.persistHint: Survives a service restart. Approval buttons are never saved. An unavailable volume produces an error.
personal.persistQuiet: Persist deferred messages on the data volume
personalNotify.event.storage: Disks, volumes and shares (warnings and errors)
personalNotify.event.system: System: power, UPS, network, certificates, VMs (warnings and errors)
personalNotify.event.updates: Updates of TitanOS, apps and plugins
personalNotify.intro: Choose which messages of the NAS reach you through your own channels, for example as a push message on your phone. These channels belong to your account only. The shared channels under Settings › Notifications stay as they are.
personalNotify.noMailServer: For e-mail, an administrator first has to set up a mail server under Settings › Notifications.
personalNotify.quietHint: During quiet hours TitanOS holds messages back and sends them together afterwards. Errors and urgent messages arrive at once. Held messages are lost if TitanOS restarts.
personalNotify.title: My notifications
phone.edit.hint: Drag to move, onto another symbol for a folder, to the edge for the next page. A tap picks a symbol for the buttons here.
phone.edit.newPage: Drag here for a new page
phone.files.pdfFirstPage: The first page as a picture – zoom with two fingers. The whole document: open or download it.
phone.files.shareFailed: The file could not be shared.
phone.files.shareReady: The file is loaded. Tap “Share” to hand it to another app.
phone.folder.label: Folder {name}, {count} programs
phone.folder.name: Name of the folder
phone.notices.swipeHint: Swipe left to delete a notification, right to mark it read. Pull down to load the list anew.
phone.settings.dockHint: At the bottom of the phone's home screen, with programs of its own (press long to arrange). Off: its programs are on the pages.
phone.settings.title: Phone
plugins.activateLaterHint: Without this option, the plugin is only installed on the data volume. Running VMs and containers remain unchanged. You can activate it later when the required hardware is available.
plugins.activationFailed: The plugin could not start. Check the hardware and service log under Tools, then retry activation.
plugins.busy: The driver is still in use. Stop its containers and other GPU jobs before disabling the plugin.
plugins.catalogDevelopment: This development build does not belong to a published release. Official downloads require a released TitanOS version. You can still use plugins from shares.
plugins.catalogError: The GitHub catalog could not be downloaded or verified. Installed, local and previously verified plugins remain visible. Refresh the catalog to try again.
plugins.catalogIntro: Install official plugins directly from GitHub. Only selected packages are downloaded, then stored on a data volume.
plugins.catalogUnavailable: The plugin catalog for TitanOS {version} has not been published in full yet. Try again later or upload matching plugin files into a share.
plugins.changes: What it changes on the system
plugins.choice.buildHint: The NAS downloads NVIDIA's sources and builds the driver itself on the plugin volume: at least 5.4 GB free, at most two CPU cores, about 15 minutes. It becomes active with the next restart.
plugins.choice.buildUse: Build and use after the next restart
plugins.choice.failed: Building {version} failed. The shipped driver {bundled} is running.
plugins.choice.kernelHint: After every kernel update the NAS rebuilds the chosen version by itself. Until it is done, the shipped driver runs.
plugins.choice.oldHint: Driver series older than the shipped one often no longer build with new kernels. If the build fails, the shipped driver stays.
plugins.choice.title: NVIDIA driver version
plugins.detectedNone: No matching hardware was detected on this NAS.
plugins.doesFiles: Adds programs and libraries to the system (under /usr).
plugins.downloadNote: Download: {size}. TitanOS checks the signature, system version, kernel and checksum before activation. This may take a few minutes.
plugins.driverAutomatic: Check daily and download new source packages automatically
plugins.driverBuildHint: The matching build environment and all working files stay on the plugin volume. At least 5.4 GB free space is required; the build uses at most two CPU cores and 2.1 GB RAM. Running GPU VMs and containers keep their current driver.
plugins.driverCheck: Check for a new NVIDIA version
plugins.driverHint: New public NVIDIA versions are verified and downloaded to the data volume. You start compilation and then choose the driver for the next NAS restart.
plugins.driverPending: Selected for the next NAS restart: {version}. Other plugin changes are blocked until restart or cancellation.
plugins.driverSource: NVIDIA {driver} · Container Toolkit {toolkit} · Source packages downloaded
plugins.driverState.building: Compiling the driver on this NAS
plugins.driverState.error: Check failed; existing driver is retained
plugins.driverState.sourceReady: Sources ready – you can start the build
plugins.driverState.unavailable: No matching build environment is available for this TitanOS version yet
plugins.emptyOfficial: To install manually, upload the image (name.raw), its description (name.plugin.json), and, for official plugins, its signature (name.plugin.json.minisig) together into a share.
plugins.emptyText: Official plugins for your TitanOS version and plugin files from your shares appear here.
plugins.enabledNote: Switching on activates the drivers and services. Switching off stops them and unloads kernel modules; modules in use prevent deactivation. The plugin files remain installed.
plugins.fromLinkText: Enter the link to the file <name>.plugin.json. The image <name>.raw must be in the same folder. TitanOS reads only the description first; the download starts when you install, directly to the data volume.
plugins.fromLinkTitle: Add a plugin from a link
plugins.integrityFailed: The installed plugin image does not match its checksum. Remove it and reinstall the original release files.
plugins.intro: Drivers and system functions that are not part of the base system. A plugin becomes part of the system. Apps (Docker) are under
plugins.kernelMismatch: This plugin was built for the kernel {built}; {running} is running here. It is not loaded until a matching version is installed.
plugins.needVolume: A data volume must be mounted before installing.
plugins.recommendedIntro: TitanOS found hardware for which a plugin exists and which no driver has taken yet. Nothing is installed without your click.
plugins.recommendedUnavailable: Offered once the catalog of this release is loaded.
plugins.removeHint: Switches the plugin off and deletes it from the volume.
plugins.removeText: The plugin is switched off and deleted from the volume. What you uploaded stays in the share.
plugins.sourceFormat: Format: {"name": "…", "plugins": [{"name": "example"}]}; the files <name>.plugin.json and <name>.raw lie next to the list. A set index from TitanOS-Plugins works too.
plugins.sourceRemoveText: Its plugins disappear from the catalog. Installed plugins stay installed but no longer get updates from this source.
plugins.sourcesText: A source is a list of community plugins (plugins.json). Its plugins appear in the catalog as “Community”, and newer versions are offered as updates. Nothing is ever installed on its own.
plugins.step.remove: Delete files from the data volume
plugins.stepsFailed: The marked step failed; later steps were not run.
plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.trustCommunity: Nobody has checked this plugin. It becomes part of the system and can do whatever the system can: reach all data, replace programs, make the NAS unusable. Only install it if you trust where it comes from.
plugins.trustLink: This plugin does not come from TitanOS and has not been reviewed. It becomes part of the system with full rights. Only install it if you trust its source.
plugins.trustOfficial: This plugin is signed by TitanOS. It becomes part of the system and runs with full rights.
plugins.updateAvailable: Version {version} is ready in a share.
plugins.updateAvailableDownload: Version {version} is available in the official catalog.
plugins.updateDownloadText: TitanOS downloads the signed new version directly to the data volume and checks it before the plugin is replaced.
plugins.updateText: TitanOS checks the new version, stops the plugin briefly and starts it with the new version. If it does not start, the previous version comes back. A plugin that is in use stays as it is.
plugins.where: Plugins live on the volume “{volume}” and are loaded as soon as it is mounted. They do not take up fixed RAM the way the base system does.
plugins.whereNone: Installed plugins live on a volume and are loaded as soon as it is mounted.
power.afterRebuild: Only after the running rebuild or check has finished
power.callOffHint: Cancelling starts again what was already ended.
power.diskTestNote: Running disk tests (prepare disks) are interrupted. With a mounted data volume they can be continued from the saved position afterwards; overwriting tests only after you confirm.
power.goingFailed: The NAS did not go down: {error}
power.maintenanceNote: Running storage maintenance (rebuild, check) may be interrupted; mdadm resumes RAID maintenance by itself after the start.
power.pendingRestart: {user} scheduled a restart after the rebuild.
power.pendingShutdown: {user} scheduled a shutdown after the rebuild.
power.preparingElsewhere: The NAS is being prepared for a restart or shutdown.
power.preparingNothing: Nothing runs that has to be ended.
power.preparingTextRestart: VMs, containers and Docker apps are being ended. Then the NAS restarts.
power.preparingTextShutdown: VMs, containers and Docker apps are being ended. Then the NAS shuts down.
power.restartNote: Takes about 1–2 minutes. The web UI reconnects by itself afterwards.
power.restartingText: This page reloads as soon as the NAS is reachable again.
power.servicesNote: All running services are stopped cleanly.
power.shutdownNote: To turn it on again, press the button on the device.
power.stuck: After 5 minutes this still runs: {names}. You can wait longer, go on anyway (VMs still running are then switched off) or cancel.
power.waitingRestart: The restart is scheduled and starts once rebuilds and checks have finished. Restarting titand drops it.
power.waitingShutdown: The shutdown is scheduled and starts once rebuilds and checks have finished. Restarting titand drops it.
power.wakeOnLanNote: With Wake-on-LAN switched on (Settings › Energy), the NAS can also be switched on again over the network.
power.workloadsNote: VMs, containers and Docker apps are ended first; they get up to 5 minutes for it. You see here what still runs.
powerButton.intro: Choose what a short press of the server’s power button does.
powerButton.longPress: Holding the button can force a hardware power-off. This setting does not change that.
powerButton.shutdownHint: Restart and shutdown use the normal system sequence to stop services and VMs cleanly. Pressing the button does not show an additional confirmation dialog.
powerButton.title: Power button
powerSchedule.intro: The NAS shuts down and starts again at set times. Running copies, backups, disk tests or a rebuild postpone the shutdown by up to six hours.
powerSchedule.noRtc: This mainboard has no wake alarm (RTC); switching on by schedule is not possible here. Wake-on-LAN, for example from Home Assistant, is an alternative.
powerSchedule.problem: Saved, but the hardware did not take everything:
powerSchedule.readOnly: In development mode nothing is shut down and the hardware is not changed.
powerSchedule.rtcHint: Switching on uses the wake alarm of the mainboard (RTC). Some mainboards need a BIOS setting for it; this is not checked on this hardware.
powerSchedule.title: Schedule and Wake-on-LAN
powerSchedule.wolDesc: Switch the NAS on over the network (“magic packet”)
powerSchedule.wolHint: Use the MAC address to wake the NAS, for example in Home Assistant's Wake-on-LAN integration. Some mainboards also need a BIOS setting.
proxy.aliasInvalid: The further name “{alias}” is not valid: only a–z, 0–9 and hyphens.
proxy.aliasesHint: Separated by commas, at most 8 ({count} entered).
proxy.allOffHint: All HTTPS names are switched off right now. The settings of each app and target are kept and apply again once they are switched on.
proxy.allOnHint: Switching off takes every name off the network at once; the settings of each app and target are kept.
proxy.appsEmpty: No app has an HTTPS name yet. Turn one on in the app editor under Docker › Edit app › “HTTPS name”.
proxy.domainHint: Optional, e.g. home.example.org. The router's DNS needs a wildcard *.home.example.org pointing at the NAS. Leave empty for .local names only.
proxy.domainInvalid: "{domain}" is not a valid domain (at least two labels, no .local, no wildcard).
proxy.domainsHint: Full names such as photos.example.org, separated by commas, at most 8 ({count} entered). The name must point at the NAS in DNS, e.g. through dynamic DNS.
proxy.hostHint: IP address or host name in the home network, over Tailscale or NetBird, e.g. of a VM.
proxy.hostInvalid: Not a valid address (IP address or host name).
proxy.howCert: Certificate: if the own certificate stored under Access covers the name (e.g. *.home.example.org), it is used. Otherwise TitanOS uses a self-signed wildcard certificate of its own, which the browser asks to confirm once per name.
proxy.howDomain: For an own domain TitanOS publishes nothing: the DNS of the router (e.g. Pi-hole, AdGuard, dnsmasq) needs a wildcard entry *.<domain> pointing at the address of the NAS.
proxy.howLocal: The NAS announces .local names in the home network itself via mDNS (avahi). This needs no router settings; some devices (e.g. older Android versions) do not know mDNS.
proxy.intro: TitanOS can make the app reachable under a name of its own such as https://immich.nas.local. TitanOS takes the connection on port 443 and passes it on to the app's port; the name is announced in the home network over mDNS. The TitanOS login never reaches the app. Saved right away, the container is not recreated.
proxy.localNameHint: Stands before “.local”, e.g. {example}. Leave empty for the name of the NAS. A new name creates a new app certificate.
proxy.localNameInvalid: Only lower-case a–z, digits, hyphens and dots, at most three parts.
proxy.localOnly: Only reachable from the home network, over Tailscale or NetBird
proxy.localOnlyOff: Without this limit the app is reachable under its name from the internet too, if the router forwards port 443 to the NAS.
proxy.mdns: Announce .local names in the home network (mDNS)
proxy.mdnsHint: Without mDNS there are no .local names; the apps are then only reachable under the own domain.
proxy.name: Name
proxy.nameInvalid: Only lower-case letters a–z, digits and hyphens (not at the start or end), at most 63 characters.
proxy.nameTaken: The app “{app}” already uses this name.
proxy.networksHint: One address or network per line (CIDR, IPv4 or IPv6), at most 32.
proxy.port: Port of the app on the NAS
proxy.portHint: The NAS port the app publishes (as in the WebUI address).
proxy.removeTargetText: The target “{app}” is then no longer reachable under {name}. Nothing changes on the target itself.
proxy.removeText: The app “{app}” is then no longer reachable under {name}. The app itself and its port stay as they are.
proxy.settingsIntro: Reach Docker apps under names of their own such as https://immich.nas.local. TitanOS accepts the connection on port 443 and passes it on to the port of the app. The TitanOS sign-in never reaches an app.
proxy.shortHint: Without the local name in between. .local names count for the whole home network: if another device has the same name, avahi renames one of them.
proxy.shortIsNas: The short name {name}.local would be the name of the NAS itself.
proxy.shortNoMdns: Short names need mDNS (under “For all names”).
proxy.tailnetHelp: How do I set this up?
proxy.tailnetIntro: Apps and targets with “Reachable through Tailscale” each become a device of their own in your tailnet, with their own name and a certificate from Tailscale. For each name TitanOS starts a small Tailscale instance from the plugin (about 20–40 MB of RAM); requests go through the TitanOS proxy, and the TitanOS sign-in never reaches an app.
proxy.tailnetNameInvalid: Name in the tailnet: only lowercase a–z, digits and hyphens, at most 63 characters.
proxy.tailnetNameTaken: “{app}” already uses this name in the tailnet.
proxy.tailnetState.https-off: HTTPS certificates are off in the tailnet
proxy.tailscale: Reachable through Tailscale (a device of its own in the tailnet)
proxy.tailscaleHint: The app gets a name of its own in the tailnet, such as https://immich.<your-tailnet>.ts.net, with a valid certificate from Tailscale. The access rules of your tailnet decide who may reach it.
proxy.tailscaleKeyHint: Create a reusable auth key in the Tailscale admin console under Settings › Keys (ideally with a tag such as tag:titanos-apps, for access rules of their own). Also turn on “MagicDNS” and “HTTPS Certificates” under DNS. The key is only needed for the first sign-in and is never shown again.
proxy.tailscaleKeyRemoved: Auth key removed. Devices that already joined keep running.
proxy.tailscaleNameHint: Becomes https://{name}.<your-tailnet>.ts.net. Leave empty for the name above.
proxy.tailscaleNoKey: An auth key is still missing under Settings › HTTPS names for apps › Tailscale.
proxy.tailscaleNoPlugin: The Tailscale plugin is not active. Names in the tailnet start once it runs.
proxy.targetsIntro: Names for things outside Docker too: VMs, LXC containers or devices in the home network, e.g. ha → Home Assistant VM. TitanOS only connects to addresses in the home network, over Tailscale or NetBird.
proxy.title: HTTPS name
proxy.toggle: Turn on the HTTPS name of {app}
proxy.unreachable: Without mDNS and without an own domain no app is reachable under a name.
proxy.verifyTLS: Check the certificate of the app
proxy.verifyTLSHint: Only switch on if the app has a certificate from a recognised authority for exactly this address; self-signed certificates then fail.
push.blocked: Notifications are blocked for this site in the browser. Allow them in the browser's site settings and reload the page.
push.denied: Permission for notifications was not given.
push.enabled: Notifications are on for this device.
push.homeScreen: On iPhone and iPad notifications only work for TitanOS on the home screen: in Safari tap "Share" › "Add to Home Screen", open TitanOS from there and turn them on here. The page needs a valid certificate for that (for example through Tailscale or Let's Encrypt).
push.intro: This device then shows messages of TitanOS (the same as the bell, from the level under "Send from"), of the AI agent and of the cameras where an administrator chose you as a recipient, even while TitanOS is not open; each can be switched off per device. They travel through the push service of the browser (at Apple, Google, Mozilla or Microsoft); the NAS needs internet access for that.
push.introPersonal: This device then shows the messages of your AI agent: task done, approval needed, reminders, and the messages of cameras where an administrator chose you as a recipient. Messages of the NAS go to owners and administrators only. They travel through the push service of the browser (at Apple, Google, Mozilla or Microsoft).
push.needsHttps: Notifications need HTTPS with a valid certificate, for example through the tailnet name of Tailscale or Let's Encrypt.
push.removeText: {name} gets no more notifications. They can be turned on again on the device itself at any time.
push.title: Notifications on this device
reconfirm.hint: Please confirm with your password that it is you.
reconfirm.hintCode: Please confirm with your password and a code from your authenticator app that it is you.
replication.code: Pairing code of the other NAS
replication.codeHint: On the other NAS, add a sending NAS under “Accept backups of other TitanOS” and paste the code here.
