replication.codeKeep: Leave empty to keep the current connection.
replication.desc: Mirrors a Btrfs volume snapshot by snapshot to a second TitanOS, for example at family or the office. After the first run only changes are sent. The other NAS must have “Accept backups of other TitanOS” on, and both need Tailscale.
replication.name: Name
replication.needBtrfs: Replication is available for mounted Btrfs volumes only.
replication.receiveHint: To let other TitanOS replicate here, turn on “Accept backups of other TitanOS” and choose a Btrfs volume.
replication.removeText: The setting is removed. What is already on the other NAS stays there.
replication.restoreText: The state {snapshot} of {source} is created as a new writable folder under “restored”. The replica itself stays unchanged.
replication.subvolumes: A snapshot of the whole volume is sent. Nested subvolumes (such as Docker's data) are not part of it.
replication.title: Replication to another TitanOS
report.intro: A summary of volumes, disks, backups, updates, UPS and the messages since the last report, through every channel switched on above and to devices with notifications. Wakes no disks.
report.title: Report about the NAS
rule321.intro: Rule of thumb for safe data: three copies, on two kinds of storage, one of them away from home. Then the data survives fire, theft or ransomware.
rule321.note: Backup jobs that are switched on count; several jobs to the same target are one copy. Cloud, SFTP, REST and another TitanOS NAS count as away from home. Whether every share is in a job shows the
rule321.title: 3-2-1 rule
safeguard.configHint: Back up the boot stick’s settings and accounts.
safeguard.dataHint: Back up files and folders to another destination.
safeguard.recoveryHint: Recover backed-up files and settings or replace a boot stick.
safeguard.restoreHint: Restore the configuration during initial setup: on a freshly prepared boot stick, choose “Restore configuration” before creating an account. Use a backup on a volume or a downloaded copy. Existing data disks are preserved.
safeguard.title: Backups
services.confirm: {name}: {count} are running. They are stopped cleanly; data and settings stay. When switched on again, whatever has autostart starts again.
services.dockerDesc: Apps and containers. Takes about 150 MB of RAM, plus the containers themselves.
services.intro: Switch off what you do not use: the service then does not run and takes no memory. Data always stays.
services.lxcDesc: Light Linux systems next to TitanOS.
services.offHint: Switched off – the tab is hidden. Existing data stays on the volume.
services.title: Services
services.vmsDesc: KVM/QEMU through libvirt. Takes about 40 MB of RAM without a running VM.
settings.appearanceDesc: Themes, colors, opacity, corners, font size and background.
settings.consoleIdle: End consoles and VM screens after
settings.consoleIdleDesc: Applies to the NAS shell, container, LXC and VM consoles and the VM screen. Only keyboard and mouse input counts. “Never” keeps open consoles running; logging out, locking and switching terminals off still end them.
settings.terminalConfirm: Ask for the password again before downloading stick backups
settings.terminalConfirmDesc: Consoles (NAS, Docker, VM screen and serial VM console) always use the existing administrator login without asking for the password again.
settings.terminalDesc: A root shell on the NAS and Docker consoles, for owners and administrators only. Your existing login is sufficient. Switching this off ends open sessions at once.
settings.timeHint: The time zone applies to NAS time and schedules. The system synchronises date and time automatically.
settings.timezoneDesc: Applies to schedules and logs of the NAS and is handed to new apps.
settings.title: Settings
settingshome.desc.appearance: Theme, accent, sliders, dock, sign-in page
settingshome.desc.services: Turn Docker, VMs, LXC on or off
settingshome.desc.speech: Whisper and Piper for Home Assistant and the agent
settingshome.desc.viewer: Docker apps in windows, GPU and sound
settingshome.todo.unknown: Some of it could not be checked.
share.appText: On the home screen, full screen and as a share target: photos and files from other apps go straight to the NAS.
share.deleteDataBlocked: The data cannot be deleted while the folder is used by:
share.deleteDataHint: Once the share is removed, the folder {path} is deleted for good with everything in it. This cannot be undone.
share.deleteDataMissing: The folder {path} does not exist. Only the share is removed.
share.deleteDataPartial: At least this much: counting stopped at the limit ({limit}). Everything is deleted all the same.
share.deleteDataStarted: The share {name} is being removed and its data deleted in the background.
share.deleteDataSubvolume: The folder is a Btrfs subvolume and is deleted as a whole.
share.deleteText: The share is removed. The files stay in {path} and are not deleted.
share.fileGone: No longer in the browser – share the file again.
share.guardHint: If an account renames many files over SMB within a short time to typical ransomware extensions, or all to the same new extension, the share becomes read-only for everyone and open connections are closed. On Btrfs a snapshot is taken at once as well.
share.guest: Guest access: anyone on the network may read without a password
share.guestWarning: With guest access every device on your network can read all files of this share.
share.iosHint: On an iPhone: in Safari “Share” › “Add to Home Screen”. iOS does not let web apps receive shares from other apps.
share.missing: The shared files did not arrive. Open TitanOS as an app once and share them again.
share.name: Name
share.nameHint: The name of the share on the network, e.g. “Photos 2024”. Letters, digits, blanks, -, _ and .
share.nfs: NFS – for Linux and devices without sign-in
share.nfsClients: Allowed hosts or networks, one per line
share.nfsClientsHint: IP address, network (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24) or host name, wildcards allowed (e.g. *.lan).
share.nfsClientsInvalid: Invalid: {clients}. Allowed are IP addresses, networks with a /prefix and host names.
share.nfsClientsNone: NFS needs at least one allowed host or network.
share.nfsReadOnlyHint: The NFS server rejects writes. After a rollback to an older version this NFS export remains disabled.
share.nfsWarning: NFS has no accounts. The selected access applies to all users on allowed clients; SMB account permissions remain independent.
share.nobodyWarning: No one has access. Samba does not offer the share then – give at least one account access.
share.noneHint: Share files from another app with “TitanOS” and they show up here.
share.otherHint: Choose “Install app” or “Add to home screen” in the browser menu.
share.previousVersionsBtrfs: Btrfs volumes only: they have snapshots.
share.previousVersionsHint: The volume's snapshots appear in Windows under Properties › Previous Versions. Everyone sees only what they may see in this share.
share.quotaHint.active: The kernel enforces the limit for every access: SMB, NFS, apps and the file manager. Windows sees it as the drive size.
share.quotaHint.off: Takes effect only once “Share quotas” is on for this volume under Storage.
share.quotaHint.pending: Quotas are on for this volume and apply after the next restart of the NAS.
share.quotaHint.unsupported: Share limits exist only on ext4 and XFS volumes, not on Btrfs.
share.quotaTooSmall: A limit must be at least 17 MB.
share.readFailed: The shared files could not be read.
share.recycle: Recycle bin: keep files deleted over SMB
share.saveText: Save the text as a file
share.smb: SMB – for Windows, macOS and Linux, with sign-in
share.timeMachine: Offer as a Time Machine target
share.timeMachineSize: Size limit in GB (0 = no limit)
share.title: Share to the NAS
share.use.backup-source: The backup job {name} saves this share.
share.use.count-limit: Counting stopped early; the figures are minimums.
share.use.docker-unknown: Docker does not answer; which containers mount the folder is unknown.
share.use.mount: Something is mounted in the folder: {path}
share.use.nested-subvolume: The folder holds another Btrfs subvolume or file system: {path}
share.use.purge-running: The data of a share is already being deleted.
share.use.share: The share {name} lies in this folder or the other way round: {path}
share.use.smb-unknown: Open SMB connections cannot be checked right now.
share.use.subvolume-snapshots: The subvolume has snapshots: {path}. Delete the snapshots first.
share.use.subvolume-unknown: Whether the subvolume has snapshots cannot be checked.
share.use.unsafe-path: The folder {path} cannot be deleted safely ({name}).
share.use.volume-snapshots: The volume has {name} snapshots. They keep their copy of the files; the space is freed only once they are deleted.
shares.copyFailed: Copying was not possible. The address is selected – copy it by hand (Ctrl/⌘+C).
shares.emptyHint: A share is a folder on a volume that computers on the network can open over SMB or NFS.
shares.guardLocked: Read-only since {time}: the account {user} renamed {files} files in a suspicious way (suspected ransomware).
shares.guardLockedHint: To lift the lock: AI agent › Functions › Ransomware guard, there “Open the share again”. Then write access can be saved here.
shares.guardUnlockText: Do this only once the affected device has been checked. Damaged files can be brought back from snapshots, the recycle bin or a backup.
shares.needVolume: A share needs a volume first.
shares.noProtocol: No network protocol is enabled for this share.
shares.perUser: Share of the KI-Agent: every account sees only its own folder here (on the network and in the file manager). TitanOS makes it and keeps the accounts up to date; no NFS and no guest access here.
shares.smbOptions: These options are available when SMB is enabled.
shares.title: Shares
sound.blocked: The browser blocked playback. Check sound permissions and test again.
sound.hint: For your account. Sounds play in the open browser after a click or keypress. Rapid notifications are grouped.
sound.title: Notification sounds
speech.agentDesc: The microphone of the input and “Read aloud” use these services instead of the device’s voice
speech.cpuDesc: without a GPU; small models run fine, large ones slowly
speech.cpuOnly: No NVIDIA GPU found. Small models run fine on the processor, large ones slowly.
speech.deviceDesc: Which GPU speech to text uses – or the processor
speech.deviceDriver: not available: the NVIDIA driver (plugin) is missing or not running
speech.deviceNote: Only speech to text uses the GPU. Text to speech (Piper) runs on the processor and is fast enough there.
speech.deviceVM: not available: passed through to a VM
speech.enableDesc: Starts both services once a model and a voice are active. TitanOS pulls the images the first time (about 0.4 GB together, about 1.9 GB with a GPU).
speech.enableNoVolume: First choose the volume for the models and voices.
speech.haDesc: Home Assistant talks to both services over the Wyoming protocol
speech.haStep1Hint: Settings › Devices & services › Add integration › “Wyoming Protocol”
speech.haStep3Hint: Settings › Voice assistants › Assistant: choose “faster-whisper” for speech-to-text, “piper” and the voice for text-to-speech; as the conversation agent the KI-Agent of TitanOS (Settings › KI-Agent › Home Assistant).
speech.intro: Speech to text and text to speech on this NAS – for Home Assistant and the KI-Agent. What is spoken does not leave the NAS.
speech.languageDesc: Which language is expected. A fixed language is faster and safer than “automatic”.
speech.model.medium: a good middle without a large GPU
speech.model.small: runs fine without a GPU too
speech.model.tiny: the smallest, only to try things
speech.needsRunning: The service is not running yet
speech.noVoices: There is no voice for this language.
speech.otherHostsApp: Home Assistant as an app on this NAS uses the address of the NAS in the home network (above).
speech.portBusy: Port {port} is used by another program
speech.reachDesc: The ports have no password. “Only Home Assistant” lets the Home Assistant set up here, a Home Assistant that uses the KI-Agent with the key, and apps on this NAS in.
speech.removeText: “{name}” is deleted from the volume. It can be downloaded again any time.
speech.sampleDe: Hallo, ich bin die Stimme deines NAS. Das Licht im Flur ist aus, und alle Sicherungen sind gelaufen.
speech.sampleEn: Hello, I am the voice of your NAS. The light in the hall is off, and all backups have run.
speech.seenNever: Nobody has connected since TitanOS started.
speech.seenRefused: Last refused {when} from {from} – the sender may not reach the services
speech.sttDesc: One model is active. Changing it takes a few seconds; larger models understand better.
speech.title: Speech services
speech.tryDesc: Speak into the microphone and see the text
speech.ttsDesc: The active voice is the default. Home Assistant can choose every downloaded voice.
speech.unavailable: There is no Docker in development mode: settings and downloads work, the services do not start.
speech.voicesError: The catalog of voices could not be loaded (internet?). Downloaded voices are listed below.
speech.volumeDesc: Volume for downloaded models and voices
speech.volumeLocked: Switch speech off to change it
ssh.keyHint: The one line from the file ending in .pub (for example ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub). Never the private key.
ssh.offHint: SSH access is switched off. Your keys count as soon as it is switched on.
ssh.onHint: With one of these keys you log in like this:
ssh.onlyAdmins: Only owners and administrators log in over SSH. Keys you store here count once your account has one of these roles.
ssh.removeLast: This is your last key. You will have no SSH access until you add a key again.
ssh.removeText: Nobody can log in to your account over SSH with the key “{name}” afterwards.
startup.empty: No order yet. Apps and VMs start after boot as before, but only once TitanOS is ready.
startup.extraHint: After “ready”, before the first app starts
startup.orderHint: A wait per entry; apps and VMs not listed start as before
startup.title: Start after boot
startup.vmAutostartOff: The VM's autostart is off – it does not start
startup.waitReady: Start only when TitanOS is ready
startup.waitReadyHint: Volumes mounted, shares reachable over SMB/NFS. Then apps and VMs start in the order below.
stay.foreverWarn: Whoever gets at a logged-in browser has access until the device is logged out. Log out after logging in on someone else's device.
stay.hint: Counted from the login. End single devices under My account › Logged-in devices; changing the password and locking an account end these logins as well.
stay.intro: How long a login lasts in the browser or the web app. Switched on, it also outlives a restart of the NAS. Applies to all accounts and to the logins there are already.
stay.offHint: Off: the login ends when the NAS restarts and after 7 days without use.
stay.title: Stay logged in
stick.asleepMany: The volumes {volumes} are asleep – their backups are not searched. Shown is what was last known.
stick.asleepOne: Volume {volumes} is asleep – its backups are not searched. Shown is what was last known.
stick.confirmReason: A backup holds password hashes and all secrets of the NAS. Enter your password once more to download it.
stick.downloadEncrypted: All copies are encrypted with the password of the backup. Keep the password apart from the NAS; without it they cannot be restored.
stick.downloadHint: Download a copy now and then and keep it away from the NAS.
stick.downloadPlain: Copies without a password (no lock) hold password hashes and all secrets of your apps in plain text – treat them like a password or set a password for the backup above.
stick.enabledHint: After every start and a few minutes after every change.
stick.encryptHint: The backup holds credentials for other services (e.g. backup targets, DDNS, Home Assistant). With a password a downloaded or stolen backup is worthless. Without the password the backup cannot be restored – keep it apart from the NAS.
stick.intro: Everything that makes up your NAS – accounts, volumes, shares, apps, network – lives on the stick only, and sticks break. So TitanOS puts copies of the configuration on a volume: once after every start and after every change. With a copy you set up a new stick in a few minutes.
stick.noVolume: No volume is mounted. The backup starts by itself as soon as there is one.
stick.off: The automatic backup is off. If the stick fails, you have to set up the NAS again by hand.
stick.ok: The configuration is saved. Newest copy from {time} on {volume}.
stick.pace.hint: There is always one backup after the start.
stick.passwordNew: New password (leave empty to keep it)
stick.plainVolume: The backup lies without a password on the unencrypted volume {volume}. Whoever gets hold of the disks can read password hashes and the credentials of your apps and services. Set a password below or choose an encrypted volume.
stick.ran: Checked. A new copy is only made when something changed.
stick.replaceIntro: When the stick fails or you want to swap it as a precaution:
stick.replaceNote: If the disks are gone as well, use a downloaded copy in the same step. After the restore the NAS is reachable at the address it had before.
stick.schedule.hint: Startup and change-triggered backups remain active. The schedule checks the configuration; unchanged data does not create duplicate backups.
stick.settingsDesc: Copies of the configuration on a volume – and how to replace a broken stick.
stick.step1: Download the zip of the same TitanOS version from the release page on GitHub.
stick.step2: Format a new stick with FAT32 and the name TITANOS and copy the content of the zip onto it.
stick.step3: Plug in the new stick and start the NAS. The disks stay as they are.
stick.step4: Open the web interface. Instead of creating a new account choose “Restore the configuration”: TitanOS finds the copies on the disks by itself. Then the NAS restarts and is its old self again.
stick.title: Back up system configuration
stick.volumeMissing: The chosen volume {volume} is not mounted. Until it is, nothing is saved.
storage.checksHint.many: No regular check is planned for the volumes {volumes} (RAID check or scrub, SMART tests for RAID 0). Errors in rarely read places otherwise show up only when the second copy is already gone.
storage.checksHint.one: No regular check is planned for the volume {volumes} (RAID check or scrub, SMART tests for RAID 0). Errors in rarely read places otherwise show up only when the second copy is already gone.
storage.checksHint.title: Regular checks are missing
storage.degradedNote: At least one disk is missing. The data is still there, but redundancy is reduced. Add a replacement disk.
storage.deleteHint: Deletes the volume with all data on it. This cannot be undone.
storage.failedNote: Too many disks are missing, the volume is not running. Do not change anything on the disks before it is clear what happened.
storage.freeHint: Free disks contain no partitions. You can create a new volume from them or add them to a volume as a spare that steps in automatically when a disk fails.
storage.missingNote: None of this volume's disks were found. Are they connected?
storage.noVolumesHint: A volume uses one or more disks for storage, protected against the failure of one or two disks depending on the RAID level.
storage.onVolumeIncomplete: Not everything could be read; the list is incomplete.
storage.pick: Select a volume to open details and actions.
storage.removeDiskConfirm: {disk} is removed from the volume {volume} and erased: TitanOS deletes the RAID label (mdadm superblock) and all filesystem signatures (wipefs). What was on the disk can no longer be read; the disk is free afterwards.
storage.shareQuotas.pending: On, apply after the next restart
storage.sleepDetails: SSDs, NVMe, the boot stick and disks passed through to VMs are excluded. Disk tests and RAID checks/rebuilds pause the timer. Apps and shares may keep disks awake. The first access after sleep can take a few seconds. Off disables automatic sleep by TitanOS; sleeping disks wake on their next access.
storage.sleepFailed: Sleep could not be enabled for the following disks. Some drives or USB enclosures do not support the command.
storage.sleepHint: Each HDD sleeps after its own period without reads or writes and wakes on the next access. The default applies to all disks; volumes and single disks can have their own value (disk before volume before default).
storage.sleepMissing: Values are still stored for {count} volumes or disks that no longer exist. They are removed the next time you save.
storage.sleepNoDisks: No hard disk found that TitanOS can put to sleep.
storage.sleepNoIdentity: No unique serial number or WWN: this disk uses the value of its volume or the default.
storage.sleepRaidNote: All disks of a volume get its value. A RAID only really sleeps when all its disks are idle: an access wakes the sleeping members anyway.
storage.sleepReason.name: not a SATA or SAS drive
storage.sleepReason.transport: The connection does not support standby
storage.sleepUnavailable: The setting could not be read from the boot stick. Automatic disk sleep remains disabled.
storage.sleepVolumeWholeHint: Default for all disks in it
storage.title: Storage
storage.wakeCause.unknown: unknown (not TitanOS itself – e.g. a share or an app)
storage.wakeHint.likely: “Probably” means TitanOS did not touch the volume itself; named is who was connected or runs there at that moment.
storage.wakeHint.systemData: TitanOS keeps its own data (logs, notifications, histories, configuration backup) on this volume and wakes it for that. Choose a volume that never sleeps:
storage.wakeHint.systemDataLink: Settings › Data and backup › System data
storage.wakeHint.unknown: “Unknown” means TitanOS itself did not touch the volume. It may have been a share (SMB, NFS), an app, a container or a VM with data there.
sysdata.aside.text: During the move these names existed on both volumes with different content. The entry here stayed in use, the one brought along lies next to it as “name.from-volume” and is not used. Look at it and delete it if you do not need it.
sysdata.common.desc: Applies to everything below unless something else is chosen there.
sysdata.config.password.none: Not set – backups are not encrypted
sysdata.config.when.change: A few minutes after every change
sysdata.config.when.daily: After changes, at most once a day
sysdata.fn.config.desc: Copies of the settings on the stick
sysdata.fn.notify.desc: Content of the bell and notifications held back
sysdata.fn.smart.desc: One entry per disk and day
sysdata.hint.ok: Good choice: this volume has no disks that go to sleep.
sysdata.hint.ownSleeps: Own volume with disks that may sleep: {functions}. These data wake the disks regularly.
sysdata.hint.spared: The disks of “{volume}” are no longer woken by system data.
sysdata.hint.sparedMany: The disks of {volumes} are no longer woken by system data.
sysdata.hint.warn: “{volume}” consists of hard disks that may sleep. System data wake them regularly.
sysdata.intro: Where TitanOS keeps its own data: backup of the settings, logs and histories.
sysdata.noVolume: No volume is mounted. Until then logs and histories stay in memory, and the settings are not backed up yet.
sysdata.title: System data
sysdata.unmounted: The volume “{volume}” is not mounted right now. Nothing is stored until it is back.
tailscale.acceptRoutes: Accept subnet routes from other Tailscale devices
tailscale.activateHint: Enable the plugin to configure Tailscale.
tailscale.approvalHint: Approve advertised subnets and this exit node in the Tailscale admin console. Your tailnet access rules determine who can connect.
tailscale.exitNone: Do not use or advertise an exit node
tailscale.exitProvide: Offer this NAS as an exit node
tailscale.firewallHint: Tailscale manages IPv4/IPv6 rules for the encrypted tunnel, UDP port 41641 and forwarding. Subnet routing uses source NAT. These rules stay ahead of the general firewall allow rule. Tailscale SSH and automatic program updates are disabled.
tailscale.httpsDisabled: At {name} TitanOS still shows its self-signed certificate. For a valid one (needed for passkeys and notifications on the iPhone) turn on "HTTPS Certificates" under DNS in the Tailscale admin console; TitanOS then gets it within five minutes. The name then appears in public certificate logs.
tailscale.httpsEnable: Turn on HTTPS in the tailnet
tailscale.httpsError: The certificate from Tailscale could not be fetched; next try in five minutes.
tailscale.httpsNeeds: Needed in the Tailscale admin console (login.tailscale.com, DNS section):
tailscale.httpsOffLink: At {name} TitanOS still shows its self-signed certificate. One click turns on HTTPS certificates for your tailnet at Tailscale; TitanOS then gets the valid certificate by itself (needed for passkeys and notifications on the iPhone). The name then appears in public certificate logs.
tailscale.httpsPublic: Note: the NAS's name in the tailnet (for example nas.your-tailnet.ts.net) then appears in the public Certificate Transparency logs. Anyone can read it there; the NAS is still reachable through it only from your tailnet.
tailscale.httpsReady: Web UI in the tailnet with a valid certificate:
tailscale.httpsWaiting: Waiting for the connection to Tailscale.
tailscale.httpsWhat: Then the browser shows no certificate warning when you open the NAS by its tailnet name, and passkeys and notifications on the iPhone work. TitanOS gets the certificate through Tailscale (Let's Encrypt) and renews it by itself. Access by IP address or the .local name keeps the NAS's own certificate.
tailscale.lanAccess: Direct local network access stays enabled.
tailscale.logout: Sign the NAS out of Tailscale
tailscale.logoutHint: The NAS will disconnect and require a new sign-in. Remote access through Tailscale will end.
tailscale.routesHint: One network prefix per line. Leave empty to expose only this NAS.
tailscale.trial: Check access and confirm by {time}. Without confirmation, the previous settings will be restored.
tasks.backupsFirst: Scheduled backups have priority (5-minute lead time)
tasks.capacityEstimate: Estimate from current array geometry; filesystem reserve and formatting affect the final value.
tasks.capacityWarning: 90% usage reached or projected within seven days at the measured growth rate.
tasks.noGrowth: No sustained growth in the observed period.
tasks.restorePreserves: Existing files and the snapshot are preserved. Snapshot identity is checked again at start.
tasks.sharedVolume: This data volume stores history and checkpoints for all maintenance tasks.
tasks.trendHint: Linear estimate from at least 24 hourly observations without major gaps. Capacity changes and stale readings invalidate predictions. Warnings appear here when loaded; no additional push messages are sent.
tasks.trendUnknown: No reliable projection: insufficient, interrupted or highly variable observations.
tasks.uploadHint: Browser upload: resuming requires the original files in the file manager.
tasks.wait.dependency: Waiting for a successful dependency in the current schedule
temperatures.alarmAtOwn: Notifies from {celsius} °C (5 °C below the chip's limit)
temperatures.alarmHint: Applies to the whole NAS. A notification comes only when two readings in a row are too hot. A chip with a limit of its own notifies 5 °C below it; otherwise the default for its kind applies (disks 60 °C, NVMe 85 °C, others 95 °C). Inputs of mainboard chips without a limit of their own never notify, because unused inputs read nonsense.
temperatures.alarmNever: Never notifies: chip without a limit of its own
temperatures.description: The temperature sensors the kernel reports, with their current values.
temperatures.heatHint: If one of these sensors stays at its limit for five minutes, TitanOS says so and shuts the NAS down in an orderly way (VMs and apps are stopped): {sensors}. Off by default.
temperatures.heatNone: No sensor of this NAS qualifies: only the processor, NVMe and graphics with a critical value of their own count, never the channels of the motherboard chip.
temperatures.none: The kernel currently reports no supported temperature sensors.
temperatures.sensorHint: Names come from the sensor driver. Unlabelled inputs are not assumed to be CPU or motherboard sensors. Drive temperatures are shown under Storage.
temperatures.title: Temperatures
ui.backupAccepted: Request for {name} accepted. Progress will update automatically.
ui.columns.hint: Drag or use the arrow keys to change the width; a double click resets it.
ui.neverConnected: No current system data received yet.
ui.searchHint: For example SSH, certificate, DNS or time zone
ui.sort.hint: Drag, or move with the arrow keys (Alt+arrow on the entry); the order applies to your account.
ui.stale: Displayed values may be out of date. Last updated {seconds} seconds ago.
ui.tasksHint: Uploads in this browser and file transfers, backups, system updates, VM jobs and volume checks reported by the NAS.
ui.tasksHintShort: Transfers, backups, updates, VMs and volumes
ui.tasksPartial: Some tasks could not be refreshed. Showing last known data.
ui.vmAccepted: Action for {name} accepted. The state will update automatically.
update.app.backDesc: Only the program of TitanOS with its web interface goes back. The NAS does not restart for it.
update.app.confirmSafe: The signature of the release and the checksum are verified. The new version first runs on trial; if it does not start, TitanOS goes back to the current one by itself.
update.app.confirmText: TitanOS loads {size} onto the stick and then restarts only its web interface, which takes about half a minute. Containers, VMs and shares keep running; the NAS does not restart. While copies, backups or disk tests are running the update is refused; with “Install updates by themselves” it waits until they are done.
update.app.restarted: TitanOS {version} is running. The NAS was not restarted for it.
update.app.restarting: The web interface is restarting … Containers, VMs and shares keep running.
update.app.rollbackText: TitanOS restarts its web interface, which takes about half a minute. Containers, VMs and shares keep running; the NAS does not restart.
update.app.text: Small updates replace only the TitanOS program with its web interface, not system image {version}. The NAS does not restart for them.
update.app.title: App updates
update.app.trial: The new version runs on trial. If it is not ready within a few minutes, TitanOS goes back to the previous one by itself.
update.auto.title: Install by itself
update.autoHint: When TitanOS finds an update, it installs it at the chosen time. A system update then restarts the NAS, stopping containers and VMs. An app update restarts only the web interface and waits until no copies, backups or disk tests are running.
update.autoNeedsChecks: Installing updates by itself needs automatic looking. Choose how often instead of “Manual only”.
update.back.desc: The previous system is still on the stick. The change applies from the next restart.
update.back.title: Back to TitanOS {version}
update.choose.autoOff: “Install updates by itself” is switched off, otherwise the next night would bring the newest version back. You can switch it on again in the settings below.
update.choose.failed: The list of versions could not be loaded. Without a connection to the project page there is nothing to choose.
update.choose.none: No version from {floor} on has been published yet.
update.choose.text: The 20 newest published versions from {floor} on are offered, older ones than the running version too. Even older versions do not know the new signing keys and are not offered.
update.choose.title: Choose a version
update.confirmSafe: The signature of the release and the checksum of every file are verified. The current version stays as the fallback.
update.confirmText: TitanOS loads {size} onto the stick, into the system that is not running. That takes a few minutes; the NAS keeps working meanwhile. The new version only becomes active with a restart that you trigger yourself.
update.downloading: Loading the new version onto the stick
update.failed: The update could not be installed. The running system is unchanged.
update.failedBefore: Version {version} did not start on this NAS before; the previous system came back by itself. It is therefore no longer installed automatically. You can try again by hand, and the next release is installed automatically again.
update.fallbackRemoved: There was no room on the stick for this update next to the previous version – the fallback version was removed.
update.fallbackRemovedFailed: Caution: there was no room on the stick for this update next to the previous version – the fallback version was removed. There is no older version left for the NAS to go back to. Please try the update again before the NAS restarts.
update.hero.released: Released on {date} · signature of the release verified
update.hero.title: TitanOS {version} is here
update.interval.hint: After an owner or administrator logs in, TitanOS also looks once in the background. If looking fails, TitanOS tries again within a day at the latest.
update.interval.manualHint: TitanOS does not look by itself, not even after a login. The button “Look now” looks at any time.
update.interval.range: Choose a spacing between 1 hour and 30 days.
update.kernel.confirm: The NAS then starts with kernel {kernel}. The running version stays as the fallback.
update.kernel.hint: The choice applies from the next system update on. For the running version, the switch appears above as an update of its own. If the NAS does not start with the other kernel, it goes back to the previous system by itself after three tries. Driver plugins are built for each kernel separately.
update.kernel.missing: Version {version} comes without the new kernel and is therefore not offered. Set the kernel below to “Stable” to install it.
update.kernel.newText: The newer kernel from trixie-backports, for very new hardware, for example network cards with RTL8127 or Intel E610 and the latest Intel and AMD graphics.
update.kernel.stableText: The kernel of Debian 13, well tested. Every driver plugin is available for it.
update.kernel.title: Kernel
update.manualHint: TitanOS tells you when it finds an update. It installs only when you say so.
update.news.title: What’s new in {version}
update.noKey: This image holds no key that updates could be verified with. Without a valid signature TitanOS installs nothing – for a development build that is the normal case. For a new version you write the stick anew.
update.pendingRollback: With the next restart TitanOS {version} starts again.
update.pendingUpdate: TitanOS {version} is on the stick and starts with the next restart.
update.rollbackEncrypted: {version} cannot open encrypted volumes. Unmounted there, with all shares, apps, VMs and containers on them: {volumes}. The data stays as it is and is back as soon as a system from 0.31.0 runs. If plugins live on an encrypted volume, {version} does not start cleanly and the stick returns to this version after three tries – choose another plugin volume or switch the plugins off first.
update.rollbackEncryptedUnknown: Whether there are encrypted volumes here could not be checked: {reason} {version} cannot open encrypted volumes; they would stay unmounted there, with everything on them. The data stays as it is and is back as soon as a system from 0.31.0 runs.
update.rollbackText: With the next restart the other system starts again. Your settings and data stay as they are.
update.rollbackWarn: An older version does not know settings that only the newer one introduced. They are not applied then.
update.singleChannel: All TitanOS updates use one stable channel. Individual new features are marked Beta in the interface.
update.slot.runningNotNext: running – the other one starts with the next restart
update.slots: The two systems on the stick
update.slotsText: The stick holds two systems. An update always goes into the one that is not running and starts three times on trial. If it does not come up, the NAS starts the former one again by itself.
update.steps.appFallback: If the new version does not start, TitanOS returns to the previous one by itself.
update.steps.appRuns: Containers, VMs and shares keep running, the NAS does not restart
update.steps.fallback: If the new system fails to start three times in a row, TitanOS {version} comes back by itself.
update.steps.label: Steps of the installation
update.steps.reachable: The NAS stays reachable until it restarts
update.steps.title: Installing TitanOS {version}
update.steps.waiting: TitanOS {version} is waiting for the restart
update.title: Updates
update.unconfirmed: This system is still on trial. In a few minutes it counts as confirmed; until then nothing else can be switched.
ups.intro: A UPS bridges a power failure with its battery. TitanOS reads its state through NUT (Network UPS Tools) and shuts the NAS down cleanly before the battery is empty – with VMs and containers stopped and volumes unmounted, so that no RAID has to sync again.
ups.modeHint.local: The UPS is attached to this NAS by USB or serial cable. Most USB devices work with the driver usbhid-ups.
ups.modeHint.network: Another device (a second NAS, a server) has the UPS on its cable and passes its state on through NUT. This NAS listens and shuts down when that one says so.
ups.modeHint.off: Without a UPS a power failure switches the NAS off hard.
ups.name: Name of the UPS there
ups.scan: Look for a UPS on USB
ups.serve: Tell other devices in the network the state of the UPS
ups.serveAfterSave: After saving, the login for the other devices shows here.
ups.serveHint: With these details you set up NUT on other devices that are powered by the same UPS. They shut down first, then this NAS.
ups.shuttingDown: The NAS is shutting down because of the power failure.
ups.title: UPS
ups.whenHint: Shutting down earlier spares the battery and leaves a reserve for a second time. If the power comes back before, everything keeps running.
ups.whenLow: When the UPS reports that the battery is almost empty
users.agentData.handedOver: Shared projects go to a member and are kept: {count}
users.agentData.loading: Checking what the AI agent keeps of this account …
users.agentData.mailAccounts: Mail mailboxes ({count}) with servers, passwords, signatures, rules and address book
users.agentData.nothing: The AI agent keeps nothing of this account.
users.agentData.part.calendar: Events and contacts of Calendar and Contacts (cannot be counted right now: the data volume is not mounted. Their folder stays there until a new account with this name first saves something; it never sees it.)
users.agentData.part.folder: The account's folder in the share “KI-Agent”
users.agentData.part.shared: Shared projects go to a member and are kept.
users.agentData.title: Deleted along with the account:
users.agentData.unavailable: The AI agent's volume is not mounted right now, so what goes along cannot be counted. What cannot be reached now is removed before a new account with this name is created.
users.apps.adminHint: Owners and administrators may use every app.
users.apps.mailHint: Off from the start, for owners and administrators too. Each mailbox is seen only by the account that sets it up.
users.apps.title: Apps
users.deleteText: The account, its settings and its access to all shares are removed. Files in the shares are kept.
users.lockText: {name} can no longer log in: web UI, API tokens, SSH and SMB are refused, all sessions and open consoles end at once. Files, shares and rights are kept; unlocking restores everything.
users.name: Name
users.ownerText: As an owner, {name} has full rights over the NAS, can manage all other accounts including owners, and can take away your rights.
users.passwordNote: The password is used for the web UI and for SMB shares. Other devices logged in with the old password are logged out.
users.passwordNoteShort: For the web interface and SMB
users.resetTwoFactorText: Two-factor login for {name} is turned off and the recovery codes stop working. All sessions of {name} end; after that the password alone signs in until 2FA is set up again.
users.smbPending: SMB only after the next sign-in to the web UI
users.title: Users
users.unlockText: {name} can log in again, with the same password, rights and shares.
viewer.bye.error: The remote view ended because of an error.
viewer.bye.forbidden: You may no longer use this app.
viewer.bye.idle: Disconnected because there was no input for a while.
viewer.bye.refused: The remote view could not be started.
viewer.bye.replaced: The app was opened in another window or browser.
viewer.clipboardEmpty: Nothing has been copied in the app yet.
viewer.clipboardSent: It is in the app's clipboard (paste it there with Ctrl + V).
viewer.codec.text: This browser does not play the remote view's video format ({codec}). Chrome, Edge, Safari and Firefox do; some Chromium builds on Linux do not.
viewer.dropHint: Drop here: the files are uploaded to the app.
viewer.ended.title: Remote view ended
viewer.err.app_forbidden: You may not use this app. An administrator allows it under Users › Programs.
viewer.err.viewer_agent: The remote view program on the NAS did not answer.
viewer.err.viewer_error: The remote view could not be started.
viewer.err.viewer_hostnet: The app uses the NAS's network directly.
viewer.err.viewer_image: The remote view program is not ready yet.
viewer.err.viewer_limit: You already have 4 remote views open. Close one to open this one.
viewer.err.viewer_memory: Not enough memory for another remote view.
viewer.err.viewer_name: The remote view does not work for this account or app (unusual name).
viewer.err.viewer_no_webui: The app has no web interface.
viewer.err.viewer_not_running: The app is not running. Start it under Docker, then reconnect.
viewer.err.viewer_unavailable: The remote view is not available on this NAS.
viewer.err.viewer_volume: The remote view has no volume (Control panel › Remote view › App profiles).
viewer.hostnet.text: This app uses the NAS's network directly (host network). The remote view only reaches apps in a Docker network of their own; open it in a tab of its own.
viewer.hostnet.title: App in the NAS's network
viewer.image.text: TitanOS downloads the remote view program once. The app opens by itself afterwards.
viewer.image.title: Setting up the remote view
viewer.insecure.text: The remote view needs a secure connection. Open TitanOS via https:// (e.g. with Let's Encrypt, Tailscale or the NAS's HTTPS name).
viewer.memory.text: There is not enough free memory for another remote view right now. Close another app window or open the app in a tab of its own.
viewer.memory.title: Not enough memory
viewer.noAudio: Sound does not work in this browser.
viewer.noDownloads: The app has not downloaded anything yet.
viewer.screen: Picture of {app}. Click to use the app.
viewer.settings.audioHint: You set the volume in the app's window.
viewer.settings.gpuHint: Rendering and encoding on the GPU; without a GPU the processor does the work.
viewer.settings.idleChange: You set the time with the consoles.
viewer.settings.imageMeanwhile: Until then the remote view goes on with the program it had.
viewer.settings.imageMissing: Not loaded yet – comes automatically with the first remote view.
viewer.settings.intro: TitanOS opens Docker apps in a browser of its own on the NAS and sends picture and sound to your window – through the TitanOS address, also via Cloudflare or VPN.
viewer.settings.noViews: No remote view is open right now.
viewer.settings.profilesHint: A browser profile of its own per account and app, so logins in the apps are kept (.titanos/viewer).
viewer.settings.qualityHint: Automatic adapts frame rate and bit rate to the connection.
viewer.settings.title: Remote view
viewer.settings.transportHint: Tiles send only what changes and redraw text losslessly after scrolling. When a large part of the picture moves for more than 5 seconds the view switches to video, and back after 3 calm seconds. Each app's window can change it.
viewer.settings.viewsNow: {open} open now, room for about {room} more (avg. {per} per view)
viewer.settings.viewsNowShort: {open} open now, room for about {room} more
viewer.transport.autoHint: Sharp text, almost no data when idle
viewer.transport.videoHint: As up to 0.67, steady data rate
viewer.unsupported.text: The remote view needs WebCodecs. Chrome, Edge, Opera and Brave from version 94, Safari from 16.4 (also iPhone and iPad) and Firefox from version 130 have it.
viewer.unsupported.title: This browser cannot show the remote view
viewer.uploadError.no_space: no room left (profile full or volume nearly full)
viewer.uploadHint: Pick uploaded files in the app's file dialog under “Uploaded”.
webapps.blocked: The app's program files do not arrive. If access goes through Cloudflare Access, the path /webapps/ needs a “Bypass” rule there: the app loads its files without your Cloudflare cookie. The files are public and hold nothing personal.
webapps.center.intro: These programs run right in your browser in a TitanOS window, without Docker and without load on the NAS. TitanOS checks them and brings new versions with its updates.
webapps.center.noVolume: Installing needs a volume: the programs are kept on the volume, not on the stick.
webapps.center.photocraftWhy: The web version from storytold lacks a file the app loads at start. Once a version starts, it can be installed here.
webapps.center.removeText: {app} disappears from the desktop of every account. Your files stay where they are. You can install the program again at any time.
webapps.center.title: Programs for the browser
webapps.conflictText: “{name}” changed since you opened it (by someone else or in another window). Overwriting replaces that version with yours.
webapps.dialog.name: File name
webapps.dialog.replaceHint: “{name}” already exists here. You will be asked whether to replace it.
webapps.migrate.item.kept: Kept (the browser program was not installed)
webapps.migrate.moreText: The programs are kept on your data volume (not on the stick) and run sealed off: they see neither your login nor any files other than the ones you open. Settings of the programs themselves (such as recently used fonts) are not remembered in that sealed-off window. Install or remove them at any time under App Center › Programs for the browser; Files › Settings › Default apps sets what a double click opens.
webapps.migrate.onNode: For the node “{name}” of the cluster.
webapps.migrate.title: Office programs right in the browser
webapps.migrate.whyText: From TitanOS 0.63 these programs run right in your browser, in a TitanOS window. That is faster than before, needs no container and no memory on the NAS, and works wherever you reach TitanOS – on the go and on your phone, too. You open documents with a double click in the file manager, and saving writes straight into the original file. The programs are checked by TitanOS and come with TitanOS updates.
webapps.migrate.whyTitle: Why T-Word, T-Exel and T-PDF are now installed this way
webapps.openFailed: The file could not be opened: {error}
webapps.replaceText: “{name}” already exists in this folder. Replacing overwrites it.
webapps.saveAsHint: {app} did not open Save As. Choose it in the app itself (File › Save As). TitanOS then asks for the folder and the name.
webapps.saveFailed: Not saved: {error}. Your changes are still in the app.
webapps.slow: The app does not answer. You can restart it or open it in a tab of its own.
webapps.standard.intro: Which program a double click in the file manager opens. Applies to your account only.
webapps.standard.none: No programs for the browser are installed. You can install them in the App Center.
webapps.standard.title: Default apps
webapps.successorNotReady: “{name}” is not ready yet. The current program stays; try again later.
webapps.unknownApp: This app is not installed on the NAS (any more).
webapps.unsavedRestart: {app} has changes that are not saved. Restarting loses them.
webapps.unsavedText: {app} has changes that are not saved. Closing loses them.
webapps.volume.hint: Your documents stay where they are. You can change the location later in the App Center.
webapps.volume.moveText: All installed programs move to the chosen volume. Your documents stay where they are. Until a program is ready in its new place, it keeps running from the old one.
webdav.accountIntro: Apps log in to WebDAV with your account name and a WebDAV password of its own. TitanOS makes it and shows it only once; your account password and second factor stay out of the apps.
webdav.createdHint: Enter these in the app. The password is only shown now; an earlier one no longer works.
webdav.intro: Shares over HTTPS as a network drive, for example in the Files app of the iPhone, in Finder or Windows Explorer – also from outside through the tailnet name. The same rights as for SMB apply; every account needs a WebDAV password of its own under "My account".
webdav.removeText: Apps using the WebDAV password can no longer log in.
webdav.title: WebDAV
welcome.bridgeText: So that VMs and apps can later get their own addresses on the home network, TitanOS connects the network port through a bridge (br0). If the network is not set up yet, this happens here automatically; the connection may drop briefly.
welcome.bridgeTitle: Home network for VMs and apps
welcome.checkFailed: Not everything could be checked, so some steps show no state.
welcome.doneText: The base system is ready. These steps make sense next. You can always find this list again under Settings › About TitanOS.
welcome.hostnameHint: The NAS shows up under this name in the network.
welcome.hostnameInvalid: Only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63 characters, no hyphen at the start or end.
welcome.intro: Your account is ready. Now pick the language, name and time zone – you can change all of it later in the settings.
welcome.localName: On the home network it is usually also reachable as {name}.
welcome.networkHint: A NAS should always be reachable at the same address. The easiest way is to reserve it for this NAS in your router; a fixed address can also be set in the network settings.
welcome.networkNow: The NAS is reachable at {address} right now. Your router hands out the address.
welcome.networkSettings: Open the network settings (fixed address, VLAN)
welcome.officeLater: More programs, and removing them, are in the App Center under “Programs for the browser”.
welcome.officeNoVolume: They are installed as soon as the first volume exists (they are kept on the volume, not on the stick).
welcome.officeText: T-Word, T-Exel and T-PDF open Word, Excel and PDF files right in the browser, in a TitanOS window: double-click in the file manager, saving writes the original file. They run on your device, not on the NAS, and come checked with TitanOS updates.
welcome.officeUnavailable: This NAS does not offer programs for the browser yet.
welcome.timezoneHint: The time zone of this browser is suggested.
welcome.title: Welcome to TitanOS
welcome.todoAppsText: Switch Docker on and install apps from the store.
welcome.todoBackupText: A backup job for the shares, to another volume, a second NAS, USB or the cloud.
welcome.todoDriversText: TitanOS found hardware with matching plugins (e.g. drivers). Have a look and install them if needed.
welcome.todoHardwareText: Report on processor, disks, network and drivers – without changing anything.
welcome.todoNotifyText: Learn by e-mail, ntfy, Telegram or Discord when a disk fails.
welcome.todoPushText: Add TitanOS to the home screen and turn on notifications.
welcome.todoRemoteText: Tailscale (plugin) or the built-in WireGuard server.
welcome.todoShareText: Folders reachable in the network over SMB or NFS.
welcome.todoStickText: The settings on the stick are backed up to a volume as soon as there is one.
welcome.todoTwoFactorText: Protects your account with a code from your phone as well.
welcome.todoVolumeText: Combine disks into a RAID. Without a volume nothing can be stored.
wg.accessAll: Everything: the internet traffic of the devices also goes through the NAS
wg.accessHome: NAS and home network (internet keeps going straight from the device)
wg.appInactive: Android app of {account}, out of the tunnel now (app ended, account locked or without administration rights)
wg.apps: "WireGuard" app for iPhone, Android, Windows, macOS and Linux: scan the QR code or import the configuration file.
wg.createdHint: In the WireGuard app choose "Add tunnel" › "Create from QR code" and scan the code.
wg.devMode: Development mode: settings are saved, but no tunnel is set up.
wg.dnsHint: For example the router, so names in the home network resolve. Empty keeps the device's DNS server.
wg.enableFirst: Turn on and save the server first.
wg.endpointHint: Name or address under which devices reach the NAS from outside, without port – ideally a name from dynamic DNS.
wg.endpointInvalid: Enter a name like nas.example.org or an IP address without port.
wg.intro: A VPN server of its own on the NAS: phones and laptops connect from anywhere with the WireGuard app and reach the NAS and the home network.
wg.onceOnly: The code holds the private key of the device and is only shown now. TitanOS does not keep it.
wg.removeText: {name} can no longer connect. Add the device again for new access.
wg.router: The router must forward UDP port {port} to the NAS (port forwarding). With the firewall on, this port is allowed from the internet by default (service "VPN tunnel").
wg.title: WireGuard
